jurisdictions.name: Alabama
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT 2026; balance sheet at end of 2025). The exemption for tax of $100 or less applies to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2023. Corporate income tax rate per ADOR 2025 summary.

fixedAnnual.name: Business Privilege Tax (Form CPT)
fixedAnnual.notes: Base is net worth apportioned to Alabama, not receipts. For a C corp, net worth = capital stock + additional paid-in capital (floored at 0) + retained earnings (floored at 0). An accumulated deficit does NOT reduce it, so a VC-backed company's base is roughly its total paid-in capital. That figure is multiplied by the Alabama apportionment factor (single sales factor with market-based sourcing since 2021, so roughly Alabama's share of sales). The rate depends on federal taxable income before NOLs apportioned to Alabama: under $1 (loss years) is $0.25 per $1,000 (0.025%). Higher brackets: $1.00 for $1 to $200k, $1.25 for $200k to $500k, $1.50 for $500k to $2.5M, and $1.75 per $1,000 at $2.5M or more. Maximum $15,000. No minimum since 2024: tax that computes to $100 or less is fully exempt and no return is required. Example: $20M paid-in capital x 1.5% Alabama sales factor = $300k Alabama net worth x 0.00025 = $75, so $0 is owed. You owe tax only when paid-in capital x Alabama factor exceeds $400k (e.g., more than about $27M raised at a 1.5% factor). Then the full computed amount is due, e.g., $50M raised gives about $188.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate annual report / Secretary of State fee
fixedAnnual.notes: The $10 corporate annual report fee that used to be paid with the BPT return was repealed by Act 2024-213, effective Oct 1, 2024 (secondary source: Alabama Retail Association; an older ADOR page still mentions the $10 fee). A one-time foreign qualification filing fee applies on registration; it is not annual and I did not verify the amount.

fixedAnnual.name: State store license (Title 40-12, Art. 7)
fixedAnnual.notes: The ADOR privilege license handbook says businesses selling software (treated as tangible personal property in Alabama) need a store license from the county probate judge/license commissioner: $1 state + $1 fee for one store (a county portion may be added). Negligible. Pure SaaS/services may need no state privilege license.

profitTaxes.name: Alabama corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 6.5% of Alabama-apportioned net income. Single sales factor with market-based sourcing. 100% deduction for apportioned federal income tax. 15-year NOL carryforward. Factor-presence nexus thresholds in the 2026 CPT instructions: $68,000 property, $68,000 payroll, or $675,000 sales in Alabama, or 25% of total property, payroll or sales.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No state-level gross receipts tax. In Alabama, the receipts-based costs come from city (and Jefferson County) business license taxes, generally about 0.1%-0.4% of receipts. For a business physically located in a city, the base is typically its Alabama receipts, with out-of-state sales deductible (Birmingham's administrator states this explicitly). Since Act 2025-408, every city and county files its license schedule with ADOR each March (revenue.alabama.gov/business-license-reports). The municipal license issuance fee cap is $14 for license years 2023-2027. SALES TAX (pass-through): ADOR Rule 810-6-1-.37 makes software licensing taxable 'regardless of form of transmission', but no ADOR rule or statute explicitly reaches remotely accessed SaaS. Secondary sources generally treat SaaS without download as non-taxable, so this is uncertain. Separately stated custom programming is not taxable. Remote sellers may use the 8% Simplified Sellers Use Tax program. PAYROLL (expense): state withholding plus local occupational taxes on gross wages, withheld by the employer. The Alabama League of Municipalities survey lists Birmingham 1%, Bessemer 1%, Auburn 1%, Opelika 1.5%, Gadsden 2%, Fairfield/Leeds/Midfield 1%, Tuskegee 2% and Macon County 1%, among others. Business personal property tax applies to office equipment (Class II, assessed at 20%); small.

calculatorOption.label: Alabama
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Alabama state receipts tax. The business privilege tax (0.025% of paid-in capital x Alabama sales share in loss years) is $0 when it computes to $100 or less, and the $10 annual report fee was repealed in 2024.

jurisdictions.name: Birmingham, AL
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year 2026 (Business License Code, Ord. 97-183 as amended, effective 1/1/2016; schedule filed with ADOR April 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Birmingham business license tax (Sch. 085 Data Processing Service / Sch. 007A general catch-all / Sch. 257 Internet Publishing)
receiptsTaxes.base: Prior-year gross receipts. Per the city's license administrator (Avenu), a business physically located in Birmingham reports ALL gross receipts from business conducted in Alabama and may deduct out-of-state sales. A service business not located in the city reports only receipts from Birmingham. Equity raises, loan proceeds and pass-through consumer taxes are excluded.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Every relevant schedule works out to 2/10 of 1% (0.2%). Sch. 085 Data Processing: 0.2% of gross receipts, minimum $100. Sch. 007A catch-all: $60 (<$5k), $100 ($5k-$10k), $150 ($10k-$15k), $200 ($15k-$20k), plus 0.2% of receipts over $20,000. Sch. 257 Internet publishing: 0.2%, minimum $200. The first-year license is based on the first 90 days of receipts, annualized. Due Jan 1, delinquent after Feb 15 (15% penalty plus another 15% Mar 16). There is no separate software schedule; which one applies to SaaS depends on the city's classification.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: Data Processing minimum is $100. The general catch-all is $60 below $5k receipts; Internet publishing minimum is $200. An issuance fee may apply (state cap $14); not confirmed for Birmingham.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Birmingham's 1% occupational tax applies to wages earned in the city (employer withholds; ALM survey and search results of city code). Treat it as payroll expense. Jefferson County's 0.025% business license applies in addition (listed separately). The city says it does not currently enforce a police jurisdiction. Non-located SaaS sellers with Birmingham customers may technically owe the license on Birmingham-sourced receipts, so the minimum would dominate.

calculatorOption.label: Birmingham
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.2% city business license on the Alabama receipts of a Birmingham-located business (out-of-state sales deductible), about $100 minimum. Default share equals Alabama's share of US population.

jurisdictions.name: Jefferson County, AL
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026 schedule filed with ADOR (Act 2011-662 / County Ord. 1801)

receiptsTaxes.name: Jefferson County Business License (JCBL, entity business license tax)
receiptsTaxes.base: Total gross receipts from business activity in Jefferson County (countywide, including inside Birmingham, Hoover and other cities). I could not read the exact sourcing language because the jccal.org site blocked fetching.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: 1/40 of 1% (0.025%) of gross receipts, minimum $25 license, maximum $15,000 license, plus a $25 issuance fee per location. Search snippets from the county site say receipts up to $100,000 pay the $50 minimum ($25 + $25 issuance). Applies to all for-profit entities with limited exceptions, in addition to city licenses.

fixedAnnual.name: JCBL minimum + issuance fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 minimum license + $25 issuance fee per location.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Jefferson County's former occupational tax is not listed on the ADOR schedule. Bessemer, Fairfield, Leeds and Midfield, all in the county, have 1% occupational taxes per the ALM survey (payroll expense).

calculatorOption.label: Jefferson County (Birmingham area)
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.025% county business license on in-county business receipts (capped at $15,000) plus $50 minimum and issuance fee; applies on top of Birmingham/Hoover city licenses.

jurisdictions.name: Montgomery, AL
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2025 schedule as amended by Ordinance 44-2024, filed with ADOR March 2026 (current for the 2026 license year)

receiptsTaxes.name: Montgomery business license tax (NAICS 518210, 519290, 541512, 541513, 541611, 541430 and similar)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the business licensed in the city (prior year). I could not confirm whether Montgomery limits this to Alabama receipts like Birmingham, because the city website blocked fetching. Assumed Alabama receipts.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Graduated schedule; each 'per 1,000' rate applies to receipts above the bracket floor:
- $0-25k: $120
- $25k-50k: $120 + $3.94/1,000
- $50k-100k: $204 + $2.89/1,000
- $100k-500k: $349 + $2.37/1,000
- $500k-1M: $1,294 + $2.15/1,000
- $1M-2M: $2,344 + $1.73/1,000
- over $2M: $3,919 + $1.43/1,000
A startup with $100k-$500k of Alabama receipts pays about $112 + 0.237%. Effective rates fall from about 0.3% at $150k to 0.16% at $5M of base. Plus a 'licensing fee' (issuance fee; amount not verified, state cap $14).

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $120 minimum for receipts up to $25,000, plus the issuance fee.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No Montgomery occupational tax appears in the ALM survey. The montgomeryal.gov license pages returned 403 to automated fetches, so everything here comes from the city's official schedule filed with ADOR.

calculatorOption.label: Montgomery
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Graduated city license of about $120 plus 0.237% of Alabama receipts (the $100k-$500k bracket rate; marginal rates fall to 0.143% above $2M).

jurisdictions.name: Huntsville, AL
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 License Fees by Schedule; the city links this same file as its '2026 License Fees by Schedule'

receiptsTaxes.name: Huntsville business license tax (Schedule 77 Service; alternatives Sch. 59 Miscellaneous, Sch. 56 Merchant-retail, Sch. 34 contractor/support offices)
receiptsTaxes.base: Prior-year gross receipts of the business conducted in the city (first year estimated). Sch. 59 and Sch. 34 instead use the GREATER of receipts or total annual gross operating cost of the in-city office.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Sch. 77 Service: $35 (<$5k), $65 ($5k-$10k), $95 ($10k-$25k), then $95 + $1.00 per $1,000 over $25,000 (0.1% marginal). Sch. 59 Miscellaneous: $35 + $1.00/1,000 over $10k, measured on receipts or in-city operating cost, whichever is greater. For a pre-profit startup with a Huntsville office this could be about 0.1% of local spending, e.g., ~$1,000 on $1M of local costs. Sch. 56 Merchant-retail (if software is treated as goods): $65 + $2.00/1,000 for $20k-$250k, then $525 + $1.00/1,000. Sch. 34 (government-contract liaison/support offices): $200 + $1/1,000 over $100k, declining to $0.50 above $1M. Renew by Jan 31; 15%/30% late penalties. The SaaS classification is the city's decision.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum (Sch. 77)
fixedAnnual.notes: $35 when receipts are under $5k. Above $25k the formula is equivalent to 0.1% x receipts + $70, which is the figure used here.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No Huntsville occupational tax. Madison County has no county receipts-based business license that I found (I did not check deeply). Ask the city which schedule applies: under Sch. 59/34, a pre-revenue office with high local costs pays on costs, not receipts.

calculatorOption.label: Huntsville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Service-schedule city license of $95 + 0.1% of receipts over $25k (the miscellaneous schedule may instead measure in-city operating cost if greater).

jurisdictions.name: Mobile, AL
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2025 schedule filed with ADOR March 2026 (license year 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Mobile business license tax
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of business conducted 'from, into or within' the city and its police jurisdiction. I could not read the ordinance's exact sourcing rules; assumed Alabama receipts for a Mobile-located business.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: The ADOR filing gives one rate per NAICS code: 541511 custom computer programming 0.2998%; 518210 data processing/hosting 0.283%; most other 5413-5419 professional services 0.29%; 541213 tax prep 0.325%. No code is listed for software publishers (511210/513210), so classification is uncertain. Minimum license $120 plus $10 issue fee and $8 zoning fee (city FAQ). Due Jan 1, delinquent after Jan 31; 15% penalty, then 30%, plus 1%/month interest.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum + issue + zoning fees
fixedAnnual.notes: $120 minimum + $10 issue fee + $8 zoning fee.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No Mobile occupational tax in the ALM survey. Mobile County License Commission issues state/county privilege licenses (flat, small).

calculatorOption.label: Mobile
calculatorOption.assumptionText: About 0.3% city business license on the Alabama receipts of a Mobile-located business (computer programming rate 0.2998%), with a $120 minimum plus $18 of fees.

jurisdictions.name: Tuscaloosa, AL
jurisdictions.taxYear: City Code Sec. 7-17 (as of Feb 2026), FY2025 schedule filed with ADOR March 2026

receiptsTaxes.name: Tuscaloosa business license tax (Payment Schedule B for 541512 systems consulting & design, 541990 other professional services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Prior-year gross receipts of the business (first year estimated and adjusted).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Schedule B is flat by bracket, then a per-$1,000 rate above $300k:
- under $15k: $75
- $15k-30k: $140
- $30k-60k: $200
- $60k-90k: $260
- $90k-180k: $400
- $180k-300k: $550
- over $300k: $550 + $2.00 per $1,000 over $300k (0.2% marginal)
Unclassified businesses (999000) use Schedule H: $75 + $4.00 per $1,000 over $10k (0.4%), so it matters which code the city assigns.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $75 minimum under Schedule B for receipts below $15k.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No Tuscaloosa occupational tax in the ALM survey.

calculatorOption.label: Tuscaloosa
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Professional-services city license: flat $75-$550 up to $300k of receipts, then 0.2% above that.

jurisdictions.name: Alaska
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (business license fee per AS 43.70.030 / 12 AAC 12.010 as compiled March 2026; biennial corporation tax per AS 10.06.845; corporate income tax brackets per AS 43.20.011(e), unchanged for 2025-2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Alaska state business license
fixedAnnual.notes: AS 43.70.030(a) / 12 AAC 12.010: $50 for an annual license, or $100 for a biennial (two-year) license, so $50/yr either way. Required for the privilege of engaging in business in the state; one license covers all of a firm's operations in Alaska. The $25 reduced fee applies only to sole proprietors aged 65+ or disabled veterans, so not to a corporation. Read directly in the official statutes/regulations PDF.

fixedAnnual.name: Biennial corporation tax / biennial report (foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: AS 10.06.845(a): a foreign corporation pays $200 every two years (domestic corporations pay $100), due before Jan 2 of the filing year. A $25 penalty applies per year or part-year of delinquency after Feb 1. The report is filed in odd or even years matching the year the certificate of authority was issued (AS 10.06.811). $200 / 2 = $100/yr. Read directly in the statute.

profitTaxes.name: Alaska corporate net income tax
profitTaxes.notes: AS 43.20.011(e) graduated brackets: 0% on taxable income under $25,000, then 2% through 9% bands, and $10,830 plus 9.4% on income over $222,000. No minimum tax. This is zero before profit, so it is informational only. Alaska conforms to the IRC and uses MTC/UDITPA apportionment. SB 113 (2025) would have adopted market-based sourcing and a single sales factor for 'highly digitized' remote businesses. The legislature passed it, Gov. Dunleavy vetoed it in Sept 2025, and the override failed 35-25 in Jan 2026. The veto and failed override come from news reports (ADN, Alaska's News Source) found in search results; I did not read them on an official site.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Alaska has no state sales/use tax (tax.alaska.gov) and no personal income tax. It has no state gross receipts tax that applies to software or professional services. A one-time $350 certificate of authority fee applies when a foreign corporation first registers. That figure comes only from secondary sources because commerce.alaska.gov fee pages returned HTTP 403, and it is not annual, so it is not counted. Local sales taxes exist in many boroughs and cities, for example Juneau 5%, Kenai Peninsula Borough 3%, Wasilla, Palmer, Kodiak, Sitka and Ketchikan. Anchorage and Fairbanks have none. Remote sellers collect these through the Alaska Remote Seller Sales Tax Commission (ARSSTC) once statewide gross sales delivered into Alaska reach $100,000 in the current or prior calendar year. There is no transaction-count threshold under the code amended July 2024, effective Jan 1, 2025. The ARSSTC uniform code treats electronically delivered digital goods and services as taxable unless the member jurisdiction exempts them, so SaaS can be taxable in member jurisdictions. Customers pay this tax and the seller passes it through, so it is not counted. Payroll: Alaska unemployment insurance has both employer and employee contributions; this is an expense the user already counts, and exact 2026 rates and wage base were not verified. Business personal property taxes exist in some municipalities (see Anchorage) but are measured by assets, not receipts.

calculatorOption.label: Alaska
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Alaska tax on receipts; $50/yr state business license plus $200 biennial foreign-corporation tax ($100/yr).

jurisdictions.name: Anchorage, AK
jurisdictions.otherNotes: The Municipality of Anchorage has no gross receipts tax, no general sales tax and no general business license. Municipal licenses are needed only for listed activities such as food service, contractors, taxis, pawnbrokers and marijuana businesses, and all of them require the state business license. The Treasury program taxes are limited to room, tobacco, rental vehicle, marijuana retail, motor fuel and alcohol retail taxes plus the E911 surcharge; none applies to SaaS or professional services. A proposed Anchorage sales tax was dropped by the mayor in January 2026 and was not on the April 2026 ballot (secondary source: ADN). Business personal property tax: the official Property Appraisal exemptions page states that the first $100,000 of assessed business personal property is exempt. Secondary reports say this took effect Jan 1, 2026, up from $20,000. A small startup with laptops and furniture will typically owe nothing. This tax is measured by assets, not receipts. There is no city payroll or head tax.

calculatorOption.label: Anchorage
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Anchorage has no gross receipts tax, sales tax, or general business license for software/services firms.

jurisdictions.name: Fairbanks, AK
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (City of Fairbanks Schedule of Fees, Resolution No. 5216, effective June 14, 2026; 2026 license based on 2025 gross receipts)

receiptsTaxes.name: City of Fairbanks business license (fee tiered by gross receipts)
receiptsTaxes.base: Prior-year gross receipts earned within Fairbanks city limits. The FAQ says a business outside the city must license if it delivers goods or provides services in the city, and online or remote sellers must register if they have sales to people or businesses in Fairbanks.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: gross receipts sourced to Fairbanks city limits (selects a flat fee tier; it is not a percentage tax)
receiptsTaxes.notes: FGC 14-602 tiers by prior-year in-city gross receipts: $0-$49,999 pays $50; $50k-$249,999 $120; $250k-$999,999 $350; $1M-$2,999,999 $580; $3M-$9,999,999 $1,125; $10M-$19,999,999 $2,200; $20M-$39,999,999 $3,350; $40M-$59,999,999 $4,500; $60M-$79,999,999 $5,900; $80M-$99,999,999 $11,500; $100M-$119,999,999 $16,000; $120M and above $25,000. The fee is flat within each tier, so its effective rate is at most about 0.1% at the bottom of a tier and far less in practice. It applies only to entities required to hold a state business license. Renewals are due the last business day of February, with a $50 late penalty on or after March 1 and a $50 civil penalty for not registering. Exemptions are listed in FGC 14-604; I could not read the code text because municode would not render. The City of Fairbanks has about 32k people, so in-city receipts for a national startup under $10M will be far below $49,999, which means $50/yr. That is modeled as a fixed amount with a zero rate.

fixedAnnual.name: City of Fairbanks business license (lowest tier)
fixedAnnual.notes: $50/yr when prior-year in-city gross receipts are $0-$49,999. This applies only if the company sells to customers in Fairbanks city limits.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Neither the City of Fairbanks nor the Fairbanks North Star Borough has a general sales tax; this comes from secondary sources. They levy alcohol, tobacco, marijuana and lodging taxes, none of which applies to SaaS. The borough levies property tax, and business personal property may be taxable; that is measured by assets and was not researched in detail. There is no payroll or head tax.

calculatorOption.label: Fairbanks
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $50/yr City of Fairbanks business license if you sell to Fairbanks customers; fee rises in tiers only above $50k of in-city receipts.

jurisdictions.name: Juneau, AK (City and Borough of Juneau)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Juneau has no gross receipts tax and no business license fee was found. Everyone making sales or rendering services in the City and Borough of Juneau (CBJ) must register with the CBJ sales tax office; the official page states no registration fee. CBJ levies a 5% sales tax on all goods, services and non-residential rentals, plus extra rates on alcohol, marijuana and short-term rentals. Digital goods sold to purchasers in Juneau are taxable. Remote sellers without physical nexus register and file through ARSSTC (statewide $100,000 threshold). This is a sales tax collected from customers and passed through, so it is not counted.

calculatorOption.label: Juneau
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Juneau has no receipts tax; its 5% sales tax (including on digital goods) is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Arizona
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 tax year for corporate income tax (Form 120); A.R.S. 10-122 annual report fee as currently in force; TPT rates per ADOR table effective Sept 1, 2026

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate income tax minimum (A.R.S. 43-1111)
fixedAnnual.notes: Tax is 4.9% of Arizona taxable income or $50, whichever is greater. The 2025 Form 120 instructions say every corporation required to file a return pays the $50 minimum. That includes loss years, and the instructions show worked examples of loss companies. For a unitary combined or consolidated group, the minimum is charged once per group.

fixedAnnual.name: Arizona Corporation Commission annual report
fixedAnnual.notes: A.R.S. 10-122 lists the annual report fee as $45 for domestic and foreign corporations. Late filing adds a penalty; a secondary source says $9/month. The ACC fee-schedule PDF could not be fetched (connection failures), so this figure comes from the statute. The one-time application for authority for a foreign (Delaware) corporation is $150 under the statute and is not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Arizona corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 4.9% for tax years after 2016. Zero before profit except the $50 minimum, which is counted in fixedAnnual. You can elect standard apportionment (double-weighted sales) or sales-factor-only. Service income is sourced to where the income-producing activity happens, unless the company qualifies and elects as a Multistate Service Provider (market sourcing, a 5-year election).

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
No gross receipts, franchise, or margin tax applies to a services or SaaS company's own receipts. Arizona's Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) is legally a vendor privilege tax measured by gross receipts, but it is normally itemized and passed to customers, so it is treated here as a pass-through sales tax. If your pricing is tax-inclusive or contracts don't let you add tax, it becomes a real cost of roughly the combined rate times Arizona SaaS receipts.

Professional services, including custom programming per Model City Tax Code (MCTC) regulations, are not a TPT classification and are not taxed. SaaS and hosted software are taxed under the personal property rental classification. Sources for this: ADOR ruling LR11-011 (2011), Director's Decision 201400197-S as cited in an ADOR presentation, and ADP v. ADOR (Ariz. Ct. App. 2023, per a Snell & Wilmer summary). Rental receipts from customers outside Arizona are deductible.

State TPT rate on rentals is 5.6% plus county excise. Combined rates per the ADOR Sept 1, 2026 table: 6.3% in Maricopa, 6.1% in Pima. City TPT is added on top; the city rental classification is broader than the state's because it also covers licensing for use.

TPT license: one-time $12 state fee per location with no state renewal fee. City license fees vary. A company with no physical presence in Arizona needs no city licenses, and ADOR's $100,000 remote-seller guidance is written for retail sales. Whether a SaaS seller with no physical presence has to license under the rental classification is unclear.

Payroll: Arizona has no local payroll or head taxes. State unemployment insurance, the job training tax, and income tax withholding are employer or employee payroll items and belong in expenses.

Business personal property tax has an indexed exemption that typical startup equipment holdings usually fall under. The 2026 threshold was not verified.

calculatorOption.label: Arizona
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $50 minimum corporate income tax plus $45 annual report; no receipts tax on services, and TPT on SaaS is assumed passed through to customers.

jurisdictions.name: Phoenix, AZ
jurisdictions.taxYear: Rates effective July 1, 2025 (unchanged in ADOR table effective Sept 1, 2026); license fees as of 2026

fixedAnnual.name: Phoenix TPT (privilege) city license renewal via ADOR
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 initial and $50 annual renewal. Owed only if the Phoenix location makes TPT-taxable sales, such as SaaS to Arizona customers. A pure professional-services business pays $0. Phoenix does not have or issue a general business license (City Clerk License Services).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Phoenix has no city income tax or tax on professional-services receipts. City TPT on SaaS (Rental, Leasing & Licensing for Use of TPP, code 214) is 2.8%, raised from 2.3% on July 1, 2025 by Ordinance G-7369. It is treated as a pass-through to customers, adding to the 6.3% state and county rate for a combined 9.1%. Phoenix also taxes the business of advertising at 0.5%, which matters only if the startup sells advertising. No head or payroll taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Phoenix
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Phoenix tax on services receipts and no general business license; a $50/yr TPT city license renewal is assumed (needed only if selling SaaS to Arizona customers), and the 2.8% city TPT on SaaS is passed through.

jurisdictions.name: Tucson, AZ
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (TPT rates per ADOR table effective Sept 1, 2026; business license fee per Tucson Code 19-39)

fixedAnnual.name: City of Tucson business license (collected by the city, not ADOR)
fixedAnnual.notes: ADOR's Tucson profile says Tucson requires a separate annual business license collected by the City of Tucson. Tucson Code 19-39 sets a $25 one-time application fee, a $50 annual fee (prorated in the first year), and a $50 renewal ($75 if late). This replaced an employee-count-based occupational license tax in 2008. The code text was read only through search-result excerpts (amlegal and elaws blocked or timed out), and the city's own pages confirm a license is required but give no amount.

fixedAnnual.name: Tucson TPT city license renewal via ADOR
fixedAnnual.notes: $20 license and $20 renewal. Owed only if TPT-licensed, e.g. selling SaaS to Arizona customers. It is unverified whether TPT licensees also owe the separate $50 city business license; both are counted here to be conservative.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Tucson has no tax on professional-services receipts and no income or payroll tax. City TPT on SaaS (rental of TPP, code 214) is 2.6%, treated as a pass-through, adding to the 6.1% Pima state and county rate for a combined 8.7%. Recent Tucson changes effective March 1, 2026 affect hotels, short-term rentals, and utilities only.

calculatorOption.label: Tucson
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $50/yr city business license plus a $20/yr TPT city license renewal if selling SaaS in Arizona; the 2.6% city TPT on SaaS is passed through.

jurisdictions.name: Mesa, AZ

fixedAnnual.name: Mesa General Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: Required since Jan 3, 2022 for most businesses with a physical presence in Mesa, including service businesses. $25 application and $25 annual renewal, with a $10 late fee. Exempt if there is no physical presence in Mesa.

fixedAnnual.name: Mesa TPT city license renewal via ADOR
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 initial and $20 annual renewal per ADOR's Mesa profile. Owed only if TPT-licensed (e.g. SaaS sales to Arizona customers).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Mesa has no tax on professional-services receipts and no income or payroll tax. City TPT on SaaS (code 214) is 2.0%, treated as a pass-through, adding to the 6.3% Maricopa state and county rate for a combined 8.3%.

calculatorOption.label: Mesa
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $25/yr general business license plus a $20/yr TPT city license renewal if selling SaaS in Arizona; the 2.0% city TPT on SaaS is passed through.

jurisdictions.name: Scottsdale, AZ
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (rates effective July 1, 2025)

fixedAnnual.name: Scottsdale Business Registration License (Service) or TPT city license (Merchant)
fixedAnnual.notes: Every business located in Scottsdale needs a Business Registration License. The Service version costs a $12 one-time application fee plus $50/yr, with a $25 penalty if filed after the start date. A TPT-licensed (Merchant) business instead attaches its ADOR TPT license showing region code SC, whose Scottsdale city fee is $50 license and $50 renewal. Either way it is about $50/yr.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Scottsdale has no tax on professional-services receipts and no income or payroll tax. City TPT on SaaS (code 214) is 1.70% since July 1, 2025 (down from 1.75%), treated as a pass-through, adding to the 6.3% Maricopa state and county rate for a combined 8.0%. Advertising is taxed at 1.70%, which matters only if selling ads.

calculatorOption.label: Scottsdale
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $50/yr city business registration (or TPT city license); the 1.7% city TPT on SaaS is passed through.

jurisdictions.name: Tempe, AZ
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (general business license fees begin Jan 1, 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Tempe General Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: Approved by council July 2025, effective Aug 1, 2025. $25/yr starting Jan 1, 2026; businesses that registered before Jan 1, 2026 pay nothing until Jan 1, 2027. It covers businesses with a permanent location in Tempe, including professional-services firms with no TPT license. The tempe.gov pages returned 403, so these details come from search-result excerpts of the city page and local news, which lowers confidence.

fixedAnnual.name: Tempe TPT city license renewal
fixedAnnual.notes: $70 initial and $50 annual renewal per ADOR's Tempe profile. Owed only if TPT-licensed (e.g. SaaS sales to Arizona customers).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Tempe has no tax on professional-services receipts and no income or payroll tax. City TPT on SaaS (code 214) is 1.8%, treated as a pass-through, adding to the 6.3% Maricopa state and county rate for a combined 8.1%. Tempe was added because it is a common Phoenix-area tech location; it has no special receipts tax on software or services.

calculatorOption.label: Tempe
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $25/yr general business license plus a $50/yr TPT city license renewal if selling SaaS in Arizona; the 1.8% city TPT on SaaS is passed through.

jurisdictions.name: Chandler, AZ

fixedAnnual.name: Chandler Business Registration
fixedAnnual.notes: Required for all businesses with a Chandler location, including service and internet-based businesses. $45 initial (prorated quarterly) and $45 each renewal year. No fee for nonprofits or businesses that already hold a specialty license.

fixedAnnual.name: Chandler TPT city license renewal
fixedAnnual.notes: $2 license and $2 renewal since Jan 1, 2018 per ADOR's Chandler profile. Owed only if TPT-licensed.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Chandler has no tax on professional-services receipts and no income or payroll tax. City TPT on SaaS (code 214) is 1.5%, treated as a pass-through, adding to the 6.3% Maricopa state and county rate for a combined 7.8%. Chandler was added as a common tech location; it has no special receipts tax.

calculatorOption.label: Chandler
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $45/yr business registration plus a $2/yr TPT city license if selling SaaS in Arizona; the 1.5% city TPT on SaaS is passed through.

jurisdictions.name: Arkansas
jurisdictions.taxYear: Franchise tax: 2026 report (for year ending 12/31/2025, due May 1, 2026). Income tax: tax years 2024-2026 (top rate falls to 4.1% from 1/1/2027).

fixedAnnual.name: Annual Corporation Franchise Tax (doubles as the annual report)
fixedAnnual.notes: Rate is 0.3% of issued and outstanding capital stock at par value, apportioned to Arkansas by (Arkansas real and personal property / total real and personal property per balance sheet). The minimum is $150. Due May 1; no extensions. Late filing adds a $25 penalty plus interest at 0.0274% per day. Paying online by card adds a $5 processing fee. A typical Delaware startup (e.g. 10M shares at $0.00001 par, so $100 of stated capital) pays the $150 minimum. TRAP: on this form, no-par stock is valued at $25 per share. A no-par Delaware corp with 10M shares would have a $250M base before apportionment, so with meaningful Arkansas assets the tax could far exceed $150. SB256 (2025), which would have cut the minimum to $100, died in committee on 5/5/2025, so $150 still applies.

profitTaxes.name: Arkansas corporation income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Graduated for tax years 2024 and later: 1% on the first $3,000, 2% on the next $3,000, 3% on the next $5,000, 4.3% over $11,000. The 2026 special session (signed May 6, 2026) cuts the top rate to 4.1% from Jan 1, 2027. Apportionment uses a single sales factor. Act 719 of 2025 adds market-based sourcing for services and intangibles (receipts sourced where delivered to the customer) and a $250,000 Arkansas gross-receipts economic-nexus threshold for nonresident corporations without physical presence. Both apply to tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2026. No minimum income tax, so $0 before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Arkansas calls its sales tax the 'gross receipts tax' (6.5% state plus local), but it is collected from customers and is pass-through, not a tax on the seller's revenue. Under 26 CAR § 30-1008, electronically delivered software is not taxable, nor is software programming or custom software development. Remotely accessed SaaS is generally treated as non-taxable (that SaaS conclusion comes from secondary sources plus the electronic-delivery rule; the rule text does not name SaaS). Most professional and consulting services are not on the taxable-services list. Getting a Certificate of Authority as a foreign corporation costs $300 once (paper; $270 online per secondary sources); it does not recur. You also need an Arkansas registered agent, a commercial cost rather than a tax. Payroll costs belong in expenses, not here: state income tax withholding and state unemployment insurance (taxable wage base reported as $7,000 per employee for 2026 by secondary sources; rates vary). Business personal property such as laptops and furniture located in Arkansas is subject to county ad valorem property tax (not researched in detail). Local business taxes: A.C.A. § 26-77-102 lets cities levy business license (privilege) taxes only on businesses situated in the city. The amount may be based on inventory or the kind of business, and 'no classification shall be based upon earnings or income', so Arkansas cities cannot levy gross receipts taxes. A business generally pays in only one city unless it has places of business in more than one. North Little Rock requires a business/privilege license for all businesses operating in city limits. It publishes no fee schedule (fees are quoted on request); renewals are due Jan 31, with a 25% penalty after Apr 1 and 50% after Jul 1.

calculatorOption.label: Arkansas
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Arkansas tax on revenue; $150 minimum annual franchise tax (0.3% of apportioned par-value stock, which is below $150 for typical low-par startup stock).

jurisdictions.name: Little Rock, AR
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (fees due Jan 1, 2026). An ordinance on the Dec 16, 2025 Board agenda raises base fees 3% from Jan 1, 2027.

fixedAnnual.name: City business license (privilege tax), Code § 17-52, class (82) Data Processing Service
fixedAnnual.notes: Class (82) covers 'sales of automatic data processing services including software development (systems analysis and programming), machine processing of client data, and consultant services'. The base fee is $470, plus $55 for each additional client-contact, marketing or systems-analyst employee, $40 for each additional programmer and $20 for each additional machine operator. The city decides the classification, and other classes could apply. (70.1)(b) non-game design and development: $200 base plus $50 per programmer and $30 per technician. (82.1) home-based or part-time data processing: $270. (187) Professionals, including consultants and engineers: $155 per professional and $50 per paraprofessional. The license is due Jan 1. Penalties are 10% after Feb 1, another 10% after Mar 1 and 30% after Apr 1, and it is not prorated. It applies only if the company operates in Little Rock (an office, or a home-based business location). A remote seller with Little Rock customers and no location there owes nothing. The 2027 ordinance would raise the class (82) base to $484; per-employee amounts stay the same. I did not confirm from official minutes that the ordinance passed.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Little Rock has no local income tax or gross receipts tax on services; Arkansas law (A.C.A. § 26-77-102) bars city license taxes based on earnings or income. City sales tax (state 6.5% + Pulaski County 1% + Little Rock 1.5%, about 9% per a city guide whose date I could not confirm) is collected from customers, and SaaS and electronically delivered software are not taxable in Arkansas. The per-employee license add-ons ($40-$55 per programmer or sales employee) behave like a small head tax, so model them in expenses if you prefer. Example: 3 programmers and 2 sales staff in class (82) come to about $470 + 3*$40 + 2*$55 = $700 per year (assuming 'additional' adds each listed employee to the base). Business personal property in Pulaski County is assessed for county property tax; that is separate from the license.

calculatorOption.label: Little Rock
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax in Little Rock; $470 base business license (data-processing class, 2026) if you operate there, plus about $40-55 per programmer or sales employee; base rises to $484 in 2027.

jurisdictions.name: Fort Smith, AR
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (fee change approved by the Board in November 2025)

fixedAnnual.name: City business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Per secondary sources and search snippets of the city site: the first year is free for new Fort Smith businesses, annual renewal is $100, and a home-occupation license has a $150 application fee. In November 2025 the Board added a $500 fee for first-time registrants and renewals without a physical brick-and-mortar presence in Fort Smith, according to Talk Business & Politics; the ordinance number and effective date were not found. That fee targets out-of-town businesses working in the city, such as contractors. Whether it reaches a remote SaaS seller is doubtful given A.C.A. § 26-77-102 ('situated' in the city; one city only unless there are multiple places of business). I could not read the official fortsmithar.gov pages (HTTP 403).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Fort Smith has no receipts or income-based local tax; state law forbids license classifications based on earnings or income. Its sales tax is collected from customers, and SaaS is not taxable in Arkansas.

calculatorOption.label: Fort Smith
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax in Fort Smith; about $100 per year business license renewal if located there (first year free), with $500 reported for businesses without a local location.

jurisdictions.name: Fayetteville, AR
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year ending Oct 31, 2026

fixedAnnual.name: City business license
fixedAnnual.notes: New license: $98 for non-home-based (commercial), $31 for home-based. Annual renewal is $10 for both. Licenses expire Oct 31, and late renewal adds $30.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Fayetteville has no receipts or income-based local tax. I checked it as the largest Northwest Arkansas tech hub; the fee is nominal.

calculatorOption.label: Fayetteville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax in Fayetteville; only a nominal $10 per year business license renewal ($98 first year for a commercial location).

jurisdictions.name: California
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 FTB rates and doing-business thresholds (2026 thresholds not yet published); 2026 Secretary of State fees

fixedAnnual.name: Corporation franchise tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: Every corporation that is incorporated in, registered in, or doing business in California owes $800 a year. That includes a Delaware corporation that never qualifies with the Secretary of State. A company is doing business in CA if it engages in any transaction for financial gain in CA, or if its CA sales, property or payroll exceed the 2025 thresholds: sales over $757,070, property or payroll over $75,707, or 25% of the company total for any of the three. Having CA employees will almost always trigger this. Newly incorporated or newly qualified corporations do not owe the minimum in their first taxable year. Before profit, the $800 is the whole state corporate tax. It is paid as the first estimated payment.

fixedAnnual.name: Statement of Information (Form SI-550), domestic and foreign stock corporations
fixedAnnual.notes: $25, due within 90 days of registering and every year after that. Missing it brings a $250 SOS penalty, which the FTB collects. Qualifying a foreign corporation (Statement and Designation by Foreign Corporation) is a one-time $100 and is not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Corporation franchise tax (C corporations other than banks/financials)
profitTaxes.notes: Applies to net income apportioned to California. Zero before profit, when the $800 minimum applies instead.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate alternative minimum tax
profitTaxes.notes: Per the FTB rate table. Only relevant once there is income.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: California has no state gross receipts or margin tax. Sales/use tax: under CDTFA Regulation 1502, prewritten software transferred by remote telecommunications (no tangible media) is not taxable, and neither is remote time-sharing access to a computer. SaaS and custom programs are generally not subject to sales tax, so there is nothing to collect for pure SaaS. Payroll costs belong in expenses and are not quantified here: state UI and ETT on the employer, and SDI withheld from employees. Local business taxes vary widely by city (see the city entries). Some Peninsula cities, for example Mountain View and Palo Alto, levy per-employee business taxes. I could not reach those city sites, so they are not verified here.

calculatorOption.label: California
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $800 minimum franchise tax (waived in the first taxable year) plus a $25 annual Statement of Information; California has no state gross receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: San Francisco, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years 2025 and 2026 (Prop M rates); 2026-27 Business Registration fees (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027)

receiptsTaxes.name: Gross Receipts Tax, Business Activity Category 5 (NAICS 51 Information, 54 Professional/Scientific/Technical, and 'all other')
receiptsTaxes.base: San Francisco gross receipts. For Category 5 this is 75% of receipts allocated to SF (services where the customer receives the benefit, intangibles where they are used) plus 25% of total receipts multiplied by SF payroll divided by total payroll. Related entities are combined.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Combined taxable SF gross receipts after allocation and apportionment. The $5M figure is stated for 2025.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rates for 2025 and 2026 are marginal brackets: 1.000% for $0-$1M, 1.000% for $1M-$2.5M, 1.500% for $2.5M-$25M, 1.176% for $25M-$50M, 1.344% for $50M-$150M, 1.512% for $150M-$250M, and 1.680% above $250M. For 2027 the first brackets rise to 1.040%, 1.040% and 1.560%. A business at or below $5M of SF gross receipts does not file or pay. Once over $5M, the brackets apply from the first dollar; the Treasurer's own restaurant example confirms there is no $5M deduction. That makes the effective rate 1.25% at $5M and about 1.375% at $10M; rateForSaaS uses 1.25%. The separate Homelessness Gross Receipts Tax applies only above $25M of SF receipts. The Overpaid Executive Tax exempts businesses with 1,000 or fewer US employees and $1B or less in gross receipts. Estimated payments are due April 30, July 31 and October 31, and the annual return is due the last day of February. For an SF-headquartered team, SF receipts are roughly 25% of total revenue, so this tax generally starts only above about $20M of total revenue.

fixedAnnual.name: Business Registration Fee (2026-27) plus state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $55 for $0-$100k of 2025 SF gross receipts, plus the $4 state fee. The fee rises in tiers: $95 to $250k, $160 to $500k, $320 to $750k, $440 to $1M, $625 to $1.5M, $875 to $2M, $1,130 to $2.5M, and $1,885 for $2.5M-$5M. Above $5M it drops to $800, because the gross receipts tax then applies. Under the 'First Year Free' program, the initial registration fee is waived for a new business or location with $5M or less in SF gross receipts that has a commercial (non-home) location.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no city income tax, and the SF payroll expense tax was fully repealed (Prop F, 2020). The Administrative Office Tax applies only to qualifying large administrative-office businesses and does not affect a typical startup. The Commercial Rents Tax falls on landlords (small-business exemption $2,325,000) and may be passed through in leases. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. Prop M (approved November 2024) reduced the categories to 7 and moved apportionment to 75% receipts / 25% payroll. I could not read the code text (amlegal blocked automated access), so all figures come from the Treasurer & Tax Collector's official pages.

calculatorOption.label: San Francisco
calculatorOption.assumptionText: About 1.25% of SF-apportioned receipts (1.0% up to $2.5M, 1.5% from $2.5M to $25M), owed only once SF receipts exceed $5M; for an SF-based team SF receipts are about 25% of total revenue plus 75% of SF customer sales; $59 registration fee.

jurisdictions.name: Los Angeles, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 business tax (measured on calendar-2025 gross receipts); rate table rev. 08/2025

receiptsTaxes.name: City of Los Angeles Business Tax, class L049 (Internet-Based Application Service Providers, Internet-Based Data Manipulation, Professions & Occupations)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts attributable to business in LA. Under City Clerk's Ruling No. 15 this is receipts from work performed in LA, plus (if the business has LA premises) a share of receipts from work performed outside LA, deemed to be 20% when there is no better information. Receipts can be apportioned out only when documented as attributable to employees or equipment outside LA. Customer location does not matter.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Worldwide (in-city plus out-of-city) total gross receipts. Applies only to registered businesses that file the renewal on time.
receiptsTaxes.notes: $4.25 per $1,000 or fraction thereof (0.425%). The old reduced $1.01 rate for internet application service providers expired after 2018; those businesses now sit in L049. 'Multimedia' businesses pay $1.01 per $1,000 (0.101%); this covers custom programming or software design for clients and website/online-service development for clients, so a services-heavy firm may qualify for part of its receipts. If one class makes up 80% or more of receipts, all receipts can be reported at that class's rate. Tax for year N is based on year N-1 receipts and is due by the last day of February (March 2, 2026). If the renewal is late, the $100k small-business exemption is lost.

fixedAnnual.name: Business Tax Registration Certificate renewal and state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: No flat annual fee when the business is exempt. A $4 state disability-access fee is added only when tax is due. There is no minimum tax for class L049.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Los Angeles has no city income tax and no payroll tax. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. Because LA taxes where the work is performed, an LA-based team owes on close to 100% of its worldwide receipts once it is over $100k. Distributed teams can apportion out receipts from work documented as done outside LA, but 20% of that work's receipts stays taxable by default.

calculatorOption.label: Los Angeles
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.425% of receipts from work performed in LA (about all receipts for an LA-based team); nothing owed if worldwide receipts are $100k or less and the renewal is filed on time.

jurisdictions.name: San Diego, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current City Treasurer schedule (2025-26)

fixedAnnual.name: Business Tax Certificate plus state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $34 a year for 12 or fewer employees, plus the $4 state fee. With 13 or more employees it is $125 plus $5 per employee, plus $4.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: San Diego has no gross receipts tax. Since July 1, 2025 there is a Minimum Wage Enforcement Fee of $1.47 per employee working in the city each year; this is headcount-based and belongs in expenses. Businesses inside a Business Improvement District may owe BID assessments. Late fee: $25 or 10%, plus 1% per month. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax.

calculatorOption.label: San Diego
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $34 business tax certificate (12 or fewer employees) plus $4 state fee; no receipts-based tax.

jurisdictions.name: San Jose, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: Rates effective July 1, 2026 (FY 2026-27)

fixedAnnual.name: Business tax (employee-count based) plus state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: Base tax of $222.89 covers 1-2 employees. Each additional employee costs $37.98 (employees 3-35), $50.62 (36-100), $63.28 (101-500) or $75.99 (501+), with a cap of $190,128.24. A $4 state fee is added. The $530.73 figure assumes 10 employees: $222.89 + 8 x $37.98 + $4. 'Employee' includes owners and managers. Rates are CPI-indexed each July, limited to 1.5% on the base and 3% on the increments. FY 2025-26 rates were $219.60 base and $37.06 per employee.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: San Jose has no gross receipts tax; the business tax scales with headcount. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. Out-of-town businesses working in San Jose pay a prorated schedule based on days present.

calculatorOption.label: San Jose
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Employee-based business tax: $222.89 base plus $37.98 per employee beyond 2 (10 employees assumed), plus $4 state fee; no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Oakland, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Measure T progressive rates in effect since January 1, 2023; OMC ch. 5.04 has no CPI indexing)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business Tax, Class F (Professional and Semi-Professional Services), which by definition includes software as a service, platform as a service, infrastructure as a service and website development
receiptsTaxes.base: Total gross receipts for the preceding calendar year (OMC 5.04.110 and 5.04.250). The definition is not limited to Oakland-sourced receipts. A reduction ('constitutional apportionment', OMC 5.04.270) is available only by written application to the City Administrator within one year.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Brackets: $60 flat up to $16,666. Then $60 + $3.60 per $1,000 above $16,666, up to $1M. Then $3,600 + $4.25 per $1,000 above $1M, up to $2.5M. Then $9,975 + $4.75 per $1,000 above $2.5M, up to $20M. Above $20M, $93,100 + $5.00 per $1,000. Effective rates are about 0.36% at $1M, 0.40% at $2.5M, 0.44% at $5M and 0.46% at $10M; rateForSaaS uses the first bracket. Measure T eliminated the small-business exemption. A newly established business pays its first tax on an estimate of first-period receipts. The return is due March 1.

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum business tax (Class F) plus state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $60 minimum (receipts of $16,666 or less) plus the $4 state fee. The city also charges a recordation and technology fee, about $4.50 according to a secondary source; I did not confirm the amount or whether it recurs. The one-time new-business registration fee is set by the Master Fee Schedule (about $90.50 according to a secondary source).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Oakland has no city income tax or payroll tax for this profile. Class K (Administrative Headquarters, taxed on gross payroll) applies only to non-revenue-producing HQ locations of a business that also has revenue-producing locations elsewhere. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. The model adds the $64 fixed amount on top of 0.36% of all receipts, which overstates the tax by about $60 a year.

calculatorOption.label: Oakland
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.36% of total gross receipts for an Oakland-based business (rising to 0.425% above $1M and 0.475% above $2.5M), plus $60 minimum tax and $4 state fee; no small-business exemption.

jurisdictions.name: Santa Monica, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY 2026-27 (Measure F changes effective January 1, 2025)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business License Tax, Group III Services (SMMC 6.08.150 lists AI, consultants, computer programmers, data processing, software/network/web development, and IT and cloud services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts attributable to business conducted in Santa Monica
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Worldwide gross receipts. Under $103,000 the business can claim exemption from the license tax, but must apply or renew by August 31 and still pays the fees.
receiptsTaxes.notes: $75 covers the first $60,000, then $3.00 per $1,000 (0.30%) above $60,000, with receipts rounded up to the nearest $1,000. Group IV Professions, which covers the enumerated licensed professions (accountants, attorneys, engineers, architects, physicians and similar), pays $5.00 per $1,000 (0.50%). Corporate or administrative headquarters are taxed on cost of operations at $2.25 per $1,000 for FY 2026-27. New-application penalties are capped at 50%.

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum license tax, CASp state fee, business license processing fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $75 minimum tax, which is waived if the business qualifies for the under-$103k exemption, plus the $4 state CASp fee and the $44.85 processing fee shown for 2026-27 new applicants. Measure F reinstated the processing fee per application; I did not confirm whether renewals pay it. A one-time zoning conformance review fee applies to in-city locations ($125.75 commercial). Business Improvement District assessments may apply.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Santa Monica has no payroll tax. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. I could not confirm the exact sourcing rules for 'attributable to business conducted in Santa Monica' (the municipal code apportionment text was not reviewed), so the 100% default share for a Santa Monica-based firm is a conservative assumption.

calculatorOption.label: Santa Monica
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.30% of Santa Monica receipts above $60k for software, IT and AI services ($75 minimum); exempt if worldwide receipts are under $103k; about $49 in state and processing fees.

jurisdictions.name: Culver City, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Culver City Municipal Code as codified through Supplement S-25, 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business License Tax: 'Computer software development' is GRT-F; 'Computer software consulting' and 'Professional services' are GRT-G
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts for the preceding 12 months. Receipts used as the measure of business tax paid to another jurisdiction are excluded. If gross receipts are less than the business's cost of operations, the cost of operations is taxed instead (CCMC 11.01.220). Cost of operations is defined as all expenses, including personnel, equipment, rent, utilities and depreciation.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: The first $200,000 of annual gross receipts is excluded. This is a deduction, not a cliff.
receiptsTaxes.notes: GRT-F is $3.00 per $1,000 (0.30%) and GRT-G is $3.50 per $1,000 (0.35%). An extra 0.01% applies to reported gross receipts over $100M. The cost-of-operations floor matters most for this calculator: a pre-profit Culver City company is effectively taxed at about 0.30-0.35% of its total spending. Example: a $3M annual burn gives about $8,400 at GRT-F if the $200k exclusion also applies to the cost-of-operations base. I could not confirm whether the exclusion applies to that base. The revenue-based model will understate this; ideally model it as rate x max(revenue, operating expenses).

fixedAnnual.name: Application and renewal fees plus state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: The application fee and annual renewal fee are set by City Council resolution. I could not read the amounts because the culvercity.gov pages were inaccessible from this session. Only the $4 state fee is counted here.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Culver City has no payroll tax. SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. Because of the cost-of-operations rule, Culver City is the one California city reviewed whose business tax clearly costs a pre-revenue company money in proportion to its spending.

calculatorOption.label: Culver City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.30% (software development) on the greater of gross receipts or total operating costs, after a $200k exclusion, so pre-profit firms pay about 0.3% of their spend.

jurisdictions.name: Berkeley, CA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (current City of Berkeley rate table)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business License Tax, Professional/Semiprofessional (code P, BMC 9.04.165)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts. I did not review Berkeley's apportionment and sourcing rules.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: $3.60 per $1,000 (0.36%), minimum $51. Other classes: Business, Personal & Repair Services (code B) $1.80 per $1,000 (0.18%); Miscellaneous (code D) $2.40 per $1,000; Administrative Headquarters (code Q) $1.20 per $1,000 of gross payroll. The rate table does not say which class covers SaaS, so the higher professional rate is used to be conservative; actual classification could be B or D.

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum business license tax plus state SB 1186 fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $51 minimum plus the $4 state fee. Any application fees were not verified.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: SaaS is not subject to California sales tax. Classification and apportionment are uncertain, so confirm with Berkeley Finance.

calculatorOption.label: Berkeley
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.36% of gross receipts (professional class; SaaS may instead be 0.18% business-services class) with $51 minimum plus $4 state fee.

jurisdictions.name: Colorado
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2025 corporate rate (also the rate on the 2026 estimated-tax worksheet); Secretary of State fees current as of Oct 2026

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State Periodic Report (annual report)
fixedAnnual.notes: $25, filed online once a year. Domestic and foreign entities pay the same. The fee went from $10 to $25 on July 1, 2024. Late filing adds a $50 penalty. A delinquent entity pays $100 to file a Statement Curing Delinquency. The Foreign Entity Authority Statement that registers a Delaware corporation to do business in Colorado is a one-time $100, not annual. Colorado has no franchise tax and no minimum corporate tax.

profitTaxes.name: Colorado corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 4.4% of Colorado net income: line 19 of the 2025 DR 0112, and the 2026 DR 0112EP worksheet also says 4.4%. Tax year 2024 was temporarily 4.25% (2024 DR 0112), a TABOR-surplus-triggered cut, so a similar temporary cut in a later year is possible. Income is apportioned by a single receipts factor (C.R.S. 39-22-303.6). From recall rather than the pages read: services and SaaS receipts are sourced to where the customer receives the benefit. There is no minimum tax: a company with zero taxable income owes $0. Returns are due the 15th day of the 5th month (May 15 for calendar-year filers).

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Colorado has no gross receipts tax, no franchise or capital tax, and no minimum tax, so before profit the state costs only the $25 periodic report.

Payroll (already counted in expenses):
- State unemployment insurance and income tax withholding.
- FAMLI paid-leave premium: 0.88% of wages in 2026 (was 0.9% in 2025), split 0.44% employer and 0.44% employee. Employers with 9 or fewer employees remit only the 0.44% employee share.
- Local head taxes (occupational privilege tax, OPT) in Denver ($4 employer + $5.75 employee per month), Glendale ($5 + $5, earnings over $750/month), Greenwood Village ($2 + $2, earnings of $250+/month) and Sheridan ($3 + $3). Aurora repealed its OPT effective Jan 1, 2025.

Sales tax (passed through to customers):
- At the state level, software provided through an application service provider (SaaS) is currently exempt (CDOR Computer Software guidance).
- HB26-1223, signed June 4, 2026, ends the state exemption for downloaded prewritten software from Jan 1, 2027. The bill summary covers downloaded software only; whether hosted SaaS also becomes state-taxable is unclear and awaits CDOR guidance.
- Many home-rule cities set their own sales tax rules and already tax SaaS: Denver at 5.15%, Boulder at 3.86% and Colorado Springs at 3.07% (each confirmed on the city's own site). Each needs its own registration or license.

Business personal property tax: owed only if the depreciated actual value of business equipment in a county is over $56,000 (tax years 2025-2026). A typical laptop-and-furniture startup is under that and owes $0; software is exempt.

calculatorOption.label: Colorado
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Colorado gross receipts or franchise tax; $25 annual periodic report; 4.4% corporate income tax only once profitable.

jurisdictions.name: Denver, CO
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (OPT guide published April 2026; sales tax guide revised 03/2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Retail sales tax license or retailer's use tax license (needed only if selling SaaS to Denver customers)
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 per location for each two-year period, renewed on January 1 of even-numbered years (prorated for mid-cycle starts), so about $25 a year. Required because Denver taxes SaaS. A company located outside Denver that sells into Denver needs the $50-per-two-years retailer's use tax license instead. A pure professional-services company with no taxable sales does not need it. Software and professional-services firms are not on Denver's business license directory, so no general business license applies.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Denver has no gross receipts or income tax on businesses.

Occupational privilege tax (OPT, a head tax; Tax Guide Topic 61, Apr 2026), which belongs in payroll expenses:
- Employee OPT: $5.75 per month, withheld from each employee who earns at least $500 in a calendar month for work performed in Denver.
- Business OPT: $4.00 per month for each such employee, plus $4.00 per month for each owner, partner or manager.
- Any entity with business activity in Denver owes at least $4 per month ($48 a year).
- A corporation has only employees, not working owners, so for a C corporation this is effectively $48 per Denver employee per year from the employer, plus $69 per year withheld from the employee.
- Businesses with fewer than 60 employees may file quarterly.

Sales tax: Denver taxes software as a service at the 5.15% city rate for 2026, wherever the software is hosted, as long as it is used in Denver. This is collected from customers.

calculatorOption.label: Denver
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Denver receipts tax; ~$25/yr sales tax license because Denver taxes SaaS; OPT head tax ($4/employee/month employer share) belongs in payroll expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Colorado Springs, CO
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Colorado Springs has no gross receipts tax and no general business license. Its official tax pages mention no occupational privilege (head) tax. The city sales tax license is required only for businesses selling at retail, and since Sept 1, 2023 it has no license or renewal fee. A temporary license costs $20.

Sales tax: Colorado Springs taxes SaaS and online software subscriptions (Tax Guide 167). The city rate is 3.07%; the combined rate is 8.20% with state, El Paso County and the Pikes Peak regional transportation authority (PPRTA). This is collected from customers. Colorado Springs uses the state's Sales and Use Tax System (SUTS) portal for filing.

calculatorOption.label: Colorado Springs
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Colorado Springs receipts tax, head tax, or license fee; city sales tax on SaaS is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Aurora, CO

fixedAnnual.name: City business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Required for any person, including corporations, that conducts business in Aurora or has employees working there. The fee is $28 per two-year license (initial or renewal), about $14 a year, plus a one-time $19 online application fee. Each location needs its own license.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Aurora has no gross receipts tax. Its occupational privilege (head) tax, formerly $2 employee + $2 employer per month, was repealed effective Jan 1, 2025 (Ordinance 2022-77).

Aurora is a home-rule city that collects its own sales tax. Secondary sources say it taxes SaaS, but I could not confirm this on an official Aurora page. Either way it is collected from customers.

calculatorOption.label: Aurora
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Aurora receipts or head tax (OPT repealed 2025); $28 two-year business license (~$14/yr).

jurisdictions.name: Boulder, CO

fixedAnnual.name: City business (sales/use tax) license
fixedAnnual.notes: Every business engaged in business in Boulder must hold a city business license, and the license always comes with a tax return filing requirement, even when $0 is due. The renewal page lists no renewal fee. The page does mention a $25 application fee for a new or relocated location. A secondary source describes this as a one-time $25 per location, so treat it as one-time rather than annual (medium confidence).

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Boulder has no gross receipts tax and no occupational privilege (head) tax.

Sales tax: Boulder's code defines computer software to include software as a service and internet subscription services, so SaaS used in Boulder is taxable at the 3.86% city rate (9.195% combined in 2026). This is collected from customers. Custom software is exempt.

calculatorOption.label: Boulder
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Boulder receipts or head tax; business license has no recurring fee; city sales tax on SaaS is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Greenwood Village, CO

fixedAnnual.name: Occupational privilege tax license
fixedAnnual.notes: One-time $10 application fee. No annual renewal is required. All businesses located in the Village must hold this license.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
I included this Denver Tech Center office hub because of its head tax; it has no gross receipts tax.

Occupational privilege tax (OPT, a head tax), which belongs in payroll expenses: $2 per month employee portion plus $2 per month employer portion for each person earning $250 or more in a calendar month for work in the Village. Owners, partners and officers earning under $250 a month owe only the employer portion.

The other remaining Colorado head taxes are Glendale ($5 + $5 per month, earnings over $750/month) and Sheridan ($3 + $3 per month, no earnings threshold); both are also payroll expenses. I found no Colorado municipality that levies a gross receipts or business-income tax on software or professional-services firms.

calculatorOption.label: Greenwood Village
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Greenwood Village receipts tax; $2/employee/month employer OPT belongs in payroll expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut
jurisdictions.taxYear: Income year 2026 (statutory rates); 2025 return figures from the Rev. 12/25 CT-1120 instructions; annual report fee is current as of Oct 2026

fixedAnnual.name: Corporation business tax minimum ($250 floor on the capital base tax)
fixedAnnual.notes: Confirmed from the statute (CGS 12-214, 12-219) and the 2025 CT-1120 instructions, Schedule B and Schedule C line 1a. Every company 'carrying on, or having the right to carry on, business in this state' owes the greatest of three amounts: (a) 7.5% of apportioned net income, (b) the capital base tax, or (c) $250. A Delaware corporation registered in CT has the 'right to carry on business' there, so it owes at least $250 even with losses and no CT revenue. The amount is prorated if the company was registered or doing business in CT for 11 months or less of the year, and tax credits cannot bring it below $250. Capital base rates (CGS 12-219(a)(1) in the 2026 Supplement): 2.1 mills (0.21%) for 2025, 1.6 mills for 2026, 1.1 mills for 2027, and 0 for 2028 and later. The $250 floor and $1M cap stay in place after 2028. The capital base is book net worth, averaged over the start and end of the year: capital stock at par, plus paid-in surplus and retained earnings (a deficit counts as negative), plus surplus reserves, minus holdings of private-corporation stock. It is apportioned by where the company's assets are (CGS 12-219a), and cash and other intangibles count as located at the principal place of business. So a company headquartered outside CT with only a few CT employees almost always pays just $250. A VC-funded company headquartered in CT can owe much more. Example: average book equity of $7M gives $11,200 for 2026 and $7,700 for 2027, then $250 from 2028. SAFEs and convertible notes booked as liabilities do not count toward book equity. The 10% surtax does not apply when the tax is $250 or gross income is under $100M (combined-group filers excepted).

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report, foreign stock corporation (Secretary of the State)
fixedAnnual.notes: Business.CT.gov lists $435 for the foreign stock corporation annual report. It must be filed online every year. Not to be confused with the domestic corporation fee, or the separate one-time $435 fee to register as a foreign corporation (registration fee recalled, not verified this session).

profitTaxes.name: Corporation business tax (net income base)
profitTaxes.notes: 7.5% of apportioned CT net income, with a single receipts factor for apportionment. NOL carryforwards can offset at most 50% of apportioned income (CT-1120 Sched. A line 4). This is $0 before profit, but the $250 minimum or capital base tax still applies. A 10% surtax applies only to companies with gross income of $100M or more, or to combined-group filers. It was extended through the 2028 income year, and on the capital base component only for 2026–2027 (PA 25-168).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Nexus: a company not otherwise taxable in CT has no economic nexus with less than $500,000 of CT-source receipts (DRS IP 2010(29.1)). Having employees or an office in CT, or registering there, creates nexus regardless of that threshold. Sales and use taxes (collected from customers, so pass-through): computer and data processing services, including B2B SaaS/remote software access, are taxed at 1% where the benefit is received in CT (DRS PS 2006(8)). Secondary sources say SaaS for personal use is taxed as a digital good at 6.35% (Special Notice 2019(8); not read directly). CT also taxes 'business analysis, management, management consulting and public relations services' at the general 6.35% rate (CGS 12-407(a)(37)(J)). A professional-services company selling those services to CT customers must collect this tax. Payroll (already in expenses): employer state unemployment insurance on a capped wage base. CT Paid Leave contributions come out of employee pay, not the employer's (recalled, not verified this session). There is no state or local payroll or head tax. The Business Entity Tax never applied to C corps and has been repealed (recalled). Local: municipalities can levy only property taxes. A business with office equipment in CT owes municipal personal property tax and must file a declaration by Nov 1 (see the city entries). The 2026 session (PA 26-68) changed corporation tax only to respond to the federal FY25 reconciliation act (bonus depreciation decoupling, R&E timing). It did not change the minimum or the capital base schedule.

calculatorOption.label: Connecticut
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; $250 minimum corporation business tax plus $435 foreign-corporation annual report. A CT-headquartered company may instead owe capital base tax of 0.16% of book equity in 2026 and 0.11% in 2027, falling to the $250 minimum from 2028.

jurisdictions.name: Stamford, CT
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026-27 (Oct 1, 2025 grand list)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No local receipts, income, or business license tax: CT municipalities can levy only property taxes (OLR 2014-R-0037), and the 2025 and 2026 Acts Affecting Taxes reports show no new local business tax. The only local cost is business personal property tax on equipment and furniture, which depends on assets, not revenue. A declaration is due Nov 1 each year, with a 25% penalty for filing late or not at all (CGS 12-41(f)). Property is assessed at 70% of value as of Oct 1 (CGS 12-62a). CT OPM open data gives a 28.47-mill real/personal rate for FY2027. Local press reported a 27.17-mill personal property rate, and real estate rates vary by district; I did not reconcile the two figures. Example: $30k of depreciated equipment works out to about $600/yr. Treat this as an expense, not a revenue tax.

calculatorOption.label: Stamford
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city receipts or business tax in Stamford (CT towns levy only property tax); business personal property tax on equipment is not modeled.

jurisdictions.name: Hartford, CT
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026-27 (Oct 1, 2025 grand list)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No local receipts, income, or business license tax: CT municipalities can levy only property taxes (OLR 2014-R-0037). Business personal property tax applies on equipment, with a declaration due Nov 1, a 25% late or non-filing penalty, and assessment at 70% of value. Hartford's real/personal mill rate is 69.95 for FY2027 per CT OPM open data (68.95 for FY2026), the highest of the cities checked. Example: $30k of depreciated equipment works out to about $1,470/yr. This depends on assets, not revenue.

calculatorOption.label: Hartford
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city receipts or business tax in Hartford (CT towns levy only property tax); business personal property tax on equipment is not modeled.
