jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026-27 (Oct 1, 2025 grand list)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No local receipts, income, or business license tax: CT municipalities can levy only property taxes (OLR 2014-R-0037). Business personal property tax applies on equipment, with a declaration due Nov 1, a 25% late or non-filing penalty, and assessment at 70% of value. New Haven's mill rate is 39.962 for FY2027 per CT OPM open data (39.4 for FY2026). Example: $30k of depreciated equipment works out to about $840/yr. This depends on assets, not revenue.

calculatorOption.label: New Haven
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city receipts or business tax in New Haven (CT towns levy only property tax); business personal property tax on equipment is not modeled.

jurisdictions.name: Bridgeport, CT
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026-27 (Oct 1, 2025 grand list)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Included because it is CT's largest city; it has no local receipts or business tax, and no other CT city does either (municipalities can levy only property taxes, OLR 2014-R-0037). Business personal property tax applies on equipment. Bridgeport's real/personal mill rate is 27.95 for FY2027 per CT OPM open data, down from 43.45 for FY2026. Example: $30k of depreciated equipment works out to about $590/yr.

calculatorOption.label: Bridgeport
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city receipts or business tax in Bridgeport (CT towns levy only property tax); business personal property tax on equipment is not modeled.

jurisdictions.name: Delaware
jurisdictions.taxYear: Franchise tax: 2025 report (due Mar 1, 2026) / 2026 tax year. Gross receipts tax: 2026 (30 Del. C. § 2301 as currently codified, latest amendment 84 Del. Laws c. 474)

receiptsTaxes.name: Delaware gross receipts tax (occupational / professional / general services license fee on gross receipts)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts from services rendered or goods sold 'within this State' (30 Del. C. § 2301(e)). In practice this is origin-based: a business located in Delaware pays on its receipts from services performed there, including for out-of-state customers (Division of Revenue FAQ: tax on 'the total gross revenues of a business, regardless of their source'; paid by the 'provider of services in the state'). A SaaS company with no Delaware office or staff selling remotely to Delaware customers is probably not covered, but Delaware's guidance doesn't address remote service providers.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Delaware-sourced gross receipts. Statutorily it's a deduction of $100,000 per month (monthly filers) or $300,000 per quarter (quarterly filers; new licensees file quarterly), not a cliff, so about $1.2M a year of Delaware receipts is tax-free and only the excess is taxed.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rate 0.3983% and the $100k/month ($300k/quarter) deduction are in 30 Del. C. § 2301(d)(1)-(2), confirmed on delcode.delaware.gov. The Division of Revenue rate table lists Professional Services, Occupational/Professional and General Services at 0.003983 with a $100,000 monthly exclusion. That table is an old PDF (2016 metadata), but it matches the statute. SaaS is normally licensed as services or professional services; this classification comes from secondary sources, not an official ruling. If the Division classed software as sales of goods, the retailer rate would be 0.7468%, also with a $100k/month exclusion; that classification is unconfirmed. One deduction per enterprise under common ownership or control (§ 2301(d)). No deductions for cost of goods, labor or taxes. Monthly returns are due on the 20th; quarterly returns at the end of the month after the quarter ends. Modeling caveat: the calculator applies the rate to all sourced revenue once you cross the threshold, which overstates this tax by up to 0.003983 × $1.2M ≈ $4,780/yr compared with the true excess-only deduction.

fixedAnnual.name: Delaware franchise tax (domestic corporation, Assumed Par Value Capital method minimum)
fixedAnnual.notes: Every Delaware-incorporated corporation owes this wherever it operates. APVC method: $400 per $1,000,000 of assumed par value capital, or any part of a million; minimum $400, maximum $200,000 ($250,000 for Large Corporate Filers). Assumed par value capital ≈ gross assets × (authorized shares ÷ issued shares). The $400 minimum only holds while that product is at or below $1M. A venture-backed startup holding cash pays more. My worked example of the official method: $5M gross assets, 8M issued and 10M authorized shares gives $6.25M, rounded up to $7M, so $2,800. The Authorized Shares method that Delaware bills by default starts at $175 but is $85,165 for 10M authorized shares, so file using APVC. Due March 1. Quarterly estimates are required if $5,000 or more is owed.

fixedAnnual.name: Delaware annual report filing fee (non-exempt domestic corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 since Sept 1, 2019, filed with the franchise tax by March 1. Late penalty is $200 plus 1.5%/month interest. A foreign corporation (one incorporated elsewhere) would instead file a $250 annual report by June 30, but that doesn't apply to a Delaware C corp.

fixedAnnual.name: Delaware business license (general / professional services)
fixedAnnual.notes: Only owed if the company actually conducts business in Delaware (office or staff there). Being incorporated in Delaware is not enough. $75 for the first location plus $25 for each additional location (30 Del. C. § 2301(a)-(b)). Renews each December 31; prorated in the first year; a 3-year license costs 3× with no discount. Not included in the calculator's fixedPerYear because the default assumes the company is incorporated but not located in Delaware.

profitTaxes.name: Delaware corporation income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 8.7% of Delaware taxable income (30 Del. C. § 1902(a)), apportioned by a single sales factor since 2020. Zero before profit. Only applies if the corporation carries on business or holds property in Delaware; a Delaware corporation with no Delaware activity doesn't file. Exempts § 1902(b)(8) holding companies.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Delaware has no sales or use tax, so SaaS and services sold to Delaware customers carry no pass-through sales tax; the gross receipts tax is charged to the seller instead. Payroll items (count in expenses): Delaware personal income tax withholding, state unemployment insurance, and Delaware Paid Family & Medical Leave contributions, which started in 2025 (rates not verified in this research). Key modeling point: nearly every venture-backed startup is a Delaware corporation, so the $450 (franchise minimum plus annual report) applies even to companies that never set foot in Delaware. The gross receipts tax and $75 license apply only to companies that operate in Delaware, and for those, receipts from work performed in Delaware (often nearly all revenue) count, not just Delaware customers. Consider splitting the UI into 'Delaware (incorporated)' at $450 fixed and 'Delaware (operating there)' at 0.3983% over $1.2M/yr of Delaware receipts plus $75. If you keep one option, the default share below is Delaware's population share; set it to around 100% for a company based in Delaware. The franchise tax rises with cash on hand under the APVC method (about $400 per $1M of gross assets × authorized/issued), which can matter for a well-funded pre-profit company.

calculatorOption.label: Delaware
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Every Delaware corporation pays the $400 franchise tax minimum (assumed par value method) plus the $50 annual report. If you operate in Delaware, 0.3983% of Delaware receipts above $100k/month is also owed (plus a $75 license); set the share near 100% if you're based there.

jurisdictions.name: Wilmington, DE
jurisdictions.taxYear: City FY2027 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027) tax rates; business license fees for calendar year 2026 (Code § 5-101 as codified through Ord. 25-073, Dec 11, 2025, Supp. 72)

fixedAnnual.name: Wilmington city business license – 'Computer services' (nonprofessional service classification)
fixedAnnual.notes: Wilmington Code § 5-101 (raised from $120 to $200 by Ord. 23-014(sub 1), effective July 1, 2023). Calendar-year license, prorated by month in the first year (§ 5-46). Each classification needs its own license (§ 5-77B), so a company also licensed for consulting/professional services (Consultants or Miscellaneous professional service, $300) would pay $200 + $300 = $500. § 5-101(b): a business under 3 years old with 10 or fewer full-time employees may pay the fee in force before the code's most recent amendment (likely the pre-2023 $120; not confirmed). Branch license is $50. Only owed if the company does business in the city. § 5-31(2) excludes a corporation whose only city activity is a statutory (registered-agent) office, which covers most Delaware corps whose registered agent is in Wilmington. Unresolved: § 5-34 waives the license for entities described in § 44-107(c), and § 44-107(c)(1) lists 'any entity classified as a corporation'. Read literally, that would exempt C corps from the license (and the head tax), but other code provisions and city practice treat corporations as licensees. I couldn't resolve this from the code.

profitTaxes.name: Wilmington net profits tax (unincorporated businesses only)
profitTaxes.notes: The 1.25% net profits tax (Code § 44-107(a)(3)-(4), FY2027 rate sheet) applies only to sole proprietors and partnerships. § 44-107(c)(1) exempts any entity classified as a corporation, so a C corp owes 0%.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Wilmington has no gross receipts tax on software or services; its only receipts-based taxes are franchise and gas taxes on utilities (2% electric, 5% cable, 2% gas) and a 2% lodging tax. Payroll items (count in expenses): (1) Wage/earned income tax of 1.25% on residents' wages and on nonresidents' wages earned in the city, withheld by the employer (§ 44-107; FY2027 rate sheet). (2) Head tax of $15 per employee per month for each employee beyond 5 working in the city (§ 5-102; FY2027 rate sheet), so a 20-person office pays $15 × 15 × 12 = $2,700/yr. Part-timers are converted at 173 hours = 1 employee. There is a head-tax exemption program for employers with 50+ full-time employees committing to 5 years in the city (§ 5-102A). The city website (wilmingtonde.gov) blocked automated access, so the fees come from the codified ordinances (Municode, Supp. 72) and the city's FY2027 budget tax-rate sheet.

calculatorOption.label: Wilmington
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $200/yr city business license (computer services; $500 if also licensed as consultants); no receipts tax. The $15/employee/month head tax over 5 employees and the 1.25% wage tax belong in payroll.

fixedAnnual.notes: Dover Code App. F as amended by Ord. 2024-22. Covers computer programming services, systems design and consulting, data processing and information retrieval. jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Newark Code ch. 13 art. VII; 2026 fee schedule effective Jan 1, 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Newark city business license – Class III (offices for professional services and administrative activities)
fixedAnnual.notes: Newark Code § 13-56: $1 × license fee ratio (163 for Class III offices) = $163, plus the § 13-57 employment adjustment ($0 for up to 5 full-time employees; +$50 for employees 6-10; +$0.50/employee for the next 90; +$1.00 for the next 200; +$1.50 beyond 300), plus a $5 technology fee (§ 13-64). Total is $168 for 5 or fewer employees and $218 for 6-10. Add $35 if in Downtown Newark (§ 13-56.1). A sole operator with no employees may pay a flat $100 (§ 13-58(a)(3)).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No gross receipts, wage or head tax. The employment adjustment is a small per-employee add-on inside the license fee.

calculatorOption.label: Newark (DE)
calculatorOption.assumptionText: About $168/yr Newark business license for a professional/administrative office with 5 or fewer employees ($218 with 6-10); no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Florida
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (annual report due Jan 1 - May 1, 2026; corporate income tax rate for tax years beginning on/after 1/1/2022)

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report (profit corporation, domestic or foreign)
fixedAnnual.notes: $61.25 annual report fee (s. 607.0122) + $88.75 supplemental corporate fee (s. 607.193) = $150, filed on Sunbiz between Jan 1 and May 1. A $400 late fee applies after May 1 and Sunbiz says it cannot be waived. The one-time foreign qualification is $35 for the application plus $35 for the registered-agent designation; that is not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Florida corporate income/franchise tax
profitTaxes.notes: 5.5% of Florida-apportioned net income; the first $50,000 of Florida net income is exempt. Nothing is owed before profit, but every corporation doing business in Florida must still file Form F-1120 each year, even when no tax is due. Florida has no franchise/capital-stock tax and no minimum tax.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No state gross-receipts tax applies to a SaaS/services company. Florida's Ch. 203 gross receipts tax covers only utility and communications-service providers. SaaS: Florida DOR TAA 16A-014 (2016) held that software subscriptions and cloud computing delivered electronically, with no tangible property, are not subject to Florida sales tax. Electronically delivered software is generally not taxable under Rule 12A-1.032; software on tangible media is taxable. Business rent tax: the 2% state sales tax on commercial rent (s. 212.031) was repealed for rental periods beginning on/after Oct 1, 2025 (TIP 25A01-04), so office rent is no longer taxed. Payroll (count in expenses): reemployment (state unemployment) tax for new employers is 2.7% on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages. Florida has no state personal income tax and no city payroll/head taxes. Tangible personal property tax: each return gets a $25,000 assessed-value exemption, so a startup with under $25k of office equipment owes nothing after filing an initial DR-405 to claim the exemption. Documentary stamp tax: 0.35% ($0.35 per $100) on promissory notes/written obligations made, executed or delivered in Florida, capped at $2,450 for unsecured notes. This is relevant to venture debt or convertible notes signed in Florida; it is not annual. Local business taxes (Ch. 205) are flat fees by business classification, sometimes scaled by employees or square footage, and owed per physical location. Rate changes are capped at 5% every other year (s. 205.0535). The Miami/Miami-Dade, Jacksonville/Duval, Tampa/Hillsborough and Orlando/Orange codes I read have no receipts-measured classification for software/services. I did not find any Florida city that levies a gross-receipts tax on software/services firms. Miami Beach, Fort Lauderdale, St. Petersburg and Tallahassee were not individually checked, but they operate under the same Ch. 205 flat-fee framework.

calculatorOption.label: Florida
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Florida receipts or franchise tax; $150 annual report fee; 5.5% corporate income tax only once profitable (first $50k exempt).

jurisdictions.name: Miami, FL
jurisdictions.taxYear: Local business tax year Oct 1, 2026 - Sep 30, 2027 (rates as codified in City of Miami Code s. 31-50 and Miami-Dade Code s. 8A-223.1, current on Municode 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: City of Miami Business Tax Receipt: Computer or data processing service (BTR code 1520)
fixedAnnual.notes: Flat $99/yr per location (City Code s. 31-50). Other classes the city might assign instead: Administrative office (0070) $131; Consultant (1530) $116; Data exchange service (3550) $606. All receipts expire Sep 30. Late penalty is 10% in October plus 5%/month, capped at 25%.

fixedAnnual.name: City of Miami Certificate of Use annual renewal (re-inspection)
fixedAnnual.notes: A Certificate of Use is required before a BTR and is renewed every fiscal year. The office/commercial annual re-inspection fee is $63 for 500-2,500 sq ft ($50 under 500 sq ft; $75 for 2,500-5,000; $88 for 5,000-15,000). The first year adds a $50 application fee and a $313 initial inspection for the first 2,000 sq ft. A separate fire safety assessment may also apply; I did not find its amount.

fixedAnnual.name: Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax: Service Business
fixedAnnual.notes: $30 for 1-10 employees + $3 per additional employee (s. 8A-223.1), plus a 50% Beacon Council surcharge (s. 8A-171.2): $45 for 1-10 employees, $4.50 per additional employee (e.g. $90 at 20 employees). The surcharged figure matches what the Tax Collector publishes. This county tax applies countywide, inside cities too. If the county instead classes the company as 'Unclassified business' it is $100 + 50% = $150. A separate 'Administrative office' receipt (same $30+$3/employee base) can be required in addition (s. 8A-207.1).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city or county gross-receipts tax, payroll tax or head tax. These fees are owed only if the company has a physical business location (an office, or a home-based business) in the City of Miami. Selling to Miami customers does not trigger them. The total assumes about 10 employees and an office under 2,500 sq ft: $99 + $63 + $45 = $207/yr. The Miami-Dade 1% discretionary sales surtax applies only to taxable sales, and Florida SaaS is generally not taxable.

calculatorOption.label: Miami
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; if you have an office in Miami, about $207/yr in flat fees (city computer-services BTR $99 + Certificate of Use renewal $63 + Miami-Dade County business tax $45).

jurisdictions.name: Jacksonville, FL
jurisdictions.taxYear: Local business tax year Oct 1, 2026 - Sep 30, 2027 (Jacksonville Ordinance Code chs. 770/772; Duval Tax Collector BTR calculator checked Oct 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Jacksonville municipal business tax: data processing (s. 772.326(a)(8))
fixedAnnual.notes: The code puts 'data processing' in one flat $625/yr class with introduction, matrimonial and escort services. A software/SaaS company is likely to fall in this class. If the Tax Collector instead uses 'Public service or repair, not specified' (s. 772.326(a)(21)), the tax is $31.25 for the first employee + $5 per additional employee (max $1,031.25), or $76.25 at 10 employees. 'Consultant' is $100 municipal + $30 county.

fixedAnnual.name: Duval County business tax: public service (s. 770.323)
fixedAnnual.notes: Scaled by employees, with principals counted: 1-5 $13.75; 6-10 $33.75; 11-15 $50; 16-20 $70; 21+ $93.75. The calculator shows a combined county + city total of $658.75 for data processing at 10 employees. Receipts expire Sep 30. Late penalty is 10% in October plus 5%/month, up to 25%. New receipts issued after Apr 1 pay half.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Jacksonville and Duval County are consolidated, so the Duval Tax Collector bills the county and municipal pieces together. There is no gross-receipts, payroll or head tax. The fees are owed only with a physical business location in Jacksonville/Duval. I used the conservative (higher) 'data processing' classification. With the generic service class, a 10-person company would pay $110/yr total ($196.25 at 20 employees). Which class applies depends on the Tax Collector, so treat the classification as uncertain.

calculatorOption.label: Jacksonville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; if you have an office in Jacksonville, about $659/yr in city + county business tax under the 'data processing' class at 6-10 employees (about $110 if classed as a general service business).

jurisdictions.name: Tampa, FL
jurisdictions.taxYear: Local business tax year Oct 1, 2026 - Sep 30, 2027 (Tampa Code s. 24-120 and Hillsborough County Code s. 46-200, current on Municode 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: City of Tampa business tax: Computer/Data supplies (software and program development), class 070
fixedAnnual.notes: $231.52 + $17.35 per worker (s. 24-120). That is $405.02 at 10 workers and $578.52 at 20. 'Worker' includes everyone engaged in the business under any contract of hire. Alternatives: Computer service (072) $115.76 + $8.67/worker; Computer systems analyst (073) $115.76 + $17.35/worker; Consultant $115.76; Administrative office $217.04 (1-5 workers), $325.57 (6-10), $434.10 (over 10).

fixedAnnual.name: Hillsborough County business tax: public service (s. 46-200)
fixedAnnual.notes: Scaled by employees, with principals counted: 1-5 $22; 6-10 $54; 11-15 $80; 16-20 $112; 21+ $150. 'Miscellaneous business not otherwise provided' is $225. Applies countywide.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no gross-receipts, payroll or head tax. These fees are owed only with a business location in Tampa. The total assumes 10 workers: $405.02 city + $54 county = $459.02/yr. The fees grow by about $17/worker (city) plus county tier steps. The Hillsborough figures come from the county code. Its Tax Collector may bill slightly different amounts if rates were raised under the 5%-every-other-year allowance; I did not check the Tax Collector's billing.

calculatorOption.label: Tampa
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; if you have an office in Tampa, about $459/yr in flat business taxes (city software-development class $231.52 + $17.35/worker at 10 workers, plus Hillsborough County $54).

jurisdictions.name: Orlando, FL
jurisdictions.taxYear: Local business tax year Oct 1, 2026 - Sep 30, 2027 (Orlando City Code ch. 36 and Orange County Code s. 25-103, current on Municode 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: City of Orlando business tax: Electronic Data Processing and Service Company (computer programming, software development), s. 36.35(86)
fixedAnnual.notes: Uses the Number of Workers scale (s. 36.36(1)). The square-footage fee is $55.13 under 2,000 sq ft ($110.25 for 2,000-5,000; $275.63 above 5,000). The worker fee is $82.69 for up to 3 workers, $132.30 for 4-5, $165.38 for 6-15, $209.48 for 16-25 and $248.06 for 26-50. At 6-15 workers in under 2,000 sq ft that is $55.13 + $165.38 = $220.51. Receipts expire Sep 30. Penalty runs from 10% to 25%, plus $250 from Feb 1. New receipts are prorated.

fixedAnnual.name: City of Orlando Certificate of Use
fixedAnnual.notes: The city's BTR guide lists a $15 CoU fee alongside the BTR. One secondary source says $20 and annual renewal. I did not confirm the exact current amount, and there is also a $5 administrative fee.

fixedAnnual.name: Orange County local business tax: public service (s. 25-103)
fixedAnnual.notes: Scaled by workers: 1-10 $30; 11-20 $40; 21-30 $50; 31-40 $70. 'Miscellaneous businesses not otherwise provided for' is $225. Applies countywide.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no gross-receipts, payroll or head tax. These fees are owed only with a business location in Orlando. The total assumes 6-10 workers in under 2,000 sq ft: $220.51 + $15 + $30 = $265.51/yr.

calculatorOption.label: Orlando
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; if you have an office in Orlando, about $266/yr in flat fees (city data-processing BTR $220.51 at 6-15 workers in under 2,000 sq ft + $15 Certificate of Use + Orange County $30).

jurisdictions.name: Georgia
jurisdictions.taxYear: Income tax: 2025 (5.19%) and 2026 (4.99%). Net worth tax table: 2025 IT-611. Secretary of State fees: schedule effective Sept 6, 2025.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual registration (corporation, including foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 fee plus $10 service charge, online or paper (SOS Corporations Division fee schedule effective Sept 6, 2025). Due Jan 1 to April 1 each year. Late penalty is $25. There is also a one-time Certificate of Authority for a foreign corporation: $225 + $10 = $235. That is a one-time cost, not annual, and the penalty for doing business without one is $500.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate net worth tax (filed on Form 600)
fixedAnnual.notes: Graduated table, not a minimum tax. $0 if Georgia-taxable net worth is $100,000 or less. Then $125 (over $100k-$150k), $150 (to $200k), $200 (to $300k), $250 (to $500k), $300 (to $750k), $500 (to $1M), $750 (to $2M), $1,000 (to $4M), $1,250 (to $6M), $1,500 (to $8M), $1,750 (to $10M), $2,000 (to $12M), then +$500 per $2M band up to $4,500 (to $22M), with a $5,000 cap over $22M. Net worth = issued capital stock + paid-in surplus + retained earnings (accumulated deficits reduce it; a deficit net worth owes $0 but must still file). A foreign (e.g., Delaware) corporation multiplies its net worth by the Schedule 8 ratio: (GA balance-sheet assets + GA gross receipts) / (total assets + total gross receipts). So a startup headquartered elsewhere with a small Georgia footprint usually owes $0-$250. A Georgia-headquartered startup holding its VC cash in Georgia can owe roughly $500-$2,000 (example: $2M net worth at a 68% ratio = $1.36M, which owes $750). An initial return is due by the 15th day of the 4th month after qualifying. It is 50% if the first period is under 6 months.

profitTaxes.name: Georgia corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 4.99% for tax years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2026, per HB 463 (Georgia Economic Growth and Tax Relief Act of 2026, signed May 2026). The rate was 5.19% for 2025 (HB 111). HB 463 allows further 0.125-point annual cuts toward 3.99%, but these depend on revenue targets. Georgia ties the corporate rate to the individual rate. Apportionment is single-factor gross receipts. The NOL deduction is limited to 80%. Estimated payments are required only if Georgia net income is expected to exceed $25,000. Zero before profitability.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Georgia has NO state-level gross receipts, franchise, or margin tax. For a pre-profit corporation the only recurring state costs are the $60 annual registration and the net worth tax ($0 for most small or out-of-state-HQ startups). SaaS: Georgia DOR Rule 560-12-2-.118 (Digital Products) reportedly treats SaaS and electronically delivered prewritten software as not subject to sales/use tax. I saw this in DOR search summaries but could not open the rule text, so treat it as reported. Either way it would be pass-through. Payroll costs belong in expenses: Georgia income tax withholding, state unemployment insurance (taxable wage base $9,500 per employee; the new-employer rate is set by GDOL and was not verified here), and local per-employee components of city occupation taxes (see the city entries). Local occupation taxes (O.C.G.A. 48-13): nearly every Georgia city/county levies an annual 'business license' occupation tax on businesses with a location there. By state law (O.C.G.A. 48-13-5) the receipts base EXCLUDES sales of goods or services delivered to or received by customers outside Georgia. So for a nationally selling SaaS company, only Georgia-customer receipts are taxed, allocated among its Georgia locations (O.C.G.A. 48-13-14). A business with no Georgia location is taxed under O.C.G.A. 48-13-7 only by the locality with its largest Georgia dollar volume, and only if it has employees/agents soliciting or serving customers there or income-producing property there.

calculatorOption.label: Georgia
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Georgia gross receipts tax; $60 annual registration, plus net worth tax that is $0 at or below $100k of Georgia-apportioned net worth (up to $5,000 cap).

jurisdictions.name: Atlanta, GA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (certificates issued in 2026, Ord. 2025-35 / 25-O-1417); 2027 rates already enacted

receiptsTaxes.name: Atlanta occupation (business) tax - gross receipts component
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts attributable to the Atlanta location (O.C.G.A. 48-13-5 definition), EXCLUDING receipts from customers outside Georgia and payments to subcontractors/independent agents. For a company whose only Georgia office is in Atlanta, this is all its Georgia-customer revenue. It is allocated across locations if the company has several (Code 30-80). Based on prior-year actual gross receipts.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Georgia-customer gross receipts of the Atlanta location (first $10,000 covered by the $50 flat tax)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Software publishers (NAICS 513210), data processing/hosting (518210), custom programming (541511), computer systems design (541512) and other computer services (541519) are all Tax Class 5 on the city's 2026 NAICS list. Class 5 rate per $1,000 above the first $10,000: $1.40 through 2025, $1.88 for 2026, $2.35 from 2027. Management consulting (541611) is Class 6 ($2.21 in 2026, $2.77 in 2027). The full 2026 range is $0.81-$2.88 across classes 1-8, rising to $1.01-$3.61 in 2027. Receipts above the cap are untaxed: cap is $400M in 2026 and $600M from 2027. The city's own example: $1M receipts, 5 employees, class 5 = $2,202.20 for 2026. Renewal returns are due Feb 15 and payment by April 1. The late-renewal fee is $500, plus 1.5%/month interest.

fixedAnnual.name: Administrative (registration) fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $75 through 2025, $191 for 2026, $215 from 2027. It may be CPI-adjusted every two years starting 2028 (Code 30-62(a)).

fixedAnnual.name: Flat tax on first $10,000 of gross receipts
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 covers $0-$10,000 of gross receipts in every class (Code 30-62).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is also a per-employee component of $25 per employee beyond the first (prorated for part-time). This is a head tax and belongs in expenses. Example: 10 employees = $225. Licensed professionals can elect $400 per practitioner instead. That option rarely applies to a software company. The tax applies to businesses with a location/office in Atlanta (including the airport). A company with no Georgia location is taxed only if Atlanta is where it does the most Georgia business AND it has employees/agents soliciting or serving customers there or income-producing property there (Code 30-77). Atlanta has no separate payroll tax. Sales tax on SaaS: see the Georgia entry (reported as not taxable).

calculatorOption.label: Atlanta
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Office in Atlanta: $1.88 per $1,000 (2026, class 5 software/IT; $2.35 from 2027) on Georgia-customer receipts above $10k, plus $191 admin fee and $50 flat tax; $25 per employee beyond the first counted in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Savannah, GA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Revenue Ordinance of 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Savannah business tax (gross receipts x profitability class, bracketed)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the Savannah location produced within Georgia. Sales to customers outside Georgia, payments to subcontractors, and receipts already taxed by another Georgia locality are excluded. Filed by Jan 31 on prior-year actual receipts, which also serve as the current-year estimate.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (bracket 1 starts at $0.01)
receiptsTaxes.notes:
The tax is a bracketed table rather than a flat rate. Computer software programming (541511), website design (541511), data processing (514210) and management consulting (541611) are Profitability Class C. Class C amounts include the $75 base tax:
- $0.01-$30k: $88
- $30k-$100k: $131
- $100k-$200k: $200
- $200k-$300k: $277
- $300k-$500k: $388
- $500k-$750k: $548
- $750k-$1M: $714
- $1M-$2M: $1,130
- $2M-$3M: $1,766
- $3M-$4M: $2,349
- $4M-$5M: $2,879
- $5M-$6M: $3,355
- $6M-$8M: $4,062
- $8M-$10M: $4,961
- the top bracket, $50M and over: $16,229
The class C 'base rate' is 0.00089. $75 + 0.089% of receipts tracks the table within about $50 for receipts under $1M, then overstates it, because the marginal rate falls with size (about 0.075% effective at $1.5M). Classes A-F run from 0.00069 to 0.00119. Licensed professionals may elect $400 per practitioner.

fixedAnnual.name: Base tax (included in the bracket amounts)
fixedAnnual.notes: A non-prorated, non-refundable $75 base tax applies to every gross-receipts account. Any positive receipts up to $30,000 total $88 in class C. An amended certificate costs $25.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No per-employee component was found in the Savannah business tax. It applies to businesses with a location in Savannah city limits, and to out-of-state businesses with no Georgia location under O.C.G.A. 48-13-7. Unincorporated Chatham County has its own occupation tax (not researched). Payroll: none at the city level.

calculatorOption.label: Savannah
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Office in Savannah: about $75 + 0.089% of Georgia-customer receipts (class C bracket table, 2026).

jurisdictions.name: Sandy Springs, GA
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current schedule (rate PDF dated 2021, still linked from the city's Schedule of Rates page in Oct 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Sandy Springs business occupation tax - gross receipts component
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the Sandy Springs location under the O.C.G.A. 48-13-5 definition (excludes sales to customers outside Georgia)
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none stated
receiptsTaxes.notes: The rate depends on the first two digits of the NAICS code. NAICS 54 (custom programming 541511, systems design, consulting): fee class 18, 0.00185 ($1.85 per $1,000). NAICS 51 (software publishers, data processing/hosting): fee class 13, 0.0016 ($1.60 per $1,000). The full range is 0.00085-0.00195, and financial institutions pay 0.0025. The city page says the tax combines total gross receipts, profitability class, number of employees and flat components. It does not say whether the $50 flat covers a first slice of receipts (as Atlanta's does), so the rate is modeled on all Georgia receipts.

fixedAnnual.name: Administrative fee
fixedAnnual.notes: Non-refundable. Practitioners electing the $400 professional fee are exempt.

fixedAnnual.name: Flat-rate tax component
fixedAnnual.notes: Per the city's Schedule of Rates page.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Employee component: $13 per employee. This is a head tax and belongs in expenses. The page does not say whether the first employee is exempt. The rate PDF is dated 2021, so confirm with the city before relying on it.

calculatorOption.label: Sandy Springs
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Office in Sandy Springs: 0.185% of Georgia-customer receipts (NAICS 54; 0.16% if NAICS 51) plus $75 admin fee and $50 flat tax; $13 per employee counted in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Alpharetta, GA
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current code (Municode version Jul 31, 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Administrative fee
fixedAnnual.notes: Annual, non-prorated, non-refundable.

fixedAnnual.name: Employee-count occupation tax (tier base)
fixedAnnual.notes:
Tax is based only on headcount (full-time equivalents), with no gross receipts component. Tiers, each plus a per-employee amount:
- 1-4 employees: $125 + $10 each
- 5-10 employees: $200 + $10 each
- 11-25 employees: $325 + $10 each
- 26-49 employees: $475 + $10 each
- 50+ employees: $175 + $17 each
The $200 shown assumes the 5-10 tier; use $125 for 1-4 employees. The headcount must include all employees, including virtual and remote workers.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Alpharetta is a major north-metro Atlanta tech hub. It has no receipts tax, so cost does not scale with revenue. The $10-$17 per-employee amounts are a head tax and belong in expenses. Applies to businesses with a location/office in Alpharetta. Licensed practitioners can elect $400 per practitioner.

calculatorOption.label: Alpharetta
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Office in Alpharetta: no receipts tax; $75 admin fee + $200 base for 5-10 employees ($125 for 1-4); the $10 per employee is counted in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Columbus, GA (Columbus Consolidated Government)
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 actual / 2026 estimate occupation tax return

receiptsTaxes.name: Columbus occupation tax (gross receipts x profit class)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the Columbus location, excluding sales to customers outside Georgia (return Section H), subcontractor payments, and sales tax remitted. Filed on prior-year actual receipts with a current-year estimate.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rates per $1,000 for classes 1-8: $1.00, $1.82, $2.52, $3.21, $3.91, $4.61, $5.31, $6.00 (0.10%-0.60%). These are the highest per-$1,000 rates among the Georgia cities checked. The class comes from a 10-year IRS profitability ratio for the dominant NAICS, set by the finance department each November. I could not find a published class for software/IT (NAICS 51/5415), so 0.006 is the class-8 UPPER BOUND, not the confirmed rate. A business paying by April 1 gets a 2% discount.

fixedAnnual.name: Administrative fee
fixedAnnual.notes: Pre-printed on the return; not charged to practitioners electing the $400 per-practitioner option.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Columbus is Georgia's second-largest city. It has no per-employee component in the occupation tax. Renewal runs Jan 1 to April 1, with a 10% delinquency penalty plus 1.5%/month interest. Confirm the class for your NAICS with the Revenue Division at (706) 225-4100.

calculatorOption.label: Columbus (GA)
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Office in Columbus: up to 0.60% of Georgia-customer receipts (class 8 upper bound; the software class is unconfirmed, and the range is 0.10%-0.60%) plus $75 admin fee.

jurisdictions.name: Hawaii
jurisdictions.taxYear: Calendar 2026. GET rates have been unchanged since before 2024; the 0.5% county surcharges run through Dec 31, 2030. Corporate income tax rates are from the Rev. 2025 Form N-30 instructions. The 2026 legislative summary (Tax Announcement 2026-06) shows no change to the GET service rate or corporate rates.

receiptsTaxes.name: General Excise Tax (GET), state portion, retail and services rate
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross income from services or SaaS used or consumed in Hawaii, with no deduction for costs. Hawaii uses market-based sourcing under the export exemption (HRS 237-29.53, HAR 18-237-29.53-11, TIR 2018-06). Services to a business are sourced to where the customer's related business activities occur, or to its principal place of business if unrelated. Services to individuals are sourced to where they live. Services used or consumed outside Hawaii are exempt. Prewritten or electronically delivered software is treated as tangible personal property and is also taxed at 4% when delivered to Hawaii customers. Letter Ruling 2012-06 held that software used entirely outside Hawaii is not subject to GET.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: None for a business with physical presence in Hawaii (for example, employees there). Remote sellers with no physical presence have GET nexus only once they reach $100,000 of Hawaii gross income or 200 Hawaii transactions in the current or preceding calendar year.
receiptsTaxes.notes: The tax is imposed on the business, not the customer. The seller may visibly pass it on, up to 4.712% including the county surcharge. Hawaii has no small-business exemption and no tiers. There is a 0.5% 'wholesale services' rate only when the service is sold to a licensed seller who resells it to another party. That is uncommon for SaaS used by the buyer. Returns: G-45 is filed semiannually if annual liability is $2,000 or less, quarterly if $4,000 or less, otherwise monthly. G-49 is the annual reconciliation. A registered licensee must file even with $0 of Hawaii receipts.

receiptsTaxes.name: County surcharge on GET, 0.5%, levied by all four counties (Honolulu, Hawaii, Kauai, Maui)
receiptsTaxes.base: The same Hawaii-sourced receipts that are taxed at the 4% rate. Receipts are allocated among counties under HAR 18-237-8.6-01 to -10. The state collects it on the same GET return.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (follows GET nexus)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Honolulu levies 0.5% from Jan 1, 2007 to Dec 31, 2030. Kauai levies 0.5% from Jan 1, 2019 to Dec 31, 2030. Hawaii County levied 0.25% in 2019 and 0.5% from Jan 1, 2020 to Dec 31, 2030. Maui levies 0.5% from Jan 1, 2024 to Dec 31, 2030. Because the rate is the same in every county, it is modeled here at the state level (combined 4.5%), not as a separate Honolulu option. The surcharge does not apply to 0.5% wholesale or 0.15% insurance-commission activity. If the counties let it expire after 2030, the combined rate falls to 4%.

fixedAnnual.name: DCCA annual report, profit corporation (domestic or foreign)
fixedAnnual.notes: $12.50 if filed online, per the DCCA release dated July 1, 2025. The official fee schedule lists $15.00 (paper). It is due by the end of the calendar quarter containing the registration anniversary, with a $10 late fee per year of delinquency. The fee schedule also mentions a possible $1 State Archives fee on permanent records; it is unclear whether that applies to annual reports.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: The rate is 4.4% of taxable income up to $25,000, 5.4% from $25,000 to $100,000 (less $250), and 6.4% above $100,000 (less $1,250), per the Rev. 2025 N-30 instructions. Hawaii has no minimum tax or franchise tax for a general C corporation; the N-30 instructions describe none. A loss-making company owes $0.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: For a pre-profit SaaS or services company, the cost is GET at 4.5% of Hawaii-sourced gross receipts, profit or not, plus a $12.50 annual report. GET is legally a tax on the business, not a sales tax, which is why it is counted here. In practice many Hawaii B2B sellers add the 4.712% maximum pass-on to invoices. A company that does this successfully shifts the economic cost to customers, and the calculator then overstates the cost (the conservative direction). One-time costs: the GET license is a one-time $20 and stays active until closed, with no renewal fee. The foreign corporation Certificate of Authority is a one-time $50. Hawaii's export exemption means a Hawaii-based company owes GET only on revenue from Hawaii customers, not on its national revenue. Use tax (HRS ch. 238, not read from an official page this session): a Hawaii-located business that buys services, SaaS or goods from out-of-state vendors who do not charge GET may owe use tax on those purchases. That is an expense on purchases, not a receipts tax. 2026 legislation (Tax Announcement 2026-06): Act 182 adds 'information technology design and production services' as a qualifying activity for the State Enterprise Zone program, for businesses joining on or after July 1, 2026. That program can grant a multi-year GET exemption to certified businesses inside a zone. Act 24 repeals the Tax Credit for Research Activities and the High Technology Business Investment Tax Credit on Jan 1, 2029. Payroll items (expense side, from memory, not verified this session): state unemployment insurance; mandatory Temporary Disability Insurance, where employees may be charged up to 0.5% of wages up to a cap; and the Prepaid Health Care Act. That act requires employer-provided health insurance for employees working 20 or more hours a week, with the employee share capped at 1.5% of wages. Hawaii counties have no local income or payroll taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Hawaii
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 4.5% GET (4% state + 0.5% county surcharge, levied in every county through 2030) on revenue from Hawaii customers, with no threshold for a company present there (remote sellers only after $100k or 200 transactions in Hawaii), plus a $12.50 annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Honolulu, HI
jurisdictions.taxYear: Calendar 2026 (Oahu GET surcharge in effect Jan 1, 2007 to Dec 31, 2030)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: The City and County of Honolulu has one government for all of Oahu and no separate city. Its only receipts-based tax is the 0.5% GET county surcharge, which the state collects on the GET return. That surcharge is already included in the Hawaii state entry (4.5% combined), so it is not listed again here and must not be added twice. Honolulu has no general business license. The Department of Customer Services issues licenses only for specific trades such as auctioneers, pawnbrokers, peddlers, scrap and secondhand dealers, firearms, and pedicabs. Software or professional-services firms need only the state GET license. Honolulu has no local income, payroll or head tax. Real property tax applies only if the company owns real property; for a renter it is built into rent.

calculatorOption.label: Honolulu
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Honolulu's 0.5% GET surcharge is already included in the Hawaii 4.5% rate; Honolulu has no separate business license or city tax.

jurisdictions.name: Hawaii County (Hilo/Kona), HI
jurisdictions.taxYear: Calendar 2026 (surcharge 0.5% from Jan 1, 2020 to Dec 31, 2030)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Hawaii County has a 0.5% GET county surcharge (0.25% in 2019, 0.5% from 2020 to 2030). It is already included in the Hawaii state entry's 4.5% combined rate, so it is not additive. I found no county receipts tax beyond that. The county's Business & Occupation Licensing covers specific occupations such as auctioneers. I could not open the official page (HTTP 403), so the absence of a general business license is from secondary sources only.

calculatorOption.label: Hawaii County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Hawaii County's 0.5% GET surcharge is already included in the Hawaii 4.5% rate; no separate county business tax.

jurisdictions.name: Maui County, HI
jurisdictions.taxYear: Calendar 2026 (surcharge 0.5% from Jan 1, 2024 to Dec 31, 2030, Ordinance No. 5551)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Maui County adopted a 0.5% GET surcharge effective Jan 1, 2024 (Tax Announcement 2023-05). Its maximum pass-on rate is 4.712%. The surcharge is already included in the Hawaii state entry's 4.5% combined rate, so it is not additive. I found no other county receipts tax. I did not check the county's general business license rules on an official page.

calculatorOption.label: Maui County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Maui County's 0.5% GET surcharge (since 2024) is already included in the Hawaii 4.5% rate; no separate county business tax.

jurisdictions.name: Kauai County, HI
jurisdictions.taxYear: Calendar 2026 (surcharge 0.5% from Jan 1, 2019 to Dec 31, 2030)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Kauai County has a 0.5% GET county surcharge from 2019 to 2030. It is already included in the Hawaii state entry's 4.5% combined rate, so it is not additive. I found no other county receipts tax. I did not check the county's general business license rules on an official page.

calculatorOption.label: Kauai County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Kauai County's 0.5% GET surcharge is already included in the Hawaii 4.5% rate; no separate county business tax.

jurisdictions.name: Idaho
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (rates and fees carry into 2026; the online statute shows 5.3% and no 2026 change was found)

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate income tax minimum tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Idaho Code 63-3025: the corporate income tax "shall not be less than twenty dollars ($20.00)". Every corporation that is transacting business in Idaho, registered with the Secretary of State, or exercising its corporate franchise there owes it, even with zero or negative income. The Form 41ES instructions say: "If the amount is less than $20, use $20." The P.L. 86-272 exception does not help a SaaS or services company, because 86-272 only protects sales of tangible goods.

fixedAnnual.name: Permanent Building Fund (PBF) tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Idaho Code 63-3082: "Every person required to file an income tax return shall pay a tax of ten dollars ($10.00)." It is added on top of the $20 minimum on Form 41. On a combined return, it is $10 for each corporation in the group that is required to file.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report
fixedAnnual.notes: Idaho Code 30-21-214(b)(7): Annual report ... No fee. It is due by the end of the entity's anniversary month and must be filed to avoid administrative dissolution or revocation. Paper filings carry a $20 manual-processing surcharge (30-21-214(f)); filing online through SOSBiz is free. The foreign registration statement is a one-time $100 fee (30-21-214(b)(23)) and is not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Idaho corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 5.3% flat rate on Idaho taxable income, effective for tax years beginning January 1, 2025 (HB 40, 2025, which cut it from 5.695%). The statute currently online, which is updated each July 1 after the session, still reads 5.3%. 2026 House Bill 589 proposed changes to 63-3024 and 63-3025, but I found no evidence that it passed. Pre-profit, only the $20 minimum plus the $10 PBF are owed.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Idaho has no gross receipts, franchise, or margin tax. Sales tax is 6% statewide, but remotely accessed software (SaaS) is not taxable: Idaho Code 63-3616 excludes remotely accessed and electronically delivered software from 'tangible personal property'. Most professional services are not taxable either, so a SaaS or services seller usually collects nothing. Only resort cities (Ketchum, Sun Valley, McCall, Sandpoint, etc.) levy local option sales taxes, and Boise is not one of them. Payroll costs (count them in expenses): Idaho state income tax withholding; state unemployment insurance (rates are experience-rated, and new-employer rates and the taxable wage base change each year — check the Idaho Department of Labor); and the Workforce Development Training Fund and administrative reserve, which are collected with UI. Idaho has no state disability or paid-leave payroll tax. There is no state general business license. You must register with the Tax Commission for withholding once you have Idaho employees.

calculatorOption.label: Idaho
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Idaho receipts tax; $20 minimum corporate tax + $10 Permanent Building Fund tax per year; annual report is free.

jurisdictions.name: Boise, ID
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Boise has no city income, payroll, or gross receipts tax; Idaho cities have no authority to levy them. Boise has no general business license. The City Clerk licenses only specific regulated activities (animals, food and alcohol, security services, vehicles and drivers, vendors, pawnbrokers, massage, tree service, special events), and the official fee schedule lists no license for software, consulting, or professional services. Boise levies no local sales tax, since it is not a resort city. The Boise Auditorium District tax applies only to lodging. Other Treasure Valley cities: per search-result snippets of their official clerk pages (I could not open the pages directly, HTTP 403), Meridian does not require a general business license, and Nampa issues licenses only for specific activities (alcohol, peddlers, pawnbrokers, security, etc.). I found no Idaho city with a receipts tax or general business tax on software or services firms.

calculatorOption.label: Boise
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Boise has no business, receipts, or income tax and no general business license for software/services firms.

jurisdictions.name: Illinois
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026 (franchise-tax exemption in effect from 1/1/2025 with no sunset in current 805 ILCS 5/15.65; new digital levies from P.A. 104-0468 start 1/1/2027)

receiptsTaxes.name: No general gross receipts tax (state level)
receiptsTaxes.base: n/a
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Illinois has no general gross-receipts, margin, or B&O-style tax on software or professional-services companies. P.A. 104-0468 (SB 3019, FY2027 revenue omnibus, enacted June 2026) adds niche levies starting 1/1/2027: (1) the Targeted Advertising Services Tax, 10% of gross receipts from targeted advertising delivered to Illinois users, owed only by providers with more than $1,000,000 of Illinois targeted-ad receipts in the prior 12 months; (2) a Social Media Platform Fee (Secretary of State) for platforms with more than 100,000 Illinois users. Neither applies to ordinary B2B SaaS or services. An ad-tech or social product would need its own line item.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report filing fee (foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: 805 ILCS 5/15.10(o): $75 for each annual report, domestic or foreign. Due before the first day of the anniversary month. A secondary source (Ahlbeck & Cook, June 2026) confirms the $75 is still owed when the franchise tax works out to $0.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual franchise tax (foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: 805 ILCS 5/15.75: 0.1% of the paid-in capital represented in Illinois, with a $25 minimum and a $2,000,000 maximum. 805 ILCS 5/15.65(d) exempts the first $10,000 of liability on and after 1/1/2025, with no end date in the current text. That $10,000 corresponds to about $10M of Illinois-allocated paid-in capital. Allocation (15.70(e)) = (IL property + gross business transacted at or from IL places of business) / (total property + total business). A foreign corp can instead elect 100% of paid-in capital. Example: a Delaware startup with $50M raised and a 10% IL factor has $5M allocated, $5,000 of tax, all exempt, so it pays $0. Liability above $10,000 is taxed only on the excess. HB 5526 (2026), which would raise the exemption to $100,000 in 2027 and repeal the domestic tax in 2028, was not enacted as of mid-2026. One-time costs, not annual: $150 to qualify as a foreign corp (15.10(j)), plus initial and additional franchise taxes at 0.15% of IL-allocated paid-in capital when capital is raised. 15.65 applies the same $10,000 exemption to 'the tax imposed under this Section', which includes initial and additional taxes, but I could not confirm how the Secretary of State applies it per filing (ilsos.gov was unreachable).

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 35 ILCS 5/201(b)(14): 7% of net income for tax years beginning on or after 7/1/2017. Single-sales-factor apportionment with market-based sourcing for services.

profitTaxes.name: Personal Property Tax Replacement Income Tax (PPRT)
profitTaxes.notes: 35 ILCS 5/201(c)-(d): 2.5% of net income for C corporations, on top of the 7%, for a combined 9.5%. NOL caps matter in the first profitable years. 35 ILCS 5/207 as amended by P.A. 104-0468 caps the NOL deduction at $500,000 for tax years ending 12/31/2024 through 12/30/2027. After that the cap is the greater of $500,000 or 15% of net income (TYE 12/31/2027), 30% (2028), 50% (2029), 65% (2030), and 80% (TYE on/after 12/31/2031). Zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Sales/use tax: SaaS is generally not subject to Illinois Retailers' Occupation/Use Tax because no software is transferred. Canned software that is delivered or licensed can be taxable at 6.25% plus local rates. Professional services are not taxable. I could not reach IDOR (tax.illinois.gov) from this environment, so the SaaS position rests on multiple secondary sources only. Payroll: Illinois unemployment insurance (IDES) and withholding are payroll expenses. There is no state head tax. Local taxes: Ill. Const. art. VII §6(e) bars home-rule units from licensing for revenue or taxing income, earnings, or occupations unless the General Assembly authorizes it. That is why Illinois cities do not levy gross-receipts or income taxes on service businesses. The one major exception for SaaS is Chicago's Personal Property Lease Transaction Tax, which is a pass-through tax. Searches found no other Illinois municipality taxing SaaS or services receipts.

calculatorOption.label: Illinois
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Illinois receipts tax; $75 annual report fee; franchise tax is $0 because the first $10,000 of liability (about $10M of Illinois-allocated paid-in capital) is exempt.

jurisdictions.name: Chicago, IL

receiptsTaxes.name: No Chicago gross receipts or business income tax
receiptsTaxes.base: n/a
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Chicago has no gross receipts, income, or BIRT-style tax on software or professional-services companies. Its Personal Property Lease Transaction Tax (PPLTT) is legally owed by the customer (the lessee). Sellers collect and remit it, so it is pass-through and is excluded here (details in otherNotes).

fixedAnnual.name: Limited Business License (BACP)
fixedAnnual.notes: Municipal Code 4-4-020 requires every business operating in Chicago that is not covered by a more specific license to hold a Limited Business License; general offices, software, and consulting fall here. BACP fee notice: $500 per two-year license from 1/1/2026 (was $250). Annualized: $250 per Chicago location. Owed only if the company has a business location in Chicago, not for merely selling to Chicago customers.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: PPLTT (cloud/SaaS 'lease tax'): 15% of the lease or rental price from 1/1/2026, set by the 2026 Revenue Ordinance passed 12/20/2025. It was 11% in 2025 and 9% in 2021-2024. It covers nonpossessory computer leases, meaning SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS used by customers in Chicago. Collection rules: (1) Sellers collect from Chicago customers. (2) Out-of-city sellers have a safe harbor and need not collect while they have under $100,000 of Chicago revenue in the last four quarters and no other significant Chicago contacts. (3) Customers must self-assess if the seller does not collect. (4) Multi-location customers can apportion use with an affidavit. (5) Charges for human-performed services or custom reports/databases are not taxable (Ruling 12). Expense hit for a Chicago-based company: it owes 15% PPLTT as the customer on its own cloud and SaaS spend (AWS, SaaS tools), which belongs in expenses. A 'small new business' exemption is available on application if the company had under $25M of gross receipts the prior year, has operated under 60 months, and holds a business license; it covers the company as lessor, lessee, or both. Head tax: none. The mayor's proposed 2026 'Community Safety Surcharge' ($21/employee/month at 100+ employees, later revised to $33 at 500+) was rejected. It does not appear in the official list of 2026 tax changes, and press reports say 26 aldermen oppose any 2027 head tax. The 2027 budget had not been adopted as of this research. Also not relevant to typical B2B SaaS: the 9% amusement tax on streaming and online games, and the new 2026 social media amusement tax ($0.50 per Chicago user per month above 100,000).

calculatorOption.label: Chicago
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Chicago receipts tax; $250/yr Limited Business License ($500 per 2-year term) if you have a Chicago office; the 15% cloud lease tax is collected from Chicago customers (pass-through), but it also applies to your own cloud/SaaS spend.

jurisdictions.name: Cook County, IL

fixedAnnual.name: General Business License (unincorporated Cook County only)
fixedAnnual.notes: $40 per 2-year period (current term 3/1/2025-2/28/2027). Required only for businesses with a fixed place of business in unincorporated Cook County. Businesses inside Chicago or other incorporated municipalities do not need it, so a typical startup pays $0.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Cook County's home-rule taxes include amusement, hotel, liquor, tobacco, fuel, firearm, gambling machine, parking, a 1% use tax on titled property, and a home-rule retailers' occupation tax on tangible goods. None is a receipts tax on software or professional services, and the county has no cloud or SaaS lease tax. The county tax list was read from the official Department of Revenue page. The absence of a SaaS tax is inferred from that list; I did not read each ordinance in full.

calculatorOption.label: Cook County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Cook County receipts tax or cloud tax on software/services; the $40 per 2-year business license applies only in unincorporated areas.

jurisdictions.name: Indiana
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026 (corporate AGI rate 4.9% for 2025 per IT-20 booklet, no change in 2026 legislative synopsis; SOS entity report fees current as of Oct 2026; business personal property threshold for 2026+ assessment dates)

fixedAnnual.name: Business Entity Report (Secretary of State), for-profit corporation
fixedAnnual.notes: Filed every other year (biennial) in the anniversary month of the entity's registration in Indiana. Fee is $31 online via INBiz or $50 by mail, so $15.50/yr annualized if filed online ($25/yr by mail). Not filing leads to administrative dissolution or revocation after about five months of delinquency. The one-time foreign corporation Certificate of Authority fee is $105 online / $125 by mail. That figure comes from secondary sources (Harbor Compliance and similar), I did not see it on an official page, and it is not recurring.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate Adjusted Gross Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 4.9% of Indiana-apportioned adjusted gross income (DOR tax-types page and 2025 IT-20 booklet). Apportionment uses a single receipts factor. Receipts from services and intangibles are market-sourced: they count as Indiana receipts if the benefit is received or consumed in Indiana. There is no minimum tax and no franchise tax, so the amount is $0 at a loss. Quarterly estimates are required only if quarterly liability exceeds $2,500. An IT-20 return is still due each year once the company has Indiana nexus.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Indiana has NO gross receipts tax, franchise/capital stock tax, or minimum tax. The utility receipts tax applied only to utilities and was repealed effective July 1, 2022 (HEA 1002-2022). SALES TAX: the state rate is 7%, but remotely accessed SaaS (cloud software that is not downloaded) is NOT a retail transaction and is not subject to Indiana sales/use tax (Sales Tax Information Bulletin #8, effective Jan 1, 2023). Prewritten software that is downloaded or delivered electronically IS taxable. Professional services are generally not taxable. PAYROLL (already in expenses): employers withhold the state individual income tax (2.95% for 2026) plus county local income tax based on the employee's county of residence (e.g., Marion County 2.02% per Departmental Notice #1, effective Oct 1, 2026). These are employee taxes the employer only withholds, not an employer cost. State unemployment insurance is an employer cost, but I did not verify its rate this session. Under SEA 1-2025, municipalities may adopt their own local income tax on individuals starting in 2028. That tax is also on individuals, not corporations. BUSINESS PERSONAL PROPERTY TAX: from the 2026 assessment date onward, business personal property is exempt if its total acquisition cost in a county is under $2,000,000 (it was $80,000 for the 2025 and earlier assessment dates). The company must claim the exemption once on Form 102/103. A typical SaaS startup with laptops and furniture therefore pays $0 (DLGF memo, June 12, 2025). LOCAL: Indiana cities and counties have no power to impose a tax unless a statute expressly grants it, and may not charge license fees above administrative cost (IC 36-1-3-8). No statute authorizes a local gross receipts or general business tax, so no Indiana city has one that applies to software or services companies.

calculatorOption.label: Indiana
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Indiana tax on receipts; only the $31 biennial business entity report (about $15.50/yr); the 4.9% corporate income tax is $0 before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Indianapolis, IN
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Indianapolis/Marion County has no gross receipts tax, business privilege tax, head tax, or corporate income tax. Indiana local units cannot impose a tax without an express statutory grant (IC 36-1-3-8). The Marion County taxes DOR administers are a 10% admissions tax limited to specific venues, a 6% supplemental auto rental excise tax, the food and beverage tax, and the innkeeper's tax. None of these applies to a SaaS or professional-services company's revenue. The Department of Business and Neighborhood Services licenses only specific regulated activities (contractors, food establishments, transient merchants, vendor carts, and similar). Several secondary sources report there is no general business license an office-based software company must buy. I could not read the indy.gov license pages directly (they render only with JavaScript), so that point comes from secondary sources plus the statute. PAYROLL (already in expenses): Marion County local income tax is 2.02% for employees who live in Marion County (Departmental Notice #1, Oct 1, 2026). The employer withholds it; it is not an employer cost. A municipal individual income tax becomes possible from 2028 under SEA 1-2025. No other Indiana city has a notable local receipts or business tax, because state law does not authorize one.

calculatorOption.label: Indianapolis
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Indianapolis has no tax on receipts and no general business license fee for software or services companies.

jurisdictions.name: Iowa
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026. Corporate rates are the same for tax years 2024 through 2027 (IDR Orders 2025-02 and 2026-01). Secretary of State fees are from the 2026 Iowa Code.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State biennial report (foreign profit corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $60 every even-numbered year, filed Jan 1 to Apr 1. Sources: Iowa Code 490.122(1)(ad) ('Biennial report ... $60') and 490.1621(4), plus the SOS fee page ('Profit Corporations: Every Even numbered year ... The filing fee is $60'). The first report is due in the first even-numbered year after the calendar year you registered. $30/yr is that fee averaged over two years. The foreign registration statement is a one-time $100 (Iowa Code 490.122(1)(v)) and is not counted here. There is no state minimum tax, franchise tax or annual business license for a general C corporation.

profitTaxes.name: Iowa corporate income tax, first $100,000 of Iowa taxable income
profitTaxes.notes: 5.5% on the first $100,000 for tax years 2024 through 2027. Iowa DOR Order 2025-02 kept the 2026 rates because FY2025 net corporate receipts were about $621M, under the $700M trigger. Order 2026-01 (Oct 5, 2026) keeps the same rates for 2027. Income is apportioned by a single receipts factor (the 'Business Activity Ratio', Schedule E of IA 1120). Service receipts are sourced under Iowa Admin. Code r. 701-503.6. The corporate alternative minimum tax was repealed for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2021, and the 2025 IA 1120 instructions have no minimum tax. Tax is zero before profit.

profitTaxes.name: Iowa corporate income tax, income over $100,000
profitTaxes.notes: 7.1% on Iowa taxable income over $100,000, for 2024 through 2027. The 2025 IA 1120 instructions describe the calculation as 7.1% minus $1,600 when income is over $100k. Rates fall further only if net corporate receipts in a fiscal year exceed $700M, with a 5.5% floor. Informational only.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Iowa has no gross receipts, margin or capital-stock tax. Iowa's 'franchise tax' (IA 1120F) applies only to banks, savings and loans, trust companies and similar financial institutions, not to a software company. Sales tax (pass-through, not counted): SaaS is a taxable enumerated service in Iowa at 6% state tax plus 1% local option sales tax where adopted. Custom software has been taxed like prewritten software since 2019. Sales of SaaS, specified digital products and prewritten software to a for-profit 'commercial enterprise' that uses them exclusively (non-commercial use only de minimis) are exempt, so B2B SaaS is often exempt and B2C SaaS is taxable. Remote sellers must collect once their gross Iowa revenue (including exempt sales) is $100,000 or more in the current or prior calendar year. Payroll (already in expenses): Iowa income tax withholding for employees working in Iowa and Iowa unemployment insurance contributions; neither is in this calculation. Local taxes: Iowa cities and counties cannot levy any tax unless a state statute authorizes it (Iowa Code 364.3(4) and 331.301(7)). The local income surtaxes Iowa authorizes (school-district instructional support surtax, Iowa Code 257.21; county EMS surtax, Iowa Code 422D.2) fall only on the state individual income tax of residents, not on corporations. I found no Iowa city or county with a receipts or business-privilege tax.

calculatorOption.label: Iowa
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Iowa receipts or minimum tax; a corporation registered in Iowa pays a $60 biennial report every even year (about $30/yr).

jurisdictions.name: Des Moines, IA
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Des Moines has no city income tax, no gross receipts tax and no general business license for an office-based software or services company. The City Clerk issues only activity-specific licenses: alcohol, tobacco, transient merchant, mobile food, peddler, pawn, theater, salvage, solid-waste hauler and similar. Under Iowa Code 364.3(4) the city cannot levy a tax that state law does not authorize. One secondary-source search snippet claimed a Des Moines code section requires every business to get a city license. I could not open the municipal code (Municode would not load) to check, and the City Clerk's own licensing page lists no such license. Sales tax (pass-through): Des Moines voters approved a 1% local option sales tax effective July 1, 2019, so the combined rate is 7% (6% state + 1%) on taxable sales such as non-exempt SaaS. Utility franchise fees and property tax on leased space reach a tenant only through bills and rent.

calculatorOption.label: Des Moines
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Des Moines levies no receipts tax, income tax or general business license; only the 1% local option sales tax, which is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Cedar Rapids, IA
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Checked because it is Iowa's second-largest city. The city's licensing page says: 'The City of Cedar Rapids does not issue general business licenses.' Its licenses cover only alcohol and tobacco, transportation, vendors and solicitors, pawnbrokers, auctioneers and similar activities. There is no city receipts or income tax (Iowa Code 364.3(4)). I did not verify the local option sales tax rate there, and it is pass-through in any case.

calculatorOption.label: Cedar Rapids
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Cedar Rapids has no receipts tax and no general business license.

jurisdictions.name: Davenport, IA
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Checked because Davenport is often described in secondary sources as having a 'general business license.' The city's own business-license page and its Title 5 license manual list only specific activities: alarms, auctioneers, signs, amusements, live entertainment, mobile food, pawn and secondhand dealers, taxis, tree trimmers, massage, and retail or transient merchants. The retail license ($75 for the first 3,999 sq ft) applies only to sellers of tangible personal property to the ultimate consumer. It does not reach SaaS or professional services. There is no city receipts or income tax (Iowa Code 364.3(4)). Confidence is medium because the license manual carries no date and I could not open the municipal code itself (ecode360 returned 403).

calculatorOption.label: Davenport
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Davenport has no receipts tax; its retail license covers only sellers of physical goods, not SaaS or services.

jurisdictions.name: Kansas
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2025. Corporate rates stay the same for 2026 per KDOR Notice 25-06. Secretary of State fees are from forms revised 3/2/26 (FA) and 7/22/26 (IFP).

fixedAnnual.name: Biennial Information Report, for-profit corporation (form IFP, covers foreign corporations under K.S.A. 17-7505)
fixedAnnual.notes: $90 per report filed online ($110 on paper), per IFP instructions Rev. 7/22/26. Due by April 15 every two years: even-year filers file in even years, odd-year filers in odd years. Since L. 2024 ch. 45 (HB 2660) it replaced the old annual report, so it works out to about $45/yr online or $55/yr on paper. The statute sets $80 plus a per-tax-period amount set by SOS regulation, and the SOS cut fees in a May 2026 regulation update. Not included here: the one-time $115 Foreign Application (FA, paper only) and the $85 penalty for late or forfeited reports.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax, normal tax
profitTaxes.notes: 3.5% of Kansas taxable income. The APEX trigger (Notice 23-10) cut it from 4% starting with TY2024, and the 2025 K-120 instructions use 3.5%. KDOR Notice 25-06 (Oct 2, 2025) says the SB 269 revenue trigger was not met, so there is no reduction for TY2026. Kansas has no minimum tax, so the liability is $0 at a loss, though a K-120 return is still required.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax, surtax
profitTaxes.notes: 3% of Kansas taxable income above $50,000, for a combined top rate of 6.5%. Through TY2026, income is apportioned with an equally weighted three-factor formula (property, payroll, sales). HB 2231 (2025) moves to a single sales factor with market-based sourcing for tax years starting on or after Jan 1, 2027. Kansas franchise tax: none for TY2011 and later (KDOR franchise tax page).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Kansas has no state gross receipts tax, no franchise or capital tax (expired after TY2010), and no minimum tax. Privilege tax applies only to banks, savings and loans, and trust companies. Sales tax: KDOR EDU-71R says remote access to software where the customer has no control or possession (SaaS/ASP) is not a taxable lease, so SaaS is not subject to Kansas sales tax. Prewritten (canned) software is taxable even when delivered electronically, and custom software is not. Kansas taxes only enumerated services, so typical professional or consulting services are generally not taxable. Remote sellers must collect once Kansas gross receipts exceed $100,000 in the current or prior calendar year (Notice 21-17), but these are pass-through taxes and not counted here. Payroll costs (Kansas withholding and state unemployment insurance) belong in expenses. Kansas has no local payroll or earnings taxes because K.S.A. 12-140 bars cities from taxing income. Note that Kansas City, Missouri does have a 1% earnings tax on wages and business net profits, but that is Missouri, not KCK. Local intangibles tax (K.S.A. 12-1,101 et seq., Form 200): some mostly rural counties and townships tax gross interest and dividend earnings of corporations whose Kansas principal office is in their jurisdiction. Riley County (Manhattan) charges 0.75%, and the 2024 Form 200 rate list does not include Sedgwick, Wyandotte or Johnson counties. This could tax interest on a startup's cash if it is headquartered in one of those places, but it is not a tax on revenue. Some Johnson County suburbs charge small flat occupation or business license taxes if you have premises there. Lenexa's 2026 fee schedule lists $58/yr for 'Office Space (no warehouse)'. Leawood requires an occupation license (amount not verified; its site blocked fetches). Overland Park repealed its business and occupations tax.

calculatorOption.label: Kansas
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Kansas has no receipts or franchise tax; the only fixed cost is the $90 biennial information report filed online, about $45/yr.

jurisdictions.name: Kansas City, KS (Unified Government of Wyandotte County/KCK)
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 occupation tax year. The 2026 amount is a CPI-W estimate.

fixedAnnual.name: Occupation tax: NAICS 541500-541519 computer system design (also 514200-514210 computer programming/data processing and 541610-541690 management consulting)
fixedAnnual.notes: UG Code §34-77 sets $136 for these classes as the 2012 base amount. §34-72 indexes it every Jan 1 by CPI-W for the 12 months ending the prior August. The UG posts 2025 fees of $188 for locksmiths and landscaping, which share the same $136 base, and BLS CPI-W Aug 2024 / Aug 2011 = 308.640/223.326 gives the same $188. The 2026 amount works out to about $193 (CPI-W Aug 2025 = 317.306) but is not posted. Flat per place of business, not per employee. The license administrator assigns the NAICS class and uses the highest-tax class if several fit. Due Jan 1, prorated by quarter for new businesses, with a 10% late penalty. A receipt is issued only after the commercial personal property statement is filed with the county assessor.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: KCK has no earnings or income tax because K.S.A. 12-140 prohibits city income taxes. That is unlike Kansas City, Missouri, which has a 1% earnings tax on wages and business net profits. KCK has no gross receipts tax. The UG occupation tax page says businesses not located in KCK but 'engaged in business activities in KCK' must register and pay for work done in the city. Whether purely remote SaaS sales to KCK customers count as engaging in business there is unclear and was not confirmed. The likely trigger is an office, staff or on-site services in KCK. A business with no fixed place of business in the city and no specific class pays a $250 2012 base (§34-76), about $345 for 2025 at the same CPI factor. City and county retail sales taxes follow the Kansas rules, so SaaS is not taxed and in any case these are pass-through. No local payroll taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Kansas City, KS
calculatorOption.assumptionText: KCK has no receipts or earnings tax; a software company with an office or staff in KCK pays a flat occupation tax of about $188/yr (2025, CPI-indexed, about $193 in 2026).

jurisdictions.name: Wichita, KS
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Code of Ordinances codified through Ord. 52-907, March 10, 2026)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Wichita has no gross receipts tax, no earnings tax (barred by K.S.A. 12-140) and no general business license. Under Code §3.04.010 an occupation or license tax applies only to businesses 'specified in this title' (Title 3), such as adult businesses, mobile food vendors, taxis, wreckers and private security. Software and professional services are not listed. A business run from a home needs a home occupation license at $35/yr (§3.96.010); an office-based company owes nothing. Sedgwick County and city sales taxes follow Kansas rules, so SaaS is not taxed and these are pass-through anyway. No local payroll taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Wichita
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Wichita has no receipts tax, earnings tax or general business license for software or services companies.

jurisdictions.name: Overland Park, KS
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Checked because it is Kansas's second-largest city and the Kansas City area's main office and tech hub. The official municipal code table of contents lists Chapter 5.04 'Business and Occupations Tax' as repealed. The city's business-license page says it licenses only certain businesses (massage, pawnbrokers, precious metal dealers, taxis and limos, transient merchants) and does not license home-based businesses. No earnings tax (K.S.A. 12-140), no receipts tax and no local payroll tax. Neighboring Lenexa charges $58/yr for 'Office Space (no warehouse)' (2026 fee schedule), and Leawood requires an occupation license whose amount was not verified. Both are small flat fees owed only if you have premises there.

calculatorOption.label: Overland Park
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Overland Park has no receipts tax and has repealed its business occupation tax.

jurisdictions.name: Kentucky
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026. KRS 141.0401 text is the version effective July 15, 2026. LLET rates have been unchanged since 2007, and the 5% corporate income tax rate has applied since 2018.

receiptsTaxes.name: Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET), KRS 141.0401
receiptsTaxes.base: Kentucky gross receipts, which is the Kentucky numerator of the sales factor under KRS 141.120. Sourcing is market-based: service receipts go to Kentucky to the extent the service is delivered to a location in Kentucky, and licensed or leased intangibles go to Kentucky to the extent they are used there.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross receipts from all sources (the denominator of the sales factor), aggregated across the affiliated group. Receipts assigned to states where the company is not taxable are excluded from that denominator under KRS 141.120(11)(c).
receiptsTaxes.notes:
The LLET is the lesser of two computations: 0.095% of Kentucky gross receipts, or 0.75% of Kentucky gross profits.
