For any activity other than manufacturing, producing, or selling a tangible product, the statute allows no cost of goods sold (KRS 141.0401(1)(d)3). So for SaaS and services, gross profits equal gross receipts, and the 0.095% receipts computation is always the lesser one.

Tiers by all-source receipts:
- $3M or less: $175 flat.
- Over $3M and under $6M: 0.095% x KY gross receipts, minus $2,850 x (6M - KY gross receipts)/3M, but never less than $175. Because of this reduction, the tax stays at $175 unless Kentucky receipts exceed about $3.09M, which means more than half of revenue for a company in this band.
- $6M or more: 0.095% x KY gross receipts.

The $175 minimum applies regardless of credits. Any LLET above $175 becomes a nonrefundable credit against the 5% corporate income tax (KRS 141.0401(3)), so once profitable a company effectively pays the greater of the income tax or the LLET. Before profit, the LLET is a real cost.

The LLET is reported on Form 720, due the 15th day of the 4th month after year-end.

2026 HB 451 would have exempted entities with under $100k of Kentucky gross receipts from the LLET starting in 2027. Its last action was referral to committee on January 29, 2026, and the codified text effective July 15, 2026 does not contain the exemption, so the exemption is not law.

fixedAnnual.name: LLET minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: Every corporation doing business in Kentucky owes this, including a pre-revenue one. It acts as a floor, not an add-on: the actual tax is the greater of $175 or the receipts-based amount.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report
fixedAnnual.notes: The $15 fee is the same for domestic and foreign corporations. The report is due between January 1 and June 30. A foreign corporation that fails to file has its certificate of authority revoked.

profitTaxes.name: Corporation income tax (KRS 141.040)
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 5% for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2018. The LLET above $175 is credited against it.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Sales tax (pass-through): Since January 1, 2023, Kentucky's 6% sales and use tax applies to prewritten computer software access services (SaaS), defined in KRS 139.010(34) and listed in KRS 139.200. Prewritten software is taxable. The Department of Revenue's Winter 2025/2026 Sales Tax Facts says AI-adaptive SaaS is still prewritten and taxable, while custom software is exempt. HB 8 (2022) also made many business services taxable. This tax is collected from customers and is not counted here.

Payroll (already in expenses): State income tax withholding is borne by employees, and state unemployment insurance is an employer cost. Local occupational license taxes on wages are withheld from employees. Rates confirmed this session:
- Louisville: 2.2% for residents, 1.45% for non-residents
- Lexington: 2.25%
- Paducah: 2.0%
- Covington: 2.45%
- Owensboro: 1.78%
- Bowling Green: 2.0% since 2024

No capital-based franchise tax: Kentucky's old corporation license tax was repealed (secondary sources say for tax years ending on or after December 31, 2005; I did not read the official repeal text).

Local sourcing: About 39 Kentucky cities tax gross receipts, about 89 tax net profits, and 170 tax payroll (KLC/KACo, October 2025). Under KRS 67.753, local net-profit and gross-receipts taxes apportion service revenue by where the work is performed (time spent), not by where customers are. Local receipts taxes therefore only matter in cities where the team actually works.

Net-profit cities often set small minimums for businesses located there:
- Covington: $100
- Owensboro: $75
- Lexington: $100
- Bowling Green: a $30 minimum appears only on a 2014 archived page; its current minimum was not confirmed.

calculatorOption.label: Kentucky
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Kentucky: $175 LLET minimum plus $15 annual report; 0.095% of Kentucky-sourced receipts once total receipts reach $6M (the $3M–$6M phase-in leaves a nationally-selling company at the $175 minimum); above $6M this overstates by up to $175 because the minimum is really a floor.

jurisdictions.name: Louisville, KY (Louisville/Jefferson County Metro)
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Louisville Metro Revenue Commission regulations, 2026 edition)

fixedAnnual.name: Occupational license tax registration
fixedAnnual.notes: Every business entity and employer must register for an account number before starting business. The 2026 regulations set no registration fee and no minimum tax.

profitTaxes.name: Occupational license tax on net profit (Metro 1.25% + TARC transit 0.20% + school boards 0.75%)
profitTaxes.notes: Applies to Louisville-apportioned net profit. Apportionment follows KRS 67.753: the average of the payroll and sales factors, with service sales sourced by time spent performing the work. Nothing is due before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Payroll (already in expenses): The wage tax is 2.2% for resident employees and 1.45% for non-residents (non-residents do not pay the 0.75% school tax). It is withheld from employees. Employers must withhold for remote employees working in Louisville even if the employer has no nexus there. The 2026 regulations also set nexus rules: remote employees create nexus at 10% or more of staff or over $75k of compensation, and digital-property sales create nexus at over $25k or 200 transactions.

Suburban cities: Some cities inside Jefferson County levy their own business license taxes. St. Matthews uses a gross-receipts license tax: a $25 first-year filing fee, renewals based on gross receipts, and a 50% discount if paid by April 30. Its rate schedule is not published on its web page. It applies only to businesses located in, or coming into, St. Matthews to conduct work.

calculatorOption.label: Louisville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Louisville taxes net profit (2.2%) and wages only; no receipts tax or minimum, so nothing before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Lexington, KY (Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government)

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum occupational license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: A $100 initial license fee is due at registration, and a $100 annual minimum is due with the net profits return. The minimum is credited against the net-profits license fee but never creates a refund, so a pre-profit corporation pays $100 a year. The exemption for gross receipts of $4,400 or less covers only individuals and sole proprietorships, not corporations.

profitTaxes.name: LFUCG net profits license fee
profitTaxes.notes: Applies to net profits from activities in Fayette County, apportioned under KRS 67.753.

profitTaxes.name: Fayette County Public Schools occupational license tax
profitTaxes.notes: Reported in news sources (not confirmed on an official page this session): 0.5% on wages and business net profits, unchanged since 1985. In 2025 the board voted to raise it to 0.75%, then dropped the increase after the Attorney General found the notice procedure unlawful. 2026 SB 76 would raise the population threshold for such increases; its final status was not checked.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (already in expenses): LFUCG's 2.25% on compensation earned in Fayette County is withheld from employees, and FCPS reportedly levies 0.5% on wages. The minimum fee applies only to companies engaged in business in Fayette County, such as through an office or employees. Customers in Lexington alone do not produce Lexington-apportioned receipts under KRS 67.753.

calculatorOption.label: Lexington
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Lexington: $100 minimum occupational license fee if you operate in Fayette County; the 2.25% net-profits fee is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Paducah, KY
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year. Ordinance 2025-09-8855 sets the Year 1 (2026) threshold at $5.13M; the tax is measured on the prior year's receipts.

receiptsTaxes.name: Gross receipts license tax (Code Ch. 106 Art. III), Schedule D
receiptsTaxes.base: Taxable gross receipts of the Paducah business location, apportioned under Sec. 106-67 (which mirrors KRS 67.753). With payroll and sales in several districts, the share is (payroll factor + sales factor)/2. For services, the sales factor is time spent performing the work in Paducah divided by total time. Customer location does not matter, so a company with no one working in Paducah has no Paducah receipts.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross receipts from a business located in Paducah (no license or tax if under $600 a year)
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Classification: Sec. 106-143 puts computer services and information on Schedule D, as do unenumerated personal services and the general classification. Licensed professions such as accountants, attorneys, and engineers are on Schedule E (0.45%).

Rate tiers: 0.30% applies up to the phased-in threshold and 0.005% applies above it. The threshold is $5,130,000 in 2026, $6.76M in 2027, $8.39M in 2028, $10.02M in 2029, and $11.65M in 2030, with CPI-U South adjustments after that.

Minimum: $50 per classification, credited against the tax.

Filing: Tax for a license year is measured on the prior year's receipts and is due April 15 (or the 15th day of the 4th month after a fiscal year-end), with the federal return attached. Sales tax, returns, and uncollectibles are deductible.

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum annual license tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Raised from $35 to $50 by the September 2, 2025 ordinance. It is credited against the receipts tax, so the actual tax is the greater of $50 or 0.30% of receipts. A pre-revenue company pays $50.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (already in expenses): Paducah's 2.0% payroll occupational license fee is withheld from employees' wages earned in the city. McCracken County levies its own occupational license tax, which I did not research. A separate license is required for each location, and for each classification taxed at a different rate.

calculatorOption.label: Paducah
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Paducah: 0.30% of receipts apportioned by where the work is done (assumes the whole team is in Paducah; zero if no one works there), with a $50 minimum shown as an add-on; the rate drops to 0.005% above $5.13M (2026).

jurisdictions.name: Florence, KY
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 renewal (measured on the 2025 federal return)

receiptsTaxes.name: Occupational license tax on gross receipts
receiptsTaxes.base: Total receipts or sales less returns and allowances, plus gross rents, from the last federal return (Form 1120 line 1c plus line 6), times the Florence allocation percentage from Schedule A. The ordinance section on apportionment (110.13) was blocked and not read. It is likely the KRS 67.753 method, where services are sourced by time spent in the city.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: 0.1% of gross receipts derived in Florence, with a $40 minimum and a $10,000 maximum per year. A new business pays on estimated first-year receipts and trues up after its first federal return. Each additional Florence location needs a $25 duplicate license.

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum license tax
fixedAnnual.notes: This is a floor: the actual tax is the greater of $40 or 0.1% of Florence receipts, capped at $10,000.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Only applies if the company operates in Florence. Boone County levies its own occupational taxes on payroll and net profits, which I did not research. Florence's payroll tax was not checked; any wage tax would already be in expenses.

calculatorOption.label: Florence
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Florence: 0.1% of receipts apportioned to Florence (assumes the team works there), $40 minimum, capped at $10,000 a year.

jurisdictions.name: Covington, KY
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current (city finance page as viewed in 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum net profits license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: The fee is the greater of 2.5% of net profits or $100, so a pre-profit business located in Covington pays $100. The city also lists a $50 fee due with the license application; whether that recurs yearly was not confirmed, so it is excluded here.

profitTaxes.name: Net profits occupational license fee
profitTaxes.notes: Applies to net profits from business conducted in the city.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (already in expenses): Covington taxes all compensation paid to employees at 2.45%. Kenton County levies its own occupational taxes, which I did not research.

calculatorOption.label: Covington
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Covington: $100 minimum net-profits license fee if you operate there; the 2.5% net-profits rate is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Owensboro, KY
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current (city page as viewed in 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum occupational license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: The fee is the greater of $75 or 1.78% of net profits, and the $75 is due at registration.

profitTaxes.name: Net profit license fee
profitTaxes.notes: Applies to net profits from activity in the city.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (already in expenses): Owensboro's 1.78% fee is withheld from employees' wages for work done in the city. It only applies if the company operates in Owensboro.

calculatorOption.label: Owensboro
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Owensboro: $75 minimum occupational license fee if you operate there; 1.78% of net profit is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Louisiana
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (franchise tax repealed for periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026; annual report fee rose to $35 on Oct 1, 2026; 5.5% flat corporate income tax applies from tax year 2025)

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $35 from Oct 1, 2026 under Act 921 of the 2026 Regular Session; it was $30 before that. Paying by credit card adds a $5 statutory convenience fee. Due each year by the registration anniversary date. Qualifying as a foreign corporation (Application for Certificate of Authority) is a one-time $155 (was $150).

fixedAnnual.name: Corporation franchise tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Repealed for franchise tax periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026 (Act 6 / HB 3, 2024 Third Extraordinary Session). The 2025 return is now CIT-620, income tax only. Earlier periods: the 2025 franchise period, filed on the 2024 CIFT-620, was $2.75 per $1,000 of Louisiana-apportioned taxable capital above $300,000, with no minimum. A new entity paid a flat $110 initial tax (R-6906A). A startup with little Louisiana apportionment owed $0 apart from that $110.

profitTaxes.name: Corporation income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 5.5% for tax periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025, with a corporate standard deduction of up to $20,000. Service businesses apportion by a single ratio of Louisiana gross receipts, sourced by market (where the service is delivered). A foreign corporation doing business in Louisiana must file CIT-620 even when no tax is due. There is no minimum income tax, so the amount is $0 before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
There is no state-level gross receipts or margin tax. Since the franchise tax repeal, a pre-profit foreign C corp pays the state only the $35 annual report fee.

Sales tax: since Jan 1, 2025, 'prewritten computer software access services' (SaaS; LDR lists Microsoft 365, Zoom, Salesforce, Slack as examples) and 'information services' are taxable at the state rate of 5% (5% runs through 12/31/2029) plus local rates. These are pass-through taxes collected from customers. LDR says consulting on hardware/software, contract programming built for a client's environment, and proprietary client-specific reports are not information services, so professional services are generally not taxable. A remote seller with no physical presence registers with the Louisiana Sales and Use Tax Commission for Remote Sellers once Louisiana sales exceed $100,000. The Commission's FAQ still lists an older alternative test of 200 transactions; secondary sources say that test was repealed effective Aug 1, 2023.

Payroll (already counted in expenses): individual income tax withholding is a flat 3% from 2025. The state unemployment insurance wage base is $7,000 for 2026 (LWC). Louisiana has no local payroll or earnings taxes.

Local taxes: every parish and municipality may levy an occupational license tax (R.S. 47:341 et seq.) on businesses with a place of business there. It is set by gross-receipts brackets, roughly 0.1-0.12%, with a $50 minimum and caps of $6,200 for retail/service and $2,000 for professionals. Shreveport's published schedule matches New Orleans and Baton Rouge: retail/service $50-$6,200, professionals $50-$2,000. No Louisiana city has a distinct receipts tax beyond this. A company with no Louisiana location does not owe it.

Parishes also levy ad valorem tax on business movable property such as furniture and computers, reported on the LAT-5 to the parish assessor. I did not research its rates.

Caveat: the Legislature's statute site (legis.la.gov) was unreachable from this environment, so statutes were read only through LDR, SOS and city documents that cite them.

calculatorOption.label: Louisiana
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $35 Louisiana annual report for a foreign corporation (from Oct 1, 2026); corporation franchise tax repealed from 2026; no state receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: New Orleans, LA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (City Code ch. 150 art. VII, codified through Supp. 117, Aug 2026; Bureau of Revenue tables)

receiptsTaxes.name: Occupational license tax (Table 1: retail dealers in merchandise, services and rentals)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the New Orleans place of business from the previous calendar year. Receipts delivered anywhere in Louisiana count toward the New Orleans location (Sec. 150-972(b)). Form 8030 allows a deduction for 'sales shipped/delivered outside Louisiana', so the base is roughly Louisiana-delivered receipts.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (a $50 minimum applies below $50,000 of taxable receipts)
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Tiered flat amounts: under $50k: $50; $50-75k: $60; $75-100k: $90; $100-150k: $120; $150-200k: $180; $200-250k: $250; $250-300k: $300; $300-400k: $360; $400-500k: $500; $500-600k: $650; $600-750k: $800; $750k-1M: $900; $1-1.5M: $1,200; then +$600 per $500k up to $5.4k at $4.5-5M; $5-5.5M: $6,000; $5.5M and up: $6,200 (cap). That works out to roughly 0.08-0.13% of receipts, about 0.12% at the top of each bracket.

Table 1 (Sec. 150-963) expressly covers 'service businesses' and businesses 'leasing, renting, or licensing the use of movable property', which is where SaaS most likely falls. A company whose receipts are mainly professional fees falls under Sec. 150-969(j) instead: 0.10% of gross receipts, $50 minimum, $2,000 maximum. The class is chosen by the majority of receipts.

Uncertain: whether SaaS or service receipts from out-of-state customers qualify as 'delivered outside Louisiana'. If they don't, the base is all receipts of the location, still capped at $6,200.

After one full calendar year, Table 1 tax is $0 if prior-year receipts were under $2,500 (Sec. 150-963(c)).

New businesses pay the $50 minimum as a tentative tax at commencement ($25 if starting on or after July 1), then within 40 days true it up using the first 30 days of receipts annualized. Renewal is due Jan 1 and delinquent after the last day of February (5% per month penalty, max 25%).

fixedAnnual.name: Occupational license tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: Minimum annual license for Table 1 and for professionals. Owed only with a place of business in New Orleans. Can be $0 after the first full year if prior-year receipts were under $2,500. A new license in the French Quarter adds one-time Vieux Carré Commission fees of $25 + $50.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Owed only if the company has a fixed place of business in New Orleans (Orleans Parish). A company selling into New Orleans from elsewhere owes no occupational license tax here.

No city income or payroll tax.

SaaS ('prewritten computer software access') is subject to state 5% plus Orleans Parish local sales tax, collected from customers (pass-through).

The parish assessor levies ad valorem tax on business furniture and equipment (LAT-5 return); I did not research its rates.

Rates are high confidence (official tables and City Code). The SaaS classification and whether the out-of-state deduction applies to SaaS/service receipts are medium confidence.

calculatorOption.label: New Orleans
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Only with a New Orleans office: occupational license tax of about 0.12% of receipts delivered in Louisiana (out-of-state sales deductible), $50 minimum, $6,200 cap.

jurisdictions.name: Baton Rouge, LA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (Metro Council Ordinance 18733, effective Jan 1, 2023; current brla.gov tables)

receiptsTaxes.name: Occupational license tax (Table 1: retail dealers in merchandise, services and rentals, R.S. 47:354)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the business location in the City of Baton Rouge or unincorporated East Baton Rouge Parish, from the previous calendar year. Deductions are those in R.S. 47:361 and the ordinance. I found no out-of-state-sales deduction in Baton Rouge's published materials, so this conservatively assumes all of the location's receipts count.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (a $50 minimum applies below $50,000 of receipts)
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Ordinance 18733 levies the state-law maximum (R.S. 47:354-359). The brackets match New Orleans Table 1: $50 under $50k, rising about 0.12% per bracket ($1,200 at $1-1.5M; $6,000 at $5-5.5M) to a $6,200 cap at $5.5M and up.

Professionals and 'all other businesses' (R.S. 47:359(J)) pay 0.1% of gross receipts, $50 minimum, $2,000 maximum. Fees paid to outside professionals for like services are excluded. The class is chosen by the majority of receipts.

New businesses pay a $50 minimum ($25 if opening on or after July 1), then the tax is computed from the first 30 days of receipts times the remaining months. Renewal is due Jan 1 and delinquent after the last day of February (5% per 30 days, max 25%; 12% annual interest for taxes due from 2023).

If Baton Rouge does in practice allow a deduction for sales delivered outside Louisiana, as New Orleans does, the share would fall to about Louisiana's share of revenue. I could not verify this.

fixedAnnual.name: Occupational license tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: Minimum annual license, owed only with a place of business in the City of Baton Rouge or unincorporated East Baton Rouge Parish. Baker, Central and Zachary levy their own.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Owed only with a business location in Baton Rouge or unincorporated East Baton Rouge Parish. Remote sales into Baton Rouge alone do not trigger it.

No city income or payroll tax.

SaaS is subject to state 5% plus East Baton Rouge local sales tax, collected from customers (pass-through).

The parish assessor levies ad valorem tax on business furniture and equipment (LAT-5 return); I did not research its rates.

The ordinance is a scanned PDF, which I read page by page. The tables and the professional rate are on the official tables PDF.

calculatorOption.label: Baton Rouge
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Only with a Baton Rouge office: occupational license tax of about 0.12% of all receipts (no out-of-state deduction assumed), $50 minimum, $6,200 cap (the cap is not modeled, so this overstates above $5.5M).

jurisdictions.name: Maine
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 tax year corporate income tax (1120ME instructions revised Dec 2025; rates unchanged since 2018). Secretary of State fees are the current statutory amounts as of October 2026. Sales tax and SaaS rule as of the Dec 2025 MRS Business Guide and Rule 326 (effective Oct 6, 2025).

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report fee, foreign business corporation (Secretary of State)
fixedAnnual.notes: 13-C M.R.S. §123 sets the fee for a foreign business corporation's annual report at $150 (a domestic corporation pays $85). Due June 1 each year, with the first report due the year after authority is granted. A late report costs another $50 on top of the fee, and leaving the penalty unpaid leads to revocation of authority. Registering in Maine also costs a one-time $250 application-for-authority fee, which is not annual. Maine has no minimum franchise tax for ordinary corporations: its franchise tax applies only to financial institutions.

profitTaxes.name: Maine corporate income tax (Form 1120ME)
profitTaxes.notes: Graduated rates on Maine net income under 36 M.R.S. §5200(1-A), unchanged since 2018 and still current for 2025: 3.5% on $0-$350k; $12,250 plus 7.93% on $350k-$1.05M; $67,760 plus 8.33% on $1.05M-$3.5M; $271,845 plus 8.93% above $3.5M. Income is apportioned by a single sales factor. Service receipts are sourced to where the service is received; if that can't be determined, to the customer's ordering office, then the billing office. Receipts from licensing intangibles are sourced to where the property is used. Nexus starts at more than $500k of Maine sales, $250k of Maine property or payroll, or 25% of total property, payroll or sales in Maine. You owe tax only if you have Maine net income, so a loss-making company owes $0. There is no current alternative minimum tax: the 2025 instructions mention only a credit for Maine AMT paid in earlier years. A secondary summary dates the repeal to 2018, which I did not confirm in the statute. This tax is informational only before profitability.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No gross receipts, margin or minimum tax applies to a non-financial C corporation in Maine, so the state's only pre-profit cost is the $150 annual report fee. SALES TAX (pass-through): the rate is 5.5%. Under MRS Rule 326 §3.B (effective Oct 6, 2025, covering leases and rentals from Jan 1, 2025), remotely accessed prewritten software that can't be downloaded is not a taxable product transferred electronically, so access-only SaaS is not taxable. Downloadable or load-and-leave prewritten software is taxable; custom software is not. Professional services are generally not taxable. The Service Provider Tax was repealed on Jan 1, 2026, and its services (telecom, ancillary, digital audio and audiovisual, and others) now fall under the 5.5% sales tax. That does not reach ordinary SaaS, but check if you resell telecom or streaming. Sales tax economic nexus is $100k of Maine sales; this is from recall and was not checked in this session. Out-of-state purchases used in Maine, such as computer hardware, owe 5.5% use tax. PAYROLL (already in expenses): state income tax withholding; unemployment insurance and the Competitive Skills Scholarship Fund contribution (rates not checked here); and Paid Family and Medical Leave contributions, collected since January 2025. PFML is 1% of wages split 0.5%/0.5% for employers with 15 or more employees. For fewer than 15 employees it totals 0.5%, and the employer may withhold all of it from wages. LOCAL TAXES: Maine municipalities levy property tax, not income, sales or gross receipts taxes. Business personal property is taxed locally, but the Business Equipment Tax Exemption (BETE, 36 M.R.S. §691) fully exempts most equipment, such as computers, first taxable on or after Apr 1, 2008. Office furniture and general office lighting are excluded from BETE and stay taxable, though BETR reimbursement may cover them. A 2025 bill (LD 746) would let towns adopt a 2% local option sales tax on lodging by referendum. It is lodging-only and irrelevant here, and I did not verify whether it was enacted. I found no Maine city with a receipts or business-privilege tax on software or services companies.

calculatorOption.label: Maine
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Maine has no gross receipts or minimum franchise tax; a corporation registered there pays a $150/yr foreign-corporation annual report fee.

jurisdictions.name: Portland, ME
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026 (city fiscal year July 2025-June 2026); licensing ordinance text is Chapter 15 as last revised 2016-2017
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Portland has no gross receipts, income or general business-privilege tax, and Maine municipalities have no general authority to levy one. Even a local option sales tax on lodging needed state legislation (LD 746, 2025). Portland has no general business license. Code of Ordinances Chapter 15 and its cross-references license only specific regulated activities: food service, liquor, entertainment, street vendors, transient sellers, pawnbrokers and secondhand dealers, towing, taxis, massage and the like. An office-based SaaS or professional services company needs none of them. I could not render the city's business-licensing web page (it is JavaScript-only and failed TLS verification), so this rests on the ordinance text. Expect one recurring local cost: municipal property tax on business personal property not exempt under BETE, chiefly office furniture and general office lighting, assessed as of April 1. On a few thousand dollars of furniture it is small. The FY2026 Portland mill rate is reported at $11.98 per $1,000 after a revaluation; that figure comes from secondary press (Mainebiz) that I could not open, not from the city assessor. Leased office space carries property tax through rent. Payroll taxes are state-level only; see Maine.

calculatorOption.label: Portland, ME
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Portland, ME has no receipts tax and no general business license; its only local tax is property tax on non-exempt business property such as office furniture.

jurisdictions.name: Maryland
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 annual report (SDAT Form 1); 2025 corporate income tax booklet, rate unchanged for 2026

fixedAnnual.name: SDAT Annual Report filing fee (Form 1, foreign stock corporation, prefix F)
fixedAnnual.notes: The 2026 Form 1 lists $300 for a domestic or foreign stock corporation. It is due April 15. Per SDAT instructions (seen as a search excerpt), the fee is owed whether or not the entity owns property, earns income, or does business in Maryland. A MarylandSaves waiver checkbox can remove the fee. Late filing adds a penalty.

profitTaxes.name: Maryland corporation income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 8.25% of Maryland taxable income. There is no minimum tax: the 2025 booklet shows a flat rate with no minimum, so nothing is owed before profit. Apportionment is a single receipts factor for tax years after 2021, and service receipts are sourced to customers in Maryland (COMAR 03.04.03.08D). HB 690 (2026), which would cut the rate to 6.25% by 2030, was a minority-party bill. I did not confirm whether it passed, and the rate is assumed to stay at 8.25%.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Sales and use tax is passed through to customers and is not counted. Since July 1, 2025, Maryland charges 3% on data/IT services (NAICS 518, 519, 5415, including custom programming and software consulting) and on software publishing (NAICS 5132). Per Technical Bulletin 56, SaaS is taxed at 3% when sold for use in an enterprise computer system and at 6% (digital product) when sold solely for individual use. There is no business-use exemption, and the resale exemption is narrow. The startup also pays this 3% on IT/SaaS it buys for use in Maryland, which belongs in expenses.

The Digital Advertising Gross Revenues Tax (2.5%-10%) applies only above $100M of global revenue and $1M of Maryland digital-ad revenue, so it is irrelevant here.

Business personal property tax is a local tax (see Baltimore and Montgomery). It is exempt if all Maryland personal property had a total original cost under $20,000. SB 137 (2026) would let SDAT collect returns from exempt filers again.

The trader's license (Bus. Reg. Title 17) covers sellers of goods and does not appear to apply to SaaS. This is based on reading the scope, not on a confirmation from the State License Bureau.

Payroll (belongs in expenses): state and county income tax withholding on employees, and state UI. FAMLI is 0.90% of covered wages split 0.45%/0.45%, and employers with 14 or fewer employees owe no employer share. Contributions are reported to start January 1, 2027; I saw this only in a Maryland Labor search excerpt, and the date has been delayed before.

Other Maryland localities: per the DLS overview of local taxing authority, local revenue comes from property, individual income, recordation/transfer, hotel, admissions and amusement, and impact taxes. Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Montgomery County have broad authority to tax 'to the same extent as the State', but I found no Maryland city or county with a general gross-receipts or business-license tax on software or services companies.

calculatorOption.label: Maryland
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Maryland receipts tax; $300/yr annual report fee as a foreign stock corporation; 8.25% income tax only once profitable.

jurisdictions.name: Baltimore, MD (Baltimore City)
jurisdictions.taxYear: Fiscal 2027 (July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027) city tax rates
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Baltimore City has no general gross-receipts tax and no general business license. The FY2027 city rate list taxes gross receipts only for hotels (9.5%), admissions (10%), and parking (20%). The Department of Consumer Protection and Business Licensing licenses only regulated categories (pawn, scrap, street vendors, late-night commercial operations, parking, towing, and similar).

Business personal property tax is $5.62 per $100 of SDAT-assessed (depreciated) value. It applies only if the company's Maryland personal property totals $20,000 or more at original cost; laptops, furniture, and equipment count. Example: about $25k of depreciated value costs about $1,400/yr. This depends on assets, not revenue, so it is not modeled.

Also owed: energy tax on commercial utility use (per-unit, billed through utilities) and a $4.00 telephone tax per line.

Payroll: the 3.2% city income tax applies to city-resident individuals and is withheld from employees, not paid by the corporation. Corporate income tax is state-only. Baltimore County, a separate jurisdiction, also showed no receipts tax in the DLS overview.

calculatorOption.label: Baltimore
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Baltimore City receipts tax or general business license; personal property tax ($5.62/$100) applies only if Maryland equipment cost is $20k or more.

jurisdictions.name: Montgomery County, MD
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 levy year (July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027)
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
The county's business taxes page lists no gross-receipts or business-receipts tax. Its excise taxes cover only e-cigarettes, fuel-energy (paid through utility bills), room rental, and telephone.

Business personal property tax for the 2026 levy year: the general county rate is $1.6765/$100, and the total with special districts is about $2.58-$4.15/$100. Rockville, Bethesda, and Silver Spring are about $2.60-$2.63; Gaithersburg is $2.73. It applies only if Maryland personal property totals $20,000 or more at original cost. The county page's '$300 minimum fee' is the state SDAT annual report fee, already counted under Maryland, not a county charge.

Circuit Court business (trader's) licenses cover sellers of goods and do not appear to apply to SaaS or services; the court page tells businesses to confirm with the State License Bureau.

Payroll: county income tax on resident employees is withheld through the state; this is an employee cost, not a corporate one.

calculatorOption.label: Montgomery County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Montgomery County receipts tax; personal property tax (about $2.60/$100) applies only if Maryland equipment cost is $20k or more.

jurisdictions.name: Washington, DC
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 D-20 (2025 rate and minimum unchanged into 2026); Sports Facilities Fee schedule current as of Oct 2025; DLCP fees current

receiptsTaxes.name: Sports Facilities Fee (formerly Ballpark Fee), Form FR-1500
receiptsTaxes.base: DC gross receipts from any activity (sales, services, etc.) sourced within the District, before expenses, for the preceding tax year ending before June 15
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: DC-sourced gross receipts (under $5,000,000 owes $0)
receiptsTaxes.notes: This is a flat-tier fee, not a true rate: $5M-$8M pays $5,500; $8,000,001-$12M pays $10,800; $12,000,001-$16M pays $14,000; over $16M pays $16,500. Of these, 0.11% is the effective rate at the $5M entry point, and across $5M-$16M the effective rate is roughly 0.07%-0.11%. Above $16M it falls because the fee is capped. It applies to anyone with $5M+ in DC receipts who files a D-20 or D-30 or is a DC UI employer, and each member of a combined group pays separately. It is due June 15 and must be paid electronically. It was renamed effective Oct 1, 2025 with no change to the calculation; after bond repayment the revenue now goes to the RFK Campus fund.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporation franchise tax minimum (D-20)
fixedAnnual.notes: $250 if DC gross receipts are $1M or less; $1,000 if they exceed $1M. DC gross receipts here are the DC sales-factor numerator, and services are sourced by market-based rules. The minimum is owed even with a loss. Per the 2025 D-20 instructions, a corporation must file if it carries on a trade, business, or commercial activity in DC or receives income from DC sources. A remote SaaS seller with DC customers therefore appears to owe this; P.L. 86-272 does not protect services or SaaS. Nonrefundable credits cannot reduce it.

fixedAnnual.name: Biennial report, foreign for-profit corporation (DLCP)
fixedAnnual.notes: $300 every two years, which is $150/yr. Late fee is $100 if filed after April 1 of the year due. It applies only if the company registers in DC as a foreign corporation, which is required when transacting business there (office, employees). One-time foreign registration is $220.

fixedAnnual.name: Basic Business License, General Business category (DLCP)
fixedAnnual.notes: $99 for a 2-year license or $198 for 4 years, so $49.50/yr; a 6-month license is $49. The General Business subcategories include IT Services, Consulting, and FinTech. It applies when operating in DC and requires a Certificate of Occupancy or Home Occupation Permit and a Clean Hands certificate. The DLCP pages list no extra endorsement or technology fee; I did not verify this at checkout.

profitTaxes.name: DC corporation franchise tax
profitTaxes.notes: 8.25% of DC taxable income (unchanged 2018-2025). Apportionment is single sales factor with market-based sourcing for services, and combined reporting applies. The tax is the larger of this and the $250/$1,000 minimum.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Sales and use tax is passed through to customers and is not counted. DC taxes data processing services, information services, and digital goods, and SaaS can fall under these. The rate is 6.0%, and sources disagree on when it rises to 7%. The OTR taxable-services page and an Oct 2025 OTR notice say 7% starts Oct 1, 2026, while OTR's page (and later reports of a further delay) say 6% runs through Sept 30, 2027. The DC Code text I read still shows Oct 1, 2026. Check with OTR before relying on either.

Personal property tax: $3.40 per $100 of value above a $225,000 exclusion. A return (FP-31, due July 31) is required even when nothing is owed. I saw this only in OTR search excerpts, not on the page itself.

Payroll (belongs in expenses): Universal Paid Leave tax is 0.75% of wages, employer-paid (raised from 0.26% in FY2025; 0.75% for all 2026 quarters per DOES). DC unemployment insurance also applies. DC does not tax nonresident employees' wages, so Maryland and Virginia residents are withheld by their home state.

The unincorporated business franchise tax does not apply to a C corporation.

Modeling caveats: the calculator line approximates the stepped sports facilities fee as 0.11% of DC receipts at $5M+. That overstates the fee above $16M because it caps at $16,500. The line also does not model the minimum tax stepping from $250 to $1,000 once DC receipts pass $1M. A company that only sells into DC remotely, with no DC office, would owe only the $250 minimum, not the biennial report or BBL.

calculatorOption.label: Washington, DC
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $250 DC minimum franchise tax ($1,000 once DC receipts top $1M) plus $150/yr biennial report and $49.50/yr business license; 0.11% of DC receipts at $5M+ approximates the flat $5,500-$16,500 sports facilities fee.

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years beginning 2025 and 2026 (corporate excise rates unchanged since 2012; single-sales-factor apportionment applies to tax years beginning on/after 2025-01-01). Annual report fee per the Corporations Division fee schedule as archived 2026-10-03.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate excise minimum (G.L. c.63 s.39(b))
fixedAnnual.notes: The excise is the greater of (a) $2.60 per $1,000 of the non-income measure plus 8.0% of apportioned net income, or (b) $456. Any business corporation that is qualified (registered) to do business in MA owes at least $456 a year, even with losses and zero MA sales. An unregistered out-of-state corporation is presumed taxable once its MA sales exceed $500,000 a year (830 CMR 63.39.1). P.L. 86-272 does not protect services or software, and MA applies it only to the income measure, never to the non-income measure or the $456 minimum. NON-INCOME MEASURE: a SaaS startup's MA tangible property is under 10% of its assets, which makes it an 'intangible property corporation' (c.63 s.30 paras 10-11). Its non-income measure is then 0.26% x net worth x income apportionment %. Net worth is book total assets minus liabilities (c.63 s.30 para 8), which for a VC-backed startup is roughly cash plus other assets, after preferred equity is counted as equity. From 2025 the apportionment % is the single sales factor: MA sales over total sales, with services sourced where delivered (c.63 s.38(c),(d),(f)). The measure beats the $456 minimum only when apportioned net worth exceeds about $175,400. Example: a company with 2.1% MA sales hits that point at about $8.4M of net worth, so $15M of equity costs about $820/yr. TRAP: a PRE-REVENUE company has zero sales everywhere, and then the sales factor is inapplicable (s.38(g)(i)). Apportionment falls back to property and payroll, so an MA-headquartered pre-revenue startup can apportion about 100% of its net worth to MA. With $10M of equity that is about $26,000/yr in cash, despite having no revenue. Estimated payments are required if the excise exceeds $1,000.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report, foreign corporation (Secretary of the Commonwealth)
fixedAnnual.notes: $100 if filed electronically, $125 on paper, $150 if late. Due 2.5 months after fiscal year end (G.L. c.156D s.16.22), i.e. March 15 for a calendar-year company. The one-time foreign registration fee is $400 ($375 by fax) and is not annual. Fee figures come from the Corporations Division fee schedule. The live site blocks automated fetches (Incapsula), so I read the Wayback Machine copy captured 2026-10-03.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate excise, income measure (G.L. c.63 s.39(a)(2))
profitTaxes.notes: 8.0% of net income apportioned to MA, for tax years beginning on/after 2012-01-01. From 2025 it uses single-sales-factor apportionment with market-based sourcing (services go where delivered; licensed intangibles go where used). It is zero before profit. The 4% 'millionaire's surtax' applies to individuals only, not C corporations.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No MA gross receipts or franchise-on-receipts tax exists. The only pre-profit costs are the $456 minimum excise (or the net-worth measure if larger; see the trap above for MA-headquartered pre-revenue companies) and the $100 annual report. SALES TAX (pass-through): MA taxes prewritten software 'regardless of the method of delivery', including 'transfers of rights to use software installed on a remote server' (830 CMR 64H.1.3), so SaaS sold to MA customers is taxable at 6.25% (G.L. c.64H s.2) with no local add-on. Truly custom software and most professional services are not taxable. The remote-seller collection threshold of $100,000 in MA sales comes from secondary sources only (I did not read 830 CMR 64H.1.7 directly). PAYROLL (already in expenses): figures below are from secondary sources and not verified on mass.gov, which blocked fetches. They are state unemployment insurance (the new-employer rate varies), the Workforce Training Fund (about 0.056% of UI wages), EMAC (about 0.34% on the first $15,000 per employee for employers with 6+ employees), and Paid Family & Medical Leave (0.88% of wages in 2026; employers with fewer than 25 covered workers may skip the employer share). LOCAL: MA cities and towns cannot levy taxes unless the legislature authorizes them (Mass. Const. Amend. Art. 89 s.7). The only authorized local options are property tax, meals (0.75%), room occupancy, cannabis (3%) and motor vehicle excise, so no MA municipality has a local receipts, income or business-license tax on software or services firms. Local personal property tax: business corporations taxed under c.63 s.39 are exempt on most personal property (G.L. c.59 s.5 cl.16(2)). Real estate, poles, wires, conduits, pipes and 'machinery used in the conduct of the business' remain taxable, but that machinery expressly excludes property used in purchasing, selling, accounting or administrative functions. A SaaS startup with leased office space and laptops typically owes little or nothing, though owned servers in MA could be assessed.

calculatorOption.label: Massachusetts
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No MA receipts tax; $456 minimum corporate excise (more if 0.26% of net worth times MA's share of sales is larger) plus $100 annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Boston, MA
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026 / calendar 2026
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Boston has no local income, gross receipts or general business-license tax; the Home Rule Amendment bars it without legislative authorization. A business certificate ($65 per 4 years, plus a $35 non-resident surcharge) is needed only if the corporation operates under a name other than its legal name (a DBA). Corporations are exempt from Boston personal property tax except on poles, wires, pipes, conduits and certain machinery (Boston Assessing). Under G.L. c.59 s.5 cl.16(2), administrative and selling equipment is excluded from taxable machinery, so a typical software office owes little or none; personal property owners still file State Tax Form 2 by March 1. Real estate tax is paid indirectly through rent. Boston's 0.75% local meals tax and room occupancy tax are pass-through and irrelevant here.

calculatorOption.label: Boston
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Boston has no local receipts, income or business-license tax.

jurisdictions.name: Cambridge, MA
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Cambridge has no local receipts, income or business-license tax. The city's FY25 adopted budget lists its only taxes as real property, personal property, hotel/motel excise, meals excise, cannabis excise, motor vehicle excise and in-lieu-of-tax payments. A business certificate ($50, valid 4 years) is needed only if the corporation operates under a name other than its own. Business corporations are largely exempt from local personal property tax (G.L. c.59 s.5 cl.16(2)), the same as in Boston.

calculatorOption.label: Cambridge
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Cambridge has no local receipts, income or business-license tax.

jurisdictions.name: Michigan
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026. The 6% CIT rate was checked in MCL 206.623, which the Legislature's site shows as current through PA 103 of 2026. The $350k threshold comes from the Treasury CIT page and the TY2024 Form 4890 booklet. The $25 annual report fee comes from LARA form CSCL/CD-268.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign profit corporation annual report (LARA)
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 fee, due May 15 each year starting the year after the corporation gets its certificate of authority (MCL 450.1911). Late penalty is $10 per month, capped at $50. If the report is more than a year late, the certificate of authority is revoked automatically. Michigan has no franchise tax or minimum tax.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
profitTaxes.notes: 6% of business income apportioned to Michigan using a single sales factor; services are sourced to where the customer receives the benefit. No return or tax is due if Michigan-apportioned gross receipts are under $350,000 or the liability is $100 or less. Estimated payments start once the expected liability is over $800. A Small Business Alternative Credit (an alternate 1.8% rate on adjusted business income, for gross receipts up to $20M, subject to compensation limits) is available. This is a tax on income, so it is zero before profit. One catch: PA 24 of 2025 (HB 4961, signed Oct 7, 2025) decouples Michigan from the federal immediate R&E expensing under IRC 174A for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2024. For Michigan, R&E (including developer salaries) must still be capitalized and amortized, so a startup losing cash can still show positive Michigan taxable income. That only matters once Michigan-apportioned receipts reach $350k, which is about $11.7M of total revenue at a 3% Michigan share.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Michigan has had no gross-receipts or margin tax since the Michigan Business Tax was replaced by the CIT on Jan 1, 2012. The only exception is a legacy MBT election for holders of certificated credits, which does not apply here. Pending bills HB 4144 (2025) and HB 6134 (introduced June 25, 2026) would raise the CIT to 8.5%; as of October 2026 both are in committee, not enacted. Sales/use tax is 6%. Per secondary sources (Aprio, Allyn), Treasury treats remotely accessed software (pure SaaS) as not taxable after Auto-Owners v. Treasury (Mich. Ct. App. 2015), but downloaded prewritten software is taxable; either way this is collected from customers, not a cost. Payroll costs (already in expenses): state unemployment insurance (UIA). Employers must also withhold city income tax for employees working or living in the 24 Michigan cities that levy one. Personal property tax: commercial personal property in a local unit with combined true cash value under $180,000 is exempt (MCL 211.9o; claim by Feb 20 on Form 5076), so a startup's laptops and furniture normally pay nothing. Cities and villages may not levy any non-property tax unless authorized by law or in place on Jan 1, 1964 (MCL 141.91), so Michigan has no local gross-receipts or business-privilege taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Michigan
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax in Michigan; $25 annual report fee. The 6% income tax is zero before profit and isn't filed below $350k of Michigan receipts.

jurisdictions.name: Detroit, MI
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (City of Detroit Form 5297 instructions, TY2025)

profitTaxes.name: City of Detroit Corporate Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 2.0% for 2025 (the state maximum for a city over 600,000 people is 2% on corporations, MCL 141.503(2)). Every corporation 'doing business' in the city must file Form 5297, whether or not it has an office there. Income is apportioned by property, payroll and sales; service receipts are sourced to where the services are rendered. The return is filed with and administered by Michigan Treasury. Quarterly estimates are required once the annual liability is over $250. Renaissance Zone deductions are available. This tax is on net income, so it is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No gross-receipts or business-privilege tax; MCL 141.91 bars cities from non-property taxes unless authorized. No general business license: BSEED says 'Not all businesses need a license', and the licensed categories (cabarets, vendors, lodging, gas stations, second-hand dealers, etc.) don't include software or professional offices. In 2024 the city dropped 34 license types and kept 42 health/safety categories. Payroll (already in expenses or employee-borne): employers must withhold Detroit city income tax from employees, at 2.4% for residents and 1.2% for nonresidents working in Detroit; this is the employee's tax, not an employer cost.

calculatorOption.label: Detroit
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Detroit has no receipts tax or general business license; its 2.0% corporate income tax is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Grand Rapids, MI
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (2025 Form GR-1120 instructions)

profitTaxes.name: City of Grand Rapids Corporation Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 1.5% corporate rate. The 2025 GR-1120 header box still reads '2024 Tax Rate', which looks like a carried-over label; the rate is unchanged. Every corporation 'doing business' in the city must file Form GR-1120, whether or not it has an office there. Income is apportioned under the uniform city income tax ordinance. Estimated payments may be required once the tax is $250 or more. This tax is on net income, so it is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No gross-receipts tax (MCL 141.91). No general business license: the City Clerk licenses only specific activities (liquor, hotels, mobile food and vending, parking facilities, pawnbrokers, second-hand dealers, snowplow, solid waste haulers, indoor events of 50+ people, home occupations, etc.). Payroll (employee-borne): employers withhold Grand Rapids income tax at 1.5% for residents and 0.75% for nonresidents working in the city. Small business personal property tax exemption under $180k true cash value applies (city assessor).

calculatorOption.label: Grand Rapids
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Grand Rapids has no receipts tax or general business license; its 1.5% corporate income tax is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Ann Arbor, MI
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (current city clerk license list; current Michigan city income tax list)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Included because Ann Arbor is Michigan's main startup hub, to show that nothing is owed there. It does not levy a city income tax: it is absent from the list of Michigan cities with an income tax published by Grand Rapids' income tax department. It has no receipts tax (MCL 141.91). The City Clerk's license list (auctioneer, liquor, marijuana facility, gem/precious metal dealer, going-out-of-business, etc.) includes no general business license for a software or professional services office. Ordinary property tax applies to real property, and personal property under $180k true cash value is exempt.

calculatorOption.label: Ann Arbor
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Ann Arbor has no city income tax, receipts tax, or general business license.

jurisdictions.name: Minnesota
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years beginning in 2026 (minimum fee brackets for 2026; 2025 brackets in notes). Secretary of State fees current as of Oct 2026.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign corporation annual renewal (Secretary of State)
fixedAnnual.notes: Foreign business corporation (Ch. 303) annual renewal: $135 online/expedited, $115 by mail. Required every calendar year. Initial certificate of authority is a one-time $220 online / $200 mail. A Minnesota-domestic corporation's annual renewal is $0, but this user is a Delaware corp.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporation franchise tax minimum fee (lowest non-zero tier)
fixedAnnual.notes: Owed on top of the regular 9.8% tax (MS 290.0922 subd. 1) whatever the profit. The base is Minnesota property + payroll + sales. Property counts owned tangible property at cost plus rent paid x 8. Payroll is Minnesota payroll. Sales are receipts sourced to Minnesota. 2026 brackets: under $1,280,000 = $0; $1,280,000-$2,559,999 = $260; $2,560,000-$12,829,999 = $770; $12,830,000-$25,639,999 = $2,560; $25,640,000-$51,279,999 = $5,140; $51,280,000 or more = $12,830. 2025 brackets: under $1,250,000 = $0; $1.25M-$2.51M = $260; $2.51M-$12.54M = $750; $12.54M-$25.07M = $2,510; $25.07M-$50.14M = $5,020; $50.14M+ = $12,540. Brackets are indexed every year. I assumed the $260 tier, which fits about 10-20 Minnesota employees. It is $0 if the company has only a remote employee or two in Minnesota, and $770 at roughly 20+ Minnesota employees or a large Minnesota office lease.

profitTaxes.name: Corporation franchise tax
profitTaxes.notes: 9.8% of taxable income (MS 290.06 subd. 1). Uses single-sales-factor apportionment. Service receipts are sourced to where the service is received. For a business customer, that is limited to states where the customer has a fixed place of business, then falls back to the ordering office, then the billing address. Intangibles (licenses) are sourced to where the purchaser uses them. The NOL deduction is limited to 70% of taxable income. The 2026 Tax Act (Ch. 128, HF 2438) decouples C corporations from OBBBA's immediate domestic R&E expensing, so Minnesota keeps 5-year amortization of R&E. As a result, a company whose costs are mostly R&D salaries could show positive Minnesota taxable income while still losing money on a book or federal basis. A corporate AMT still appears in the M4 instructions (Schedules AMTI/AMTT apply when Minnesota net income plus preferences exceeds $40,000).

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
No gross receipts tax: Minnesota has no general receipts, margin, or franchise-on-receipts tax for a software or services company. The only revenue-linked charge is the minimum fee step function above. Revenue counts toward it only once Minnesota-sourced sales, plus Minnesota payroll and property, pass $1.28M. For a national seller with no Minnesota staff, sales of about 1.7% of revenue reach $1.28M only at about $75M of total revenue.

Nexus: Minnesota has no published dollar bright line. The Department of Revenue says providing services to Minnesota customers who receive them in Minnesota, even if performed remotely, can create a filing requirement. It handles nexus determinations case by case on Forms C101/C102.

Sales tax (pass-through): Online-hosted software (SaaS) subscriptions are NOT taxable. Custom software is not taxable, and IT, consulting, and professional services generally are not either. Prewritten (canned) software is taxable however it is delivered, including downloads. The state rate is 6.875%, plus local taxes: Minneapolis totals 9.025% and St. Paul 9.875% (rate guide effective 10/1/2026). The governor's 2025 proposal to tax accounting, legal and brokerage services was not enacted in 2025 (1st Special Session Ch. 13). The 2026 Tax Act summary (Ch. 128) contains no such expansion either.

Payroll (already in expenses):
- Minnesota UI: 2026 taxable wage base $44,000 and base tax rate 0.40%. New-employer rates are set by industry. These figures came from uimn.org search snippets; I did not read the pages in full.
- Minnesota Paid Leave premiums began 1/1/2026 at 0.88% of wages. Employers pay at least 50% and may deduct up to 0.44% from employees. The small-employer rate is 0.66% (30 or fewer employees and average wage under 150% of the state average), with the employer paying at least 33%. pl.mn.gov returned 403, so these figures come from search snippets of the official site.
- No local income or payroll taxes.

Local: MS 477A.016 bars any county or city from imposing new taxes on sales or income. Special local taxes (lodging, food and beverage, admissions) need legislative authorization and don't apply to SaaS or professional services. I found no Minnesota city with a general gross receipts or business-privilege tax on software or services. This is Likely, based on the statute plus the city pages I checked; I did not survey every city.

Other: MinnesotaCare's 2% provider tax is a gross receipts tax that applies only to health care providers.

calculatorOption.label: Minnesota
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; $135 foreign-corp annual renewal plus the $260 minimum fee (2026), which applies once Minnesota payroll + property (rent x 8) + Minnesota sales reach $1.28M ($0 below that, $770 above $2.56M).

jurisdictions.name: Minneapolis, MN
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city gross receipts, business-privilege, income or head tax. Minneapolis licenses only regulated business types: animal, alcohol/tobacco, body art/massage, contractors, door-to-door/secondhand, dry cleaning, entertainment, food, innovative small business, lodging and vehicles. An office-based software or consulting company falls under none of these, so I found no general business license fee. The city page lists categories but has no explicit statement that unlisted businesses are exempt. The combined sales tax rate is 9.025% (state 6.875% + Minneapolis 0.50% + Hennepin County 0.15% + transit 0.50% + metro area 1.00%), effective 10/1/2026. It is pass-through and applies only to taxable items such as downloaded prewritten software, not SaaS. Minneapolis also levies 3% downtown/special taxes on restaurant food, liquor, lodging and entertainment, none of which applies here.

calculatorOption.label: Minneapolis
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Minneapolis has no gross receipts, business-privilege or head tax, and no general business license for software or services firms.

jurisdictions.name: St. Paul, MN
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city gross receipts, business-privilege, income or head tax. The Department of Safety and Inspections licenses only listed regulated categories (liquor, animal, auto, entertainment, food, trades, etc.), and none covers an office-based software or consulting firm. The city tells businesses that don't see their type to call a Project Facilitator rather than stating they are exempt, so absence of a license fee is from the category list. The combined sales tax rate is 9.875% (state 6.875% + St. Paul 1.50% + transit 0.50% + metro area 1.00%), effective 10/1/2026. It is pass-through and does not apply to SaaS.

calculatorOption.label: St. Paul
calculatorOption.assumptionText: St. Paul has no gross receipts, business-privilege or head tax, and no general business license for software or services firms.

jurisdictions.name: Mississippi
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (franchise tax rate from the DOR's published phase-out schedule; 2025 rate and the $25 minimum confirmed in the 2025 Form 83-100 instructions, Rev. 01/26)

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate franchise tax (minimum)
fixedAnnual.notes: Capital-based, not receipts-based. Base: capital stock, surplus, undivided profits and true reserves (net book equity, so accumulated losses reduce it) apportioned to Mississippi. The apportionment ratio is MS real/tangible property plus MS gross receipts, divided by total property plus total gross receipts. MS capital is floored at the assessed value of MS property. Rate per $1,000 of MS capital over $100,000: $0.75 for 2025, $0.50 for 2026, $0.25 for 2027, and the tax is repealed for 2028 onward (SB 2858, 2016). The minimum is $25. Every corporation qualified to do business in MS must file even if inactive. Foreign corporations with MS income sources are subject to the levy even if not qualified. A pre-profit SaaS startup with a small MS receipts share will almost always land under $100k of MS capital and pay the $25 minimum. Example: $20M equity times 1% MS share gives $200k, so ($200k - $100k) / $1,000 x $0.50 = $50 for 2026. Filed with the income tax return (Form 83-105), due the 15th day of the 4th month after year end.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (foreign for-profit corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 per the SOS Services & Fees Schedule (Revised October 2024), under 'Foreign Profit & Non-Profit Corporations'. Filed online and due April 15; an online portal convenience fee may apply. Don't confuse this with the $250 for foreign LLCs. The certificate of authority to qualify a foreign profit corporation is a one-time $500, not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 0% on the first $5,000 of MS taxable income, 4% on the next $5,000, 5% above $10,000 (2025 instructions; I found no 2026 change to corporate rates). There's no minimum income tax. Apportioned and filed on the combined income and franchise return. It's zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Mississippi has no gross receipts, margin, or B&O-style tax. Pre-profit, the only state-level costs are the $25 minimum franchise tax (through 2027) and the $25 annual report.

Sales tax (pass-through, not counted): state rate 7%. SB 2449 (2023) amended the sales and use tax law to say 'Computer software maintained on a server located outside the state and accessible for use only via the internet is not a taxable retail sale' and is not a taxable use. So SaaS hosted outside MS isn't taxable, but SaaS hosted on servers in MS can be. Computer software services (design, programming, installing, configuring, debugging, modifying, testing, troubleshooting) remain taxable at the retail rate. Other professional services are generally not taxed. Jackson adds a 1% special sales tax on certain retail sales and Tupelo adds 0.25% (DOR FAQ).

Payroll (already in expenses): state unemployment insurance (MDES) on MS employees and state income tax withholding. Mississippi has no local income or payroll taxes. The individual income tax is phasing down to a 4% flat rate in 2026.

Other: business personal property in MS (furniture, computers) is subject to local ad valorem property tax. Any physical business location in a MS municipality or county needs the uniform statutory local privilege license ($20 to $150 per year by employee count, Miss. Code §27-17-9), whichever city it's in. See the Jackson entry.

I looked for other MS cities with a local receipts or business tax on software or services companies and found none. Local options are limited to legislatively authorized special and tourism sales taxes and the fixed statutory privilege license. That was a search, not an exhaustive survey of all municipalities.

calculatorOption.label: Mississippi
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Mississippi receipts tax; $25 minimum franchise tax (phased out, repealed from 2028) plus $25 foreign-corporation annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Jackson, MS
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026 (statute text marked current as of January 1, 2025; the city page lists no amounts)

fixedAnnual.name: Business privilege license
fixedAnnual.notes: This is the uniform statutory amount under Miss. Code §27-17-9, the same in every MS municipality and county; it isn't set by Jackson. $20 a year for 3 or fewer employees, $30 for 4 to 10, and $30 plus $3 per employee over 10 for 11 or more, capped at $150 (manufacturers with 11+ pay $80). $30 assumes a small startup with 4 to 10 employees at the Jackson location. It applies only to businesses operating within city limits: Jackson's application asks for proof of occupancy (lease, deed, or utility bill), a notarized privilege tax form, and an SOS good-standing certificate or annual report. Renewed annually. A remote seller with customers in Jackson but no location there owes nothing. The city site only says 'Fees vary based on business type and size'. The amounts come from the statute text on FindLaw, a secondary host of the official code.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Jackson has no city income, payroll, or gross receipts tax; Mississippi doesn't authorize local income taxes. The 1% Jackson special (infrastructure) sales tax on certain retail sales is collected from customers, so it's pass-through and not counted. Business personal property in a Jackson office is subject to city, county, and school ad valorem property tax, which is not receipts-based. Not worth its own calculator line: at $20 to $150 a year the license is effectively $0, and it's the same statewide.

calculatorOption.label: Jackson
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Jackson receipts tax; a statewide $20-$150 privilege license applies only if you have a location there.

jurisdictions.name: Missouri
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (tax year 2026; registration report fee per RSMo 351.125/351.127 as in force Oct 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Annual corporate registration report (foreign or domestic for-profit corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: RSMo 351.125: $15 if filed electronically ($40 on paper), plus the $5 technology-fund add-on in RSMo 351.127, so $20 online or $45 on paper. RSMo 351.120 requires every foreign corporation licensed to do business in Missouri to file. It is due in the month the corporation qualified (or a month it later picks). There is an optional biennial filing under RSMo 351.122: $30 electronic + $10 = $40 per two years, the same $20/yr. The text of 351.127 says the add-on expires Dec 31, 2026, so from 2027 the online fee may drop to $15 unless the legislature extends it. The certificate-of-authority fee to qualify is one-time, not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Missouri corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: RSMo 143.071: 4% of Missouri taxable income for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2020. No minimum tax. Zero before profit. Amendment 5, which would have phased out the income tax and allowed broad sales taxes on services, was rejected by voters on Aug 4, 2026 (news reports, not an official source), so nothing changes.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No state gross receipts tax. The corporation franchise tax is gone: RSMo 147.010 says 'For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2016, no annual franchise tax shall be imposed.' SaaS is not subject to Missouri sales/use tax (12 CSR 10-109.050: 'The sale of software as a service is not subject to tax'; electronically delivered canned software is also not taxable, while software on tangible media is). Payroll costs belong in expenses: Missouri income tax withholding and state unemployment insurance. County business personal property tax applies to business equipment (computers, furniture). It is assessed by the county where the equipment sits, scales with equipment rather than revenue, and is not modelled here. RSMo 71.620 bars city license taxes on lawyers, CPAs, physicians and similar professions, and on architects/engineers without an office in the city. A software company gets no such exemption. Many Missouri cities charge their own business license taxes measured by gross receipts (see the city entries); the state does not.

calculatorOption.label: Missouri
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Missouri has no receipts or franchise tax (franchise tax repealed from 2016); a foreign corporation pays a $20 online annual registration report.

jurisdictions.name: Kansas City, MO
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (calendar year). Rate table from KC Code Sec. 40-63, codified through Ord. 260342 (Apr 16, 2026); identical to the 2022 RD-105 Table A

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license tax (Table A: retail, wholesale and service)
receiptsTaxes.base: Annual gross receipts of the business licensed in KC. Sec. 40-62: '12 times the average monthly gross receipts ... from whatever source derived, from all services performed ... and all commissions, fees, charges and compensation earned'. The RD-105 asks for 'KCMO gross receipts'. Sec. 40-64 lets a licensee apply for fair apportionment if the tax would burden interstate commerce. For a KC-located wholesaler, the city's guidance counts KC deliveries plus sales shipped from KC to points in Missouri, which suggests interstate receipts may be excludable. How a KC-based SaaS company's out-of-state receipts are treated is unverified.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (flat $25 minimum covers receipts up to $28,000)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Brackets: $25 flat for $1 to $28,000. Above that, a base plus a marginal rate per $1,000 over the bracket floor: $0.90 for $28k–55k (base $25), $0.89 for 55k–110k ($50), $0.88 for 110k–220k ($99), $0.87 for 220k–440k ($196), $0.86 for 440k–880k ($388), $0.85 for 880k–1.76M ($767), $0.84 for 1.76M–3.52M ($1,515), $0.83 for 3.52M–7.04M ($2,994), $0.82 for 7.04M–14.08M ($5,916), $0.81 for 14.08M–28.16M ($11,689), falling to $0.75 above $901.12M. Effective rate: about 0.090% at $100k, 0.088% at $500k, 0.087% at $1M, 0.084% at $5M, 0.083% at $10M. Modelled as 0.085% plus $25, which is within about 3% of the true fee from $100k to $10M (slightly high at the low end). Filing: Form RD-105 within 60 days of opening (on estimated receipts), then each year before March 1, with a true-up against the prior year's actual receipts. 5%/month late penalty, max 25%. Sec. 40-61 requires a license of any corporation 'engaged in any business ... within the City'. City guidance says businesses located elsewhere that operate in KC also need one. A remote seller with no KC employees or office is probably outside it, but that is unverified.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 flat for gross receipts up to $28,000 (Table A). Counted as the fixed part of the 0.085% + $25 approximation.

profitTaxes.name: Earnings and profits tax on net profits
profitTaxes.notes: KC Code Sec. 68-382(a)(5): 1.0% on 'net profits of all corporations earned as a result of work done or services performed or rendered or business or other activities conducted in the city'. Sec. 68-384 allocates with a three-factor average of property, payroll and gross receipts; services are sourced where the income-producing activity is performed (cost of performance). Zero before profit. Voters renewed the tax on April 7, 2026, keeping it until 2031 (news reports).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (expense, not modelled here): the same 1% earnings tax applies to wages of KC residents and of nonresidents working in KC. Employers must withhold it, but the employee bears it; KC has no employer-paid payroll expense tax. Local sales tax follows Missouri's base, so SaaS is not taxed. From Jan 1, 2026, license renewals reportedly require a Business Personal Property Tax receipt (county property tax on equipment; search-result excerpt of kcmo.gov, page not readable). Renewals may also require a Missouri no-tax-due letter. kcmo.gov blocks automated fetches (403), so the FAQ and current RD-105 PDF could not be read. Rates were taken from the official code (Municode, read via its API) and a hosted copy of the 2022 RD-105, which match.

calculatorOption.label: Kansas City, MO
calculatorOption.assumptionText: About 0.085% of gross receipts plus $25 (Kansas City business license, Table A tiers); assumes your office is in KC and all receipts count, though the city may apportion out-of-state receipts on request.

jurisdictions.name: St. Louis, MO (City)
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year June 1, 2026 – May 31, 2027 (fee schedule unchanged since FY2007); earnings tax 2026

fixedAnnual.name: Graduated Business License (GBL) tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Set by the number of full-time and full-time-equivalent employees, including owners and officers, who worked in the City in the prior calendar year. An employee is someone working 1,920+ hours/yr. Tiers: 0–2 $200; 3–5 $325; 6–10 $675; 11–20 $1,500; 21–30 $2,250; 31–40 $3,000; 41–50 $4,500; 51–75 $7,500; 76–100 $11,250; 101–150 $15,000; 151–200 $20,250; 201–300 $25,500; 301–400 $30,000; 401–500 $34,500; 501+ $37,500. The first license costs $200 if you start June 1–Jan 1, or $100 if you start Jan 1–May 31. The $675 figure assumes 6–10 City employees. Due before June 1. Required of 'any person who engages in any business within the City Limits'.

profitTaxes.name: Earnings tax on business net profits (Form E-234)
profitTaxes.notes: 1% of net profits, allocated by a three-factor formula: gross receipts, property, payroll. The city says a business with any one factor must file an E-234, so a company selling into St. Louis without an office may still have to file a zero-tax return before profit. Voters renewed the tax for five years on April 7, 2026 (Prop E, about 85% yes; news reports).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (expense, not modelled here): the Payroll Expense Tax is 0.5% of wages earned in the City, paid by the employer. The city page lists no small-employer exemption. Separately, 1% earnings tax is withheld from wages of employees who live or work in the City; the employee bears it. Both are filed quarterly on W-10/P-10. The City's gross receipts taxes cover only restaurants and parking, and its merchants'/manufacturers' license covers sellers of goods, so neither applies to SaaS or services. Business personal property tax is also assessed by the City. No SaaS sales tax (Missouri base).

calculatorOption.label: St. Louis
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $675/yr Graduated Business License assuming 6–10 employees working in the City ($200 for 0–2, $1,500 for 11–20); no receipts tax on services.

jurisdictions.name: Clayton, MO
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027 (fee based on calendar-2025 receipts for renewals)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license fee on gross receipts (Code ch. 605, Sec. 605.090)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts of the business licensed in Clayton. Excerpts of the code quote '$1.25 for one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) of gross receipts or fraction thereof'. Not verified: whether a Clayton-based company counts all national receipts or can apportion.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (minimum fee $50)
receiptsTaxes.notes: $1.25 per $1,000 (0.125%), minimum $50. No maximum appeared in the excerpts seen. New businesses estimate; renewals use the prior calendar year's receipts. Due June 30, delinquent Aug 1. Clayton is the St. Louis County seat and a major office district, which is why it is listed. Other St. Louis County municipalities (Town and Country, Glendale, Ellisville, Richmond Heights, etc.) have similar gross-receipts license codes that were not researched. claytonmo.gov and ecode360.com returned 403 to every fetch. All figures come from search-engine excerpts of those official pages, which agreed with each other.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: Minimum annual license fee $50. It is a floor, so adding it on top of 0.125% overstates by up to $50.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city earnings tax. Clayton's 8% gross receipts tax applies only to utilities. Payroll and sales taxes follow Missouri and St. Louis County rules. No SaaS sales tax.

calculatorOption.label: Clayton, MO
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.125% of gross receipts (minimum $50) Clayton business license; assumes your office is in Clayton and all receipts count.

jurisdictions.name: Columbia, MO
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027 (Code Sec. 13-27 as amended by Ord. 25859, Jan 6, 2025)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license fee on gross receipts
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts; the city's guidance says 'all revenue received from doing business in Columbia, Missouri'. A Columbia-based company presumably counts its receipts; how out-of-city customers are treated is not spelled out.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none (minimum fee $75)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Code Sec. 13-27(a): '$0.25 per $1,000 of gross receipts', minimum $75, maximum $10,000 (the cap is reached at $40M). The council paused a planned graduated structure on Apr 15, 2024, so the flat rate and cap stand. New businesses estimate; established ones use the prior 12 months (Sec. 13-28). The city also lists a $45 application fee; whether it applies to renewals is unverified.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $75 minimum annual fee. The $45 application fee applies at least to new applications.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city earnings or payroll tax. No SaaS sales tax. Small in dollar terms: 0.025% is $250 per $1M.

calculatorOption.label: Columbia, MO
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.025% of gross receipts (minimum $75, maximum $10,000) Columbia business license; assumes your office is in Columbia.

jurisdictions.name: Independence, MO
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Ch. 5 rewritten by Ord. 19553, May 2024; fee per city Schedule of Fees and the current city web page)

receiptsTaxes.name: Occupation business license fee
