receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts per Sec. 5.01.002, consistent with the federal tax accounting basis. Businesses inside the city report all receipts. Under Sec. 5.01.013(B), businesses outside the city report only receipts from activity within the city.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none ($75 covers the first $25,000)
receiptsTaxes.notes: $75 for the first $25,000 of receipts, plus $0.31 per $1,000 (or fraction) above $25,000, maximum $50,000. New businesses in Independence with 10 or fewer employees pay a flat $75 in their first year. Sec. 5.01.003 requires a license of every person 'whether or not located in the City' doing business there, and 'one act thereof shall constitute doing business'.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license base fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $75, covering the first $25,000 of receipts.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city earnings or payroll tax. No SaaS sales tax. Small: about $310 per $1M of receipts.

calculatorOption.label: Independence, MO
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $75 plus 0.031% of gross receipts over $25k (maximum $50,000) Independence business license; assumes your office is in Independence.

jurisdictions.name: Springfield, MO
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Code Ch. 70 as published on Municode, 2026 supplement)

receiptsTaxes.name: Occupational business license, standard scale
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross sales or receipts for the license year (Sec. 70-82). Only contractors are expressly limited to receipts from work performed inside the city.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Sec. 70-84 lists about 140 named occupations; software/SaaS is not one of them. The closest catch-all is item 117, 'service agents or agencies ... not otherwise specified': $25 minimum for the first $10,000, plus the Sec. 70-81 standard scale above that. The scale charges $0.50 per $1,000 from $10k to $100k, $0.35 from $100k to $200k, and $0.25 over $200k, with fractions rounded up to $1,000. That works out to about $70 at $100k, $105 at $200k, and $305 at $1M, i.e. roughly 0.025% plus $55 above $200k. Classification for a software company is unverified; the city's F1/F2/F3 category system may assign a flat fee instead. The city says businesses based outside Springfield that conduct business inside it are 'likely' required to be licensed.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license (approximation offset)
fixedAnnual.notes: The real minimum is $25. $55 is the intercept that makes 0.025% + $55 match the scale above $200k; it overstates by up to $30 at very low receipts.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city earnings or payroll tax. No SaaS sales tax.

calculatorOption.label: Springfield, MO
calculatorOption.assumptionText: About 0.025% of gross receipts plus $55 (standard-scale business license, $25 minimum), assuming Springfield treats a software company as a 'service agency'.

jurisdictions.name: Lee's Summit, MO

fixedAnnual.name: Business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Flat $55 per the city's licensing page; expires one year from issuance. Code Sec. 28-30 points to the city's Schedule of Fees and Charges.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No receipts-based license tax for general businesses and no earnings tax. Negligible, but listed because it is a fixed annual amount.

calculatorOption.label: Lee's Summit, MO
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $55 flat Lee's Summit business license.

jurisdictions.name: St. Louis County, MO
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No county-level gross receipts or earnings tax. The county's $5 merchant/manufacturer license is only for sellers or manufacturers of goods, so it doesn't apply to SaaS or services. Businesses must register with the County Assessor for business personal property tax (a property tax on equipment, not modelled). Most of the county is inside municipalities, many with their own gross-receipts license codes (see Clayton). Based on search-result excerpts of stlouiscountymo.gov; the pages were not read in full.

calculatorOption.label: St. Louis County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No county-level receipts tax or license fee for a services company in St. Louis County.

jurisdictions.name: Montana
jurisdictions.taxYear: Corporate income tax: tax years beginning 2025 (2025 Form CIT instructions; same rules for 2026). Annual report: 2026 and 2027 filing seasons.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate income tax minimum tax
fixedAnnual.notes: MCA 15-31-121(3): 'Each corporation subject to taxation under this part shall pay a minimum tax of not less than $50.' The 2025 CIT instructions say the $50 minimum 'applies to each corporation having activity in Montana, regardless of whether the company has a net operating loss' (in a combined return, $50 for each member with Montana activity). The only exception is the elective 0.5% alternative tax described in otherNotes.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (foreign profit corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: The fee is normally $20 if filed Jan 1 to Apr 15, and $35 after ($20 plus a $15 late fee), per the SOS fee sheet PDF. The SOS fees page currently shows the on-time fee as 'WAIVED', and SOS press releases say the fee is waived for reports filed Jan 1 to Apr 15 in both 2026 and 2027 (the third and fourth years in a row). Late filings still cost $35. Budget $20/yr from 2028 unless the waiver is renewed. The one-time foreign Certificate of Authority fee is $70.

profitTaxes.name: Montana corporate income tax (formerly corporation license tax)
profitTaxes.notes: 6.75% of Montana net income, or 7% with a water's-edge election (MCA 15-31-121). For tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2024 (SB 124, 2023), income is apportioned by a single receipts factor. Service and intangible receipts are sourced by market, e.g. services 'to the extent the service is delivered to a location in Montana' (MCA 15-31-311). Montana has its own NOL rules (15-31-119), with carrybacks capped at $500,000 per period. Nothing is owed above the $50 minimum until there is Montana taxable income.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No gross receipts, franchise, or margin tax applies to this company in Montana. The only receipts-measured option is the ELECTIVE alternative tax (MCA 15-31-122): 0.5% of Montana gross receipts, paid instead of income tax. It is available only if the company's only Montana activity is receipts (no owned or rented property in Montana) and Montana receipts are at most $100,000. It is also not subject to the $50 minimum. A pre-profit company would elect it only if it costs less than $50, i.e. Montana receipts under $10,000, so it can only lower the bill. A company with employees in Montana likely fails the 'only receipts' test. Montana has no general state sales or use tax, so SaaS is not taxed. Local resort taxes (up to 3%, or 4% in some places) exist only in about 11 voter-approved resort communities (e.g., Whitefish, Big Sky, West Yellowstone) and apply to lodging, restaurants, and luxury goods, not SaaS. That list comes from secondary sources. A 2025 bill for a general local-option sales tax (HB 489) failed in the House Local Government Committee 6-11, per secondary sources. Business personal property (class 8, e.g. laptops and servers) is exempt up to $1 million statewide aggregate market value (revenue.mt.gov), so a small startup owes no equipment tax but must report by Feb 15 if it owns property in Montana. Payroll costs belong in expenses: Montana income tax withholding, state unemployment insurance (UI) on wages, and workers' comp. Montana cities do not levy local income or gross receipts taxes. City business licenses are flat or scale with headcount or square footage: Billings, Missoula, Bozeman (below), Helena, Great Falls. The corporate e-file mandate does not apply to corporations with gross receipts of $750,000 or less.

calculatorOption.label: Montana
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Montana: $50 minimum corporate income tax (owed even at a loss); no receipts tax; the $20 annual report fee is waived for on-time filings in 2026 and 2027.

jurisdictions.name: Billings, MT
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current Business Tax Determination form (2024 revision, still the posted form in 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: City business license (business, occupation and profession tax)
fixedAnnual.notes: The official 2024 form pre-fills Basic Tax as $55.00, plus $6 for each full-time employee over 5 ('Excess of 5: $6 ea'). The $50 health fee and $200-$500 liquor fees on the form do not apply to a software or services office. Examples: 10 FTE pays $55 + 5 x $6 = $85; 30 FTE pays $205. The license runs one year from the month issued and is renewed annually. The schedule lives in Billings Municipal Code Art. 13-400; the code text was not readable (JS-only site), so the per-employee mechanics are from the form only.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No local receipts, income, or payroll tax. Per the city site, anyone who 'conducts business in the City or is based in the City' needs a license. It is unclear whether a remote SaaS seller with Billings customers but no office or staff there must license, and I found nothing saying it is enforced against such sellers. Treat it as applying only if you have an office or employees in Billings. A separate license is needed for each location.

calculatorOption.label: Billings
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Billings: $55/yr business license plus $6 per full-time employee over 5, only if you have an office or staff there; no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Missoula, MT
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2027 fee schedule (effective October 1, 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: City business license renewal (General license, FTE-based)
fixedAnnual.notes: FY2027 renewal: $28 per full-time-equivalent (FTE) employee, with a 4-FTE minimum ($113) and 85-FTE maximum ($2,410), plus a 5% tech fee on total fees. That makes the minimum about $118.65/yr, used here. 10 FTE pays $280 + 5% = $294; 85+ FTE pays about $2,531. First year (new application) for a commercial location in city limits: $63/FTE, minimum $252 (4 FTE), maximum $5,355, plus 5%. Home-based: $42/FTE, minimum $168. Outside city limits: $35/FTE, minimum $139. FTE = total weekly hours of all employees and owners / 40. Headcount is taken as of May 31 of the prior year, or projected 60 days after opening for a new business. The code does not say whether employees outside Missoula count.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No local receipts, income, or payroll tax. Per city FAQ, 'Any person or entity conducting business and/or offering goods or services within the Missoula City Limits, and grossing more than $6,000 annually' needs a license. Web-based businesses physically in the city are explicitly covered. The fee schedule's 'Outside City Limits' category suggests outside businesses serving Missoula are also covered. Whether a remote SaaS seller with Missoula customers must license is unclear, and enforcement against such sellers is unverified. Treat it as applying if you have an office or staff in Missoula. Commercial rental licenses (by square footage) fall on landlords, not tenants.

calculatorOption.label: Missoula
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Missoula: business license renewal of $28 per FTE (4-FTE minimum, about $119/yr with the 5% tech fee), only if you operate there; no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Bozeman, MT
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (as shown on city site per search excerpt)

fixedAnnual.name: City business license (standard)
fixedAnnual.notes: Search-engine excerpts of the official bozemanmt.gov business license pages show a $75 application fee for commercial, home-based, and out-of-city-limits businesses, and a $75 renewal for standard licenses. Licenses are valid 12 months from the end of the month issued. The pages returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches, so I could not read or confirm the fee myself.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Included because Bozeman is Montana's main tech hub. No local receipts, income, or payroll tax. The flat license applies only if you operate in Bozeman. Bozeman is not a resort-tax community (nearby Big Sky is, but that tax does not reach SaaS). The official pages returned 403 when fetched: https://www.bozemanmt.gov/departments/community-development/business-licenses and https://www.bozemanmt.gov/departments/community-development/business-licenses/business-license-renewal

calculatorOption.label: Bozeman
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Bozeman: $75/yr flat business license if you operate there (amount unconfirmed); no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Nebraska
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026 (income tax rate: 5.20% for tax years beginning in 2025, 4.55% for 2026, 3.99% for 2027 on; occupation tax report due March 1, 2026, then every even year)

fixedAnnual.name: Biennial occupation tax and report for foreign corporations (Secretary of State)
fixedAnnual.notes: Neb. Rev. Stat. 21-304/21-306. A foreign corporation authorized in Nebraska files a biennial report as of January 1 of each even year. It is due March 1 and delinquent after April 15 (most recently 2026, next 2028). The tax is double the domestic schedule in 21-303 and is measured by the actual value of real and personal property the corporation uses in Nebraska. The domestic minimum is $26 for $10,000 or less, so a foreign corporation pays at least $52 for property of $10,000 or less (a remote employee's laptop). The cap is $30,000. $52 every 2 years is about $26/yr. The tiers continue at double the domestic schedule: $80 up to $20k of property, $120 up to $30k, $400 up to $100k. Reading the statute gives the $52 minimum by arithmetic, and Discern states it explicitly (secondary source). I found no separate filing fee for this report on the SOS fee page. LB315 (2025) would have repealed this tax, but it was indefinitely postponed on April 17, 2026, so the tax is still in force. One-time costs are not included: the certificate of authority costs $100 online or $110 on paper, plus $10 for the certificate.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax (flat)
profitTaxes.notes: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2734.02 sets the rate at 5.20% for tax years beginning in 2025 (confirmed in the 2025 Form 1120N booklet). It falls to 4.55% for tax years beginning in 2026 and 3.99% for 2027 onward. Income is apportioned by a single sales factor. There is no minimum tax, and nothing is owed before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Nebraska has no gross receipts, franchise or margin tax. Sales tax is 5.5% state plus local; Omaha is 1.5% and Lincoln 1.75% per the Q1 2026 Form 10 schedule. Sales tax is passed through to customers. Software is taxable 'regardless of the manner in which it is conveyed' (Reg 1-088), including downloaded software. Consulting that results in a transfer of software (programming, customization, installation) is taxable. Pure advisory consulting is exempt. Remotely accessed SaaS is generally not taxable because it is not a transfer of 'computer software'. That conclusion comes from secondary sources (Numeral, Anrok and others); I found no DOR document stating it outright. Software that performs a security function can be taxed as a security service. Remote sellers must register above $100,000 of gross sales into Nebraska or 200 transactions a year (DOR Wayfair FAQ). The 2026 legislative changes summary shows no expansion to SaaS or digital services and no new business-level receipts tax. Payroll costs belong in expenses: state income tax withholding and state unemployment insurance. Nebraska has no local income taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Nebraska
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax in Nebraska; a $52 occupation tax every two years (about $26/yr) as a foreign corporation with under $10k of property there.

jurisdictions.name: Omaha, NE
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Omaha Municipal Code codified through Ord. 44760, Aug 4, 2026; 2027 recommended budget)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Omaha's official ONEBiz page says: 'there is no business license requirement with the City of Omaha.' Omaha has no general gross receipts or business tax on software or professional services firms. Its occupation taxes are industry-specific: restaurants and bars 2.5% of food and beverage receipts, hotels 5.5%, tobacco 3%, telephone 4.00% since Oct 1, 2024 (LB 1023; previously 6.25%), car rental $8 per contract, plus liquor and similar permits. Enhanced Employment Area and Capitol District occupation taxes apply only to businesses inside those redevelopment districts. In the Capitol District, non-retail office users pay about $0.25 per sq ft of office space a year. That figure is from a search snippet of the city FAQ PDF, which returned 403 when I tried to read it. Head tax, unresolved: Municode still lists Article XIII, the business occupational privilege tax ($2/month per owner, partner, manager or employee, paid by the business), and Article XIV, the employee occupational privilege tax ($2/month withheld from each employee earning at least $250/month). Neither appears as a revenue line in the 2025-2027 budget tables, which list each occupation tax separately, or on the Finance Department's forms list. So they are likely not collected now, but I could not confirm that directly. If collected, they would add about $24 per worker per year at most; count that in expenses as a payroll cost. Local sales tax is 1.5% (7.0% combined) and is passed through; SaaS is generally not taxable in Nebraska. Omaha has no local income tax.

calculatorOption.label: Omaha
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Omaha has no business license or receipts tax on software or services; its occupation taxes cover only restaurants, hotels, telecom, tobacco and car rental.

jurisdictions.name: Lincoln, NE
jurisdictions.otherNotes: The City Treasurer's occupation tax page lists only industry-specific or district taxes: car rental 4%, hotel/motel 4%, restaurant/bar 2%, short-term rental 4%, telecommunications 4% of gross receipts. Two Enhanced Employment Area taxes apply only to businesses physically inside those retail districts: Gateway/Shops at Lincoln at 0.5% of all gross receipts and SouthPointe Pavilions at 1% of all gross receipts. An office-based software firm elsewhere in Lincoln owes none of these. Lincoln has no general business license, gross receipts tax or head tax. Local sales tax is 1.75% (7.25% combined) and is passed through; SaaS is generally not taxable in Nebraska. Lincoln has no local income tax. I found no other Nebraska city with a general receipts or business tax that reaches software or services companies; Nebraska city occupation taxes are industry-specific (restaurants, hotels, telecom) or limited to EEA districts.

calculatorOption.label: Lincoln
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Lincoln has no business license or receipts tax on software or services; its occupation taxes cover only hotels, restaurants, telecom, car and short-term rentals, and two retail districts.

jurisdictions.name: Nevada
jurisdictions.taxYear: Commerce Tax taxable year July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 (return due Aug 14, 2026); the same rates apply to FY 2026-27. Secretary of State fees are current as of Oct 2026. MBT rate is from the Dec 2025 return form.

receiptsTaxes.name: Commerce Tax (NRS 363C)
receiptsTaxes.base: Nevada gross revenue for the July 1 to June 30 taxable year, MINUS $4,000,000. Service revenue is sitused to Nevada in proportion to where the purchaser gets the benefit, i.e. market-based (NRS 363C.220). The rate applies only to the amount over $4M (NRS 363C.300).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Nevada-sitused gross revenue (not total revenue everywhere)
receiptsTaxes.notes: The rate depends on the business category that produces the most Nevada gross revenue (NRS 363C.097). SaaS and software publishers (NAICS 512/513/516/518, 'publishing, software and data processing', NRS 363C.430, amended 2025): 0.253%. Professional, scientific and technical services, including custom programming and IT consulting (NAICS 54, NRS 363C.460): 0.181%. Administrative and support services (NAICS 561): 0.154%. Formula: tax = rate x (NV gross revenue - $4,000,000). Since the 2019 SB 497 change, businesses with $4M or less of Nevada gross revenue do not file. Out-of-state businesses need both a minimum connection with Nevada and more than $4M of NV gross revenue. 50% of Commerce Tax paid is a non-refundable credit against the Modified Business Tax. Nevada is about 0.96% of US population, so a national seller needs roughly $400M+ of total revenue to cross the threshold. In practice this never bites a startup.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual List of Officers fee (foreign corporation, NRS 80.110)
fixedAnnual.notes: Tiered by the 'value' of authorized shares, computed at a minimum par of $0.001/share (no-par shares count at $1/share). $75,000 or less: $150. Over $75k to $200k: $200. Over $200k to $500k: $300. Over $500k to $1M: $400. Then +$275 per additional $500k, max $11,125. A typical Delaware startup with 75M or fewer authorized shares at par $0.00001-$0.0001 pays $150. Late fee is $75.

fixedAnnual.name: State Business License fee (NRS Ch. 76)
fixedAnnual.notes: $500/yr for domestic and foreign profit corporations, paid with the annual list. Late fee is $100. In the first year there is also a one-time foreign qualification fee ($75 at the lowest authorized-share tier) and a $150 initial list. Registered agent fees are extra and not included.

profitTaxes.name: No corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Nevada has no corporate or personal income tax. The Commerce Tax, a receipts tax, takes its place for large businesses.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll (already counted in expenses): the Modified Business Tax for general business is 1.17% of quarterly gross wages, after deducting employer-paid health benefits, above a $50,000 per quarter exclusion (rate cut from 1.378% effective July 1, 2023; the Dec 2025 return form still shows .0117). Returns are quarterly and must be filed even when no tax is due. State unemployment insurance (DETR) also applies; its rate was not researched here. Sales tax: the Department of Taxation FAQ says electronically delivered software and digital products are not subject to Nevada sales/use tax. SaaS is therefore pass-through-free here, but software on physical media is taxable. Counties levy business personal property tax on equipment such as computers, assessed by the county assessor. It is not a receipts tax and not quantified here. Local business license fees (see the city/county entries) apply only where you have a place of business. Most southern Nevada jurisdictions charge a semiannual gross-revenue license of about 0.056% of the location's revenue. Reno charges 0.085% and Sparks 0.1%.

calculatorOption.label: Nevada
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Nevada: $650/yr ($150 annual list + $500 state business license), plus a 0.253% Commerce Tax only once Nevada-sourced revenue tops $4M a year; the real tax is on the excess over $4M only.

jurisdictions.name: Las Vegas, NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: LVMC Chapter 6.04 as codified through Supplement 61 (posted July 2026); rates unchanged since Ord. 6327 (2014)

receiptsTaxes.name: City business license fee, gross-sales based (LVMC 6.04.005)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross sales/revenue of the business licensed at a fixed place of business in the City, billed semiannually on the prior six months' gross. The definition (LVMC 6.02.010) has no market-sourcing or apportionment, so for a company whose only office is in Las Vegas this is effectively all of its revenue.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Semiannual fee by semiannual gross: $0-30k $55. $30,001-180k $100. $180,001-300k $200. $300,001-540k $300. $540,001-720k $400. $720,001-900k $500. $900,001-1.08M $600. $1,080,001-1.25M $700. Over $1.25M: gross x 0.00056 on the full amount. That works out to about 0.056% of revenue, slightly higher in the low brackets (up to about 0.11% just above a bracket edge). SaaS/software is not in any fixed-fee category, so it defaults to this schedule (6.04.005(A)). The 'Internet retailer' category (sells digital goods or services primarily online) is also gross-sales based unless the business elects a $5,000/yr fixed fee (6.02.150(D)-(E)). An 'Administrative or corporate office space' may elect a $200/yr fixed fee instead. The first semiannual fee for a new gross-sales license is the greater of $100 or the industry's average semiannual fee (6.02.180). A one-time $50 processing fee applies (6.02.085). A license is issued only to a fixed place of business in the City (6.02.120).

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum gross-sales license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $55 per semiannual period while semiannual gross is $30,000 or less. One-time $50 processing fee not included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Applies only if you have an office or other fixed place of business inside the City of Las Vegas limits. Many 'Las Vegas' mailing addresses (the Strip/Paradise, Enterprise, Spring Valley, Summerlin South) are actually unincorporated Clark County, which has its own nearly identical schedule (see the Clark County entry). There is no city payroll or head tax, and no city sales tax on SaaS.

calculatorOption.label: Las Vegas
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Las Vegas city license: about 0.056% of your Las Vegas office's total revenue (not market-sourced), $110/yr minimum; only if you have an office inside city limits.

jurisdictions.name: Henderson, NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Henderson Municipal Code Chapter 4.05 as codified through Supplement 59 (posted Sept 2026); schedule from Ord. 3291 (2015)

receiptsTaxes.name: Gross revenues business license (HMC 4.05.010 / 4.05.410)
receiptsTaxes.base: Semiannual gross revenues of the business at its fixed place of business in the city. Goods count if 'originating in the city regardless of destination'; services count at the total amount charged (HMC 4.04.010). Not market-apportioned.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Semiannual fee by semiannual gross: $0-12k $25. $12k-18k $35. $18k-24k $42. $24k-30k $54. $30k-45k $66. $45k-90k $78. $90k-135k $90. $135k-180k $100. $180k-240k $120. $240k-300k $167. $300k-360k $200. $360k-420k $230. $420k-480k $270. $480k-540k $300. $540k-600k $350. $600k-660k $370. $660k-720k $400. $720k-780k $440. $780k-840k $470. $840k-900k $500. $900k-960k $540. $960k-1.02M $570. $1.02M-1.08M $600. $1.08M-1.14M $640. $1.14M-1.2M $670. Over $1.2M: full total x 0.00056. Software/SaaS is not an enumerated fixed-fee category, so it pays on gross revenue (4.05.410). Flat alternatives exist for other activities: 'Management, marketing, or consulting service' is $75 semiannual, and 'Office only' (an office not conducting an enumerated business) is $50 semiannual. A one-time $25 application fee per license classification applies (4.04.065). A fixed place of business is generally required (4.04.020(B)).

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum gross-revenue license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 per semiannual period while semiannual gross is $12,000 or less. One-time $25 application fee not included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Applies only with a business location in Henderson. HMC 4.05.010(B) also reaches businesses outside the city 'providing services within the city' that are not otherwise classified. It is aimed at on-site service providers; whether it reaches remote SaaS sellers is untested and probably not. There is no city payroll tax, and no sales tax on SaaS.

calculatorOption.label: Henderson
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Henderson city license: about 0.056% of your Henderson office's total revenue, $50/yr minimum; only if you have an office in Henderson.

jurisdictions.name: Reno, NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: City of Reno FY 2026/2027 adopted business license fees (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027)

receiptsTaxes.name: Annual gross receipts business license fee (RMC Title 4; fee schedule per RMC 4.04.110)
receiptsTaxes.base: Annual gross receipts for goods sold or services performed within the city (RMC 4.04.008). Receipts from sales/services performed beyond city limits are excluded only where another political subdivision requires a license for them. For a company operating from Reno this is likely most or all of its revenue.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Reno gross receipts (the rate applies to the excess over $100,000)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Annual fee: $0-20,000 $70. $20,001-100,000 $150. $100,001-5,000,000: $150 + 0.085% of the amount over $100,000. Over $5,000,000: $4,315 + 0.065% of the amount over $5M. Distribution, manufacturing and warehouse businesses instead pay by square footage. A one-time application processing fee applies: $40 commercial, $25 home-based. Commercial locations may also face one-time planning ($90) and building ($90) reviews and a $105 fire inspection. Whether the fire inspection is annual was not verified.

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum gross-receipts license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: For gross receipts of $20,000 or less. It is $150 between $20,001 and $100,000. One-time processing and inspection fees are not included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Applies to businesses doing business within Reno city limits. Unincorporated Washoe County and Sparks license separately. There is no city payroll tax, and no sales tax on SaaS.

calculatorOption.label: Reno
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Reno city license: $70/yr, plus 0.085% of Reno gross receipts over $100k (0.065% over $5M); assumes all revenue of a Reno-based office counts.

jurisdictions.name: Clark County (unincorporated), NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Clark County Code Title 6 as codified through Supplement 149 (posted Sept 2026); schedule from Ord. 2422 (1999)

receiptsTaxes.name: County business license, gross revenue schedule (CCC 6.12.340 computer and data processing; 6.12.995 schedule)
receiptsTaxes.base: Semiannual gross revenue of the business at a fixed place of business in unincorporated Clark County, 'regardless of place of delivery'. A business taxable inside and outside the state/county may elect three-factor apportionment (property, payroll, sales; services sourced by cost of performance) under CCC 6.08.100. For a startup whose people and property are all in the county, that is still about 100%.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: CCC 6.12.340 puts 'sales or service of computers or related computer programming services' on the gross schedule. Semiannual fee by semiannual gross: $0-12k $25. $12k-18k $30. $18k-24k $42. $24k-30k $54. $30k-45k $66. $45k-90k $78. $90k-135k $90. $135k-180k $100. $180k-240k $120. $240k-300k $167. $300k-360k $200. $360k-420k $230. $420k-480k $270. $480k-540k $300. $540k-600k $350. $600k-660k $370. $660k-720k $400. $720k-780k $440. $780k-840k $470. $840k-900k $500. $900k-960k $540. $960k-1.02M $570. $1.02M-1.08M $600. $1.08M-1.14M $640. $1.14M-1.2M $670. Over $1.2M: 0.05555%. Flat alternatives: 'Consultant service' $200/yr, 'Management service' $150/yr, 'Administrative office space' $150/yr. A one-time $45 application processing fee applies (CCC 6.08).

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum gross-revenue license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 per semiannual period while semiannual gross is $12,000 or less. One-time $45 processing fee not included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Covers only unincorporated areas: the Strip/Paradise, Enterprise, Spring Valley, Winchester, Sunrise Manor, Summerlin South and others. Many 'Las Vegas' addresses fall here. Businesses inside Las Vegas, Henderson or North Las Vegas city limits license with the city instead. There is no county payroll tax.

calculatorOption.label: Clark County (unincorporated)
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Unincorporated Clark County license: about 0.056% of your office's total revenue, $50/yr minimum; only if your office is outside city limits (e.g. on the Strip).

jurisdictions.name: North Las Vegas, NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: NLVMC Chapter 5.02 as codified through Supplement 146 (posted Sept 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Gross monthly income business license (NLVMC 5.02.080)
receiptsTaxes.base: Semiannual gross sales/revenues of the business. Goods and services count if 'originating in the City without any regard to their final destination' (NLVMC 5.02.001), so it is location-based, not market-sourced.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Unless otherwise specified, every business pays semiannually on gross. The schedule matches Clark County's: $25 for $0-12k semiannual, rising in steps to $670 at $1.14M-1.2M, then 0.0005555 x gross above $1.2M. Fees are due Jan 31 and Jul 31 on the preceding half-year, and no fee is under $25. For unlisted businesses the director chooses a fixed or gross-based fee (5.02.320). A one-time $30 processing fee applies (5.02.035).

fixedAnnual.name: Minimum gross-revenue license fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 per semiannual period. One-time $30 processing fee not included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Applies only with a place of business in North Las Vegas. There is no city payroll tax.

calculatorOption.label: North Las Vegas
calculatorOption.assumptionText: North Las Vegas license: about 0.056% of your North Las Vegas office's total revenue, $50/yr minimum; only if you have an office there.

jurisdictions.name: Sparks, NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Sparks Municipal Code 5.12.100 as codified through Supplement 24 (posted Sept 2025)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license fee (SMC 5.12.100)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts from sales within city limits and from services performed within city limits (SMC 5.04.030).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Sparks gross receipts (the $1 per $1,000 applies to the excess over $10,000)
receiptsTaxes.notes: $80 per year plus $1.00 for each $1,000 (or portion) of gross receipts over $10,000, i.e. 0.1% on the excess. There is also a $4/yr regional technology fee (SMC 5.12.103) and a one-time $25 processing fee. This is the highest general receipts rate found among Nevada localities.

fixedAnnual.name: Base license fee + regional technology fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $80 base + $4 technology fee. One-time $25 processing fee not included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Applies to businesses engaged in business within Sparks (Reno's neighbor in Washoe County). The 'within city limits' services base is ambiguous for a SaaS company whose staff work in Sparks but whose customers are elsewhere; treat it as its whole revenue to be conservative. There is no city payroll tax.

calculatorOption.label: Sparks
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Sparks city license: $84/yr, plus 0.1% of Sparks gross receipts over $10k; assumes all revenue of a Sparks-based office counts.

jurisdictions.name: Carson City, NV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Carson City Municipal Code 4.04.020/4.04.040 (codified version posted Aug 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Business license fee, 'all other businesses' (CCMC 4.04.020)
fixedAnnual.notes: Flat $63.85/yr. 'Out-of-town businesses' pay $79.90/yr. One-time $25 application fee.

fixedAnnual.name: Per-employee fee (CCMC 4.04.040)
fixedAnnual.notes: $6.15 per full-time-equivalent employee, including the holder, for the first 100 FTEs, then $2.85 each. Shown here for 1 FTE.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Checked: Carson City (the consolidated state capital) has no gross receipts license fee for ordinary businesses (only cannabis businesses pay 3% of gross). The cost is a small flat fee plus a per-employee charge. There is no payroll tax beyond that, and no sales tax on SaaS.

calculatorOption.label: Carson City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Carson City: no receipts tax; about $70/yr flat license ($63.85 + $6.15 per employee, shown for 1).

jurisdictions.name: New Hampshire
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026 (BPT/BET rates per statute; filing thresholds for taxable periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025, which are adjusted only every two years, so they also cover 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (foreign corporation with a certificate of authority)
fixedAnnual.notes: RSA 293-A:1.22(b)(8) sets the fee at $100, the same for domestic and foreign corporations. It is due between Jan 1 and Apr 1 each year (RSA 293-A:16.21). Paying late adds $50 (RSA 293-A:1.22(a)(17)). Secondary sources say filing online through NH QuickStart costs $102 because of a $2 processing fee; I could not reach the SOS site to confirm that. A foreign corporation that gets its certificate of authority between Dec 1 and Apr 1 skips that year's report. Registering in the first place costs a one-time $100 certificate-of-authority fee, which is not recurring.

profitTaxes.name: Business Profits Tax (BPT)
profitTaxes.notes: 7.5% for taxable periods ending on or after Dec 31, 2023 (RSA 77-A:2, III). Profits are apportioned by a single sales factor with market-based sourcing (a service is sourced where it is delivered, intangibles where they are used) for periods ending on or after Dec 31, 2022 (RSA 77-A:3, I(b)). There is no minimum tax. A return is required once gross business income everywhere exceeds $109,000 for periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025, even if there is no profit (DRA figure, read via search excerpts because the DRA site blocked direct access; the statute's base amount is $92,000, indexed every two years). BET paid is credited against BPT, and unused credit carries forward 10 taxable periods (RSA 77-A:5, X). That means BET paid before profitability can be recovered against BPT later.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: BUSINESS ENTERPRISE TAX (BET) is the one New Hampshire tax that costs money before profit, but it is measured by payroll, not receipts. The rate is 0.55% of the taxable enterprise value tax base for periods ending on or after Dec 31, 2022 (RSA 77-E:2, II). The base is compensation paid or accrued, plus interest paid or accrued, plus dividends paid (RSA 77-E:1, IX). Each part is apportioned separately (RSA 77-E:4): compensation by the share of compensation paid for services performed in NH, interest by the NH property share, and dividends by a three-factor average. In practice, for a pre-profit startup with no debt and no dividends, BET is about 0.55% of wages paid to NH-based employees. Example: one NH employee earning $150k means roughly $825 a year. If the company has no NH payroll or property (it only sells into NH), BET is about $0. Whether you must file depends on everywhere totals, not apportioned ones: total gross business receipts over $298,000, OR total enterprise value tax base (roughly total payroll everywhere) over $298,000, for periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025. That figure is from DRA, read via search excerpts; NHPR reported it as $297,000, but DRA's figure governs. Most VC-backed startups with staff will cross the payroll test even with no revenue. HB 155 (2026 Laws ch. 280) raises both thresholds to $400,000 for tax years beginning Jan 1, 2027. It also sets up an automatic trigger that cuts the BET rate by 0.005 percentage points each time collections beat estimates by $100M, down to a 0.25% floor. No cut has happened yet, so 0.55% is current. Estimated BET payments are required once estimated tax exceeds $260 (RSA 77-E:5, II). Because BET scales with NH headcount rather than revenue, it fits the calculator's expenses (as an add-on to NH payroll), not a revenue rate. OTHER: New Hampshire has no general sales or use tax, so there is no SaaS sales tax to collect. The Interest and Dividends Tax was repealed for tax years beginning Jan 1, 2025, and never applied to a C corporation's operations. There is no state personal income tax on wages. Employers pay state unemployment insurance (a payroll expense).
sources: https://www.revenue.nh.gov/resource-center/frequently-asked-questions/business-enterprise-tax (403 to direct fetch; content read via search-result excerpts only)
https://www.revenue.nh.gov/resource-center/frequently-asked-questions/business-profits-tax (403 to direct fetch; content read via search-result excerpts only)

calculatorOption.label: New Hampshire
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax in New Hampshire; $100/yr annual report as a registered foreign corporation; the 0.55% Business Enterprise Tax falls on NH-based payroll (about $825/yr per $150k NH salary), so count it with expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Manchester, NH
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Manchester has no local income, receipts or payroll tax. New Hampshire is a Dillon's Rule state, and its cities and towns are authorized to levy property taxes only (secondary source: NH Fiscal Policy Institute). New Hampshire also has no tax on business personal property, so an office lease or equipment brings no local tax beyond whatever the landlord passes through in rent. The city's business license (Code of Ordinances ch. 110, §110.02) covers only the activities it lists: common victualers and food service, junk and second-hand dealers, pawnbrokers, hotels and inns, high-impact retail, tattoo parlors, taxi and TNC companies, towing, employment offices, circuses and carnivals, arcades and dance halls, peddlers, fairs and similar. Software/SaaS and professional-services offices are not on the list, so no city license fee applies. I read that list via search excerpts of the American Legal Publishing code; both the code site and manchesternh.gov refused direct connections. No other New Hampshire city has a local receipts or business tax, for the same reason.
sources: https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/manchester/latest/manchester_nh/0-0-0-3996 (403 to direct fetch; §110.02 text read via search-result excerpt)

calculatorOption.label: Manchester
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Manchester has no local receipts, income or payroll tax, and its business license doesn't cover software or services offices.

jurisdictions.name: New Jersey
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2025 (2025 CBT-100 instructions, the latest published). I found no 2026 change to the minimum-tax schedule or the annual report fee.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporation Business Tax (CBT) minimum tax
fixedAnnual.notes: A company with a net loss pays the minimum tax instead of the income tax. The minimum is set by New Jersey-sourced gross receipts (Schedule J line 6, market-sourced): under $100k pays $500; $100k to under $250k pays $750; $250k to under $500k pays $1,000; $500k to under $1M pays $1,500; $1M or more pays $2,000. Two special cases: if the company files a separate return and belongs to an affiliated or controlled group (IRC 1504/1563) whose total payroll is $5M or more, the minimum is $2,000 no matter what its NJ receipts are. Short first years are not prorated, and $0 returns are generally not allowed. Who has to file: every foreign corporation holding a NJ certificate of authority, plus any corporation with economic nexus (NJ receipts over $100k, or 200+ transactions delivered to NJ customers). Registering alone triggers the $500. If the prior year's liability was over $1,500, quarterly estimated payments are required.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report fee (Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services)
fixedAnnual.notes: $75 a year for both domestic and foreign for-profit corporations. Due by the last day of the anniversary month of formation or authorization. There is also a one-time $100 fee for a foreign corporation's certificate of authority (not annual).

profitTaxes.name: Corporation Business Tax (net income)
profitTaxes.notes: 9% when entire net income is over $100k; 7.5% for $50,001-$100k; 6.5% for $50k or less. The reduced rates apply to the whole income, not brackets. Services are apportioned by a single receipts factor with market sourcing (where the benefit is received). Mandatory unitary combined reporting since 2019. Owed only when it exceeds the minimum tax, so it is zero before profit.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate Transit Fee (CBT surtax)
profitTaxes.notes: 2.5% for privilege periods beginning 1/1/2024 through 12/31/2028. Applies only when NJ allocated taxable net income is over $10M, and then to the entire amount (a cliff, not just the excess), for 11.5% in total. Zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
New Jersey has no state gross receipts or margin tax. Before profit, the only cost is the fixed minimum CBT plus the annual report fee.

Sales tax (6.625%) is pass-through and not counted. Per TB-72, pure SaaS is not taxable because no software is transferred. SaaS that is an 'information service' is taxable (information collected, compiled or analyzed by the seller, e.g. Westlaw/LexisNexis-type products). Electronically delivered prewritten software is taxable unless the buyer uses it exclusively in its business. Installing and servicing prewritten software is taxable. Professional services (consulting, etc.) and truly custom software are not taxable.

Payroll costs belong in expenses: employer UI, disability and family leave contributions, plus the Newark and Jersey City 1% employer payroll taxes for staff there.

Local taxes: NJ municipalities can levy only state-authorized taxes. I found no NJ city with a general receipts or business-privilege tax. The Jan 2026 OLS committee statement on S4219 says only Newark and Jersey City (population over 200,000) impose an employer payroll tax under the Local Tax Authorization Act. Some towns (e.g. Atlantic City) have mercantile licenses; I did not research their amounts.

calculatorOption.label: New Jersey
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $500 New Jersey minimum corporation tax (for NJ receipts under $100k; it steps up to $2,000 at $1M+ of NJ receipts) plus the $75 annual report; no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Newark, NJ
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Newark has no gross receipts or business-privilege tax. It has an employer payroll tax: 1% of payroll for services performed in Newark, or supervised from Newark, filed quarterly. This belongs in expenses, not here. State law (Local Tax Authorization Act, N.J.S.A. 40:48C) caps it at 1% (confirmed by the Jan 2026 OLS statement on S4219). Newark's own pages describe a reduced 0.5% rate for employers whose workforce is more than 50% Newark residents. I only saw that in search-result snippets: newarknj.gov and ecode360 blocked automated reads, so I could not verify it directly. Hotel and parking taxes do not apply to a SaaS company. I found no recurring general business license fee for an office-based software firm, but I could not confirm this from the city's code.

calculatorOption.label: Newark
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Newark has no receipts tax; its 1% employer payroll tax belongs in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Jersey City, NJ
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Jersey City has no gross receipts or business tax. It has an employer payroll tax (Ord. 18-133, since 1/1/2019): 1% of gross payroll for employers located in Jersey City, filed quarterly. Wages of Jersey City residents are exempt, and so are employers with quarterly gross payroll under $2,500. This belongs in expenses, not here. The tax was challenged in Mack-Cali Realty v. State. Per secondary sources, the Appellate Division found it unconstitutional in 2021, and the NJ Supreme Court in 2022 affirmed and sent it back to the lower court for discovery. I did not read those opinions. The city's FAQ still lists the tax as in force. Property, hotel and parking taxes do not apply. I found no recurring general business license fee for an office-based software firm, but I did not confirm this from the city code.

calculatorOption.label: Jersey City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Jersey City has no receipts tax; its 1% employer payroll tax (non-resident wages) belongs in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: New Mexico
jurisdictions.taxYear: GRT rates for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (state rate 4.875%); corporate income and franchise tax for tax year 2025 (5.9% flat rate from 2025); Secretary of State biennial report fee as charged in 2025

receiptsTaxes.name: Gross receipts tax (GRT), state rate plus local option increments
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts sourced to New Mexico. SaaS and downloaded software are licenses of a digital good, which New Mexico treats as property, not a service. Those receipts are sourced by destination: the delivery location, or the buyer's address in the seller's records. The rate is the combined rate at that location. Non-professional services also go by destination (where the product of the service is delivered). Professional services (work that needs a state license or a master's degree or higher) are sourced to the seller's location. For an out-of-state seller that is code 88-888, state rate only (4.875%). Receipts from software or services used outside New Mexico are not New Mexico receipts.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Applies only to sellers with no physical presence in New Mexico: taxable receipts sourced to New Mexico of $100,000 or more in the previous calendar year. A company with a New Mexico office or employee owes GRT from the first dollar of New Mexico-sourced receipts.
receiptsTaxes.notes: The rate shown, 7.625%, is Albuquerque's combined rate (largest market). July 2026 to June 2027 combined rates from TRD's official GIS layer: Albuquerque 7.625%, Santa Fe city 8.1875%, Las Cruces 8.39%, Rio Rancho 7.4375% (Sandoval County part) and 7.875% (Bernalillo County part), Farmington 8.1875%, Los Alamos 7.6875%, Roswell 8.2708%. Non-tribal rates run from 5.25% to 9.4375%. Out-of-state professional services (code 88-888) and out-of-state R&D services (code 77-777) are at 4.875%. Legally GRT is a tax on the seller for the privilege of doing business, so the seller owes it whether or not it bills the customer. TRD says it is common to pass it on, and when you do it must be separately stated on the invoice. SaaS contracts and sales-tax engines normally add it to NM invoices like a sales tax. That makes it a pass-through for most SaaS startups, so the calculator option leaves it out. If a company quotes tax-inclusive prices or doesn't bill it, it absorbs roughly 7.6% to 8.4% of NM-sourced revenue in the major cities. All city and county GRT is part of this one state-administered return; no New Mexico city has a separate receipts tax. Returns are generally due on the 25th of the month after the reporting period.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate franchise tax
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 a year, reported on Form CIT-1. Owed by every domestic or foreign corporation engaging in business in NM or having or exercising its corporate franchise in NM, whether actively engaged in business or not, even with no income tax due. Also owed by corporations immune from income tax under P.L. 86-272. Each corporation in a filing group pays $50.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State biennial corporate report
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 filing fee every two years (shown as $12.50 a year), required of domestic and foreign profit corporations. A $25 first report is also due within 30 days of qualifying. The late penalty is $200. The biennial report is due by the 15th day of the third month after the end of the tax year according to 12.3.2 NMAC (secondary filing services say the fourth month).

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 5.9% from tax year 2025; before that it was 4.8% on the first $500k and 5.9% above. Worldwide combined reporting is the default unless water's-edge or federal consolidated is elected. Income is apportioned under UDITPA using a three-factor formula (property, payroll, sales), with special elections for manufacturers and headquarters. NOLs carry forward 20 years. Zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll items (already counted in expenses): NM state income tax withholding, state unemployment insurance (SUTA), and the Workers' Compensation Administration fee. The fee is $4.30 per covered employee per quarter, of which $2.30 is the employer's share, $2.00 is withheld from the employee, and the rest goes to the Uninsured Employers' Fund. That split comes from secondary and older TRD sources and was not re-checked for 2026. Compensating tax (NM's use tax) is owed on purchases used in NM when the vendor didn't charge GRT, for example software tools bought from vendors that don't collect NM GRT. It is a cost on purchases, not on revenue. GRT also has a statewide address-to-rate lookup service, built by TRD and UNM EDAC at grt.edacnm.org. No New Mexico city or county has a separate receipts or business-privilege tax; local GRT increments are collected through the state GRT return. City business registration or license fees (about $35 a year) apply only to premises in that city. Las Cruces, the second-largest city, combined GRT 8.39%, has no other business tax. Its $35 annual business registration fee for a place of business inside the city comes from a search snippet of the city code only. One-time costs (not annual): the foreign corporation qualification filing with the Secretary of State and the $25 first report.

calculatorOption.label: New Mexico
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $50 franchise tax plus a $25 report every two years; New Mexico's gross receipts tax (4.875% state, about 7.6% to 8.4% in major cities) is assumed itemized on NM invoices like sales tax.

jurisdictions.name: Albuquerque, NM
jurisdictions.taxYear: City fiscal year starting July 1, 2026 (license fee $36.75 from July 1, 2026); GRT rate for July 2026 to June 2027

fixedAnnual.name: City business license
fixedAnnual.notes: $36.75 a year from July 1, 2026 ($35 before that). Required from July 1, 2025 to operate a place of business inside city limits, including home-based businesses; one license and fee per location. It replaced the old business registration. Late renewal can cost $10 a day. A Fire Marshal life-safety inspection fee also applies to most commercial premises when licensing: $35 up to 1,500 sq ft, $100 for 1,501 to 6,000, $250 for 6,001 to 12,000, $400 above that. The city doesn't say whether the inspection recurs every year, so it is left out of the total. A company with no premises in Albuquerque owes nothing.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city income tax, payroll tax or separate gross receipts tax. Albuquerque's combined GRT rate is 7.625% (location code 02-100, TRD July 2026 to June 2027 layer): 4.875% state plus municipal and Bernalillo County increments. It is filed on the state GRT return and is normally invoiced to customers (see the New Mexico entry), so it is not counted here. Receipts are destination-sourced, so the Albuquerque rate applies to SaaS delivered to Albuquerque customers. It also applies to professional services sold from an Albuquerque office.

calculatorOption.label: Albuquerque
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $36.75 city business license if you have premises in Albuquerque; its 7.625% combined gross receipts tax is assumed passed to customers.

jurisdictions.name: Santa Fe, NM
jurisdictions.taxYear: City fee schedule last updated 5/26/2020 (latest published); GRT rate for July 2026 to June 2027

fixedAnnual.name: City business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Standard business license $35, required of anyone conducting business in Santa Fe city limits. Renewable licenses last one year from payment; non-renewable licenses expire each calendar year. Late fee $10. The schedule also lists a $10 'Out of Jurisdiction' license, probably for outside businesses working in the city. Whether a remote SaaS seller with no presence needs it is unclear, and it isn't counted. Fee schedule dated 2020.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual fire inspection
fixedAnnual.notes: $30 a year for premises of 1,500 sq ft or less; $50 for 1,501 to 3,000; $100 for 3,001 to 6,000; $150 for 6,001 to 9,000; $200 above 9,000. A one-time certificate of occupancy inspection is also charged: $75 for 3,000 sq ft or less, $175 for a home occupation. Applies only with premises in the city.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city income, payroll or separate receipts tax. Santa Fe city's combined GRT rate is 8.1875% (location code 01-123, TRD July 2026 to June 2027 layer). It is filed on the state GRT return and normally invoiced to customers (see the New Mexico entry), so it is not counted. Lodgers' tax applies only to lodging. Amounts are from a fee schedule last updated in 2020, so confidence is medium.

calculatorOption.label: Santa Fe
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $35 city business license plus a $30 annual fire inspection if you have small premises in Santa Fe; its 8.1875% combined gross receipts tax is assumed passed to customers.

jurisdictions.name: New York
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2025 (2025 Form CT-3/CT-3-I/CT-3-M, the latest published). The fixed-dollar-minimum table, 0.1875% capital rate and 30% MTA surcharge are statutory and also apply to 2026 (Tax Law §§209-B, 210 as currently in force).

fixedAnnual.name: Article 9-A fixed dollar minimum (FDM) franchise tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Tax due is the LARGEST of three bases: business income (zero while losing money), capital, and the FDM. The FDM is set by New York receipts (receipts sourced to NY by customer location). 2025 table for C corps: up to $100k: $25; $100k-250k: $75; $250k-500k: $175; $500k-1M: $500; $1M-5M: $1,500; $5M-25M: $3,500; $25M-50M: $5,000; $50M-100M: $10,000; $100M-250M: $20,000; $250M-500M: $50,000; $500M-1B: $100,000; over $1B: $200,000. Qualified emerging technology companies (QETCs) and qualified NY manufacturers use a lower table: $19 / $56 / $131 / $375 / $1,125 / $2,625 / $3,750 (over $25M). Short years are reduced 50% (6 months or less) or 25% (more than 6 and up to 9 months). The $25 shown is for a pre-revenue startup or one with NY receipts of $100k or less.

fixedAnnual.name: Department of State biennial statement (BCL §408)
fixedAnnual.notes: $9 every two years (BCL §104-A), due from domestic corporations and foreign corporations authorized to do business in NY. Shown as $4.50 a year. The one-time application for authority for a Delaware corp to qualify in NY is $225 (BCL §104-A). That fee isn't recurring, so it's excluded.

fixedAnnual.name: MTA surcharge on the franchise tax (only if in the MCTD)
fixedAnnual.notes: Applies only to corporations doing business, keeping an office, or deriving receipts in the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District: NYC's five boroughs plus Dutchess, Nassau, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Suffolk and Westchester. The rate is 30% (Tax Law §209-B, tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2024; CT-3-M line 4). It's charged on the NY franchise tax (the largest base, before credits) times the MCTD apportionment percentage, which averages three factors: property, receipts (MCTD receipts over NY receipts) and payroll. At the $25 FDM the surcharge is at most $7.50. This amount is counted in the New York City calculator option, not in this state option, because it only applies inside the MCTD.

profitTaxes.name: Article 9-A business income base tax
profitTaxes.notes: 6.5% of NY-apportioned business income. 7.25% if the business income base exceeds $5M. QETCs pay 4.875%; qualified NY manufacturers pay 0%. Apportionment uses a single receipts factor with customer sourcing. It's zero while losing money, and NOLs carry forward.

profitTaxes.name: MTA surcharge on income-based tax (MCTD only)
profitTaxes.notes: 30% of the NY tax apportioned to the MCTD. At the 6.5% rate that equals 1.95% of MCTD-apportioned income (2.175% at the 7.25% rate). It also applies to the FDM or capital-base tax when one of those is the tax due.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: CAPITAL BASE: this is the item most likely to cost a funded pre-profit startup more than the FDM. The capital base tax is 0.1875% of business capital (average total assets at FMV minus liabilities, minus investment capital) times the NY business apportionment factor (NY receipts over total receipts). Under §210(1)(b) that rate runs through tax years beginning before 1/1/2030, then drops to 0%. The tax is capped at $5M. When it exceeds the FDM, it replaces the FDM. Investment capital is limited to qualifying stock held more than a year, so a startup's cash and short-term holdings should count as business capital (Inferred from the CT-3 Part 4/5 structure; not confirmed against a ruling). Example: $10M average net assets x 5.85% NY receipts share x 0.1875% = about $1,100/yr instead of $25. The rate is 0% for 'small business taxpayers' (§210(1)(f): entire net income of $390k or less, total money and property received for stock / capital contributions / paid-in surplus of $1M or less, 100 or fewer full-time NY employees, and not part of a larger affiliated group) and for QETCs. Most VC-backed companies fail the $1M capital-contribution test. A QETC is a company located in NY whose primary products/services are 'emerging technologies', a category that includes software and information and communication technology (Public Authorities Law §3102-e). For these rate benefits the $10M product-sales cap is ignored (CT-3-I). A NY-located software startup may qualify, which would give it a 0% capital rate and a lower FDM. NEXUS: a registered foreign corp with an office or employees in NY is taxable regardless of receipts. A remote seller is taxable once its NY receipts reach $1,283,000 (tax years 2024-2026). PASS-THROUGH SALES TAX: remotely accessed prewritten software (SaaS) is taxable in NY. State 4% plus local tax (8.875% in NYC, 8.75% in Erie County) is collected from customers and sourced by where users are located. Some 'information services' are also taxable. Most professional services are not. PAYROLL (already in expenses): MCTMT employer payroll tax inside the MCTD applies only if MCTD payroll exceeds $312,500 per quarter. From 7/1/2025, Zone 1 (NYC) rates by quarterly payroll are 0.055% up to $375k, 0.115% for $375k-437.5k, 0.60% for $437.5k-2.5M, and 0.895% above $2.5M. Zone 2 rates are the same except 0.34% and 0.635% for the top two brackets. NY unemployment insurance also applies. Employees pay disability and paid family leave. LOCAL: other than NYC, no NY city imposes a general business, receipts or corporate income tax. Cities may tax utilities' gross receipts (General City Law §20-b: up to 1%, or 3% in Buffalo, Rochester and Yonkers), which doesn't reach software companies.

calculatorOption.label: New York
calculatorOption.assumptionText: New York charges no receipts tax, but there's a $25 minimum franchise tax that steps up with NY receipts ($500 at $0.5-1M, $1,500 at $1-5M) plus a $9 biennial statement; a funded company that raised over $1M may instead owe 0.1875% of its NY-apportioned net assets if that's larger.

jurisdictions.name: New York City, NY
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2025 (2025 Form NYC-2 and instructions). The FDM table and rates are unchanged in the Administrative Code for 2026.

fixedAnnual.name: NYC Business Corporation Tax (BCT) fixed dollar minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: BCT due is the largest of: business income base (zero pre-profit), capital base, and the FDM based on NYC receipts (single receipts factor, customer-sourced). 2025 table, the same as the state's: up to $100k: $25; $100k-250k: $75; $250k-500k: $175; $500k-1M: $500; $1M-5M: $1,500; $5M-25M: $3,500; $25M-50M: $5,000; $50M-100M: $10,000; $100M-250M: $20,000; $250M-500M: $50,000; $500M-1B: $100,000; over $1B: $200,000. Short periods are annualized. The $25 shown is for a startup with $100k or less of NYC receipts.

fixedAnnual.name: NY State MTA surcharge on the state FDM (state tax, MCTD only)
fixedAnnual.notes: This is a New York State tax (Tax Law §209-B, 30%), but it applies only to companies in the MCTD, which includes all of NYC, so it's counted here. It equals 30% of the state franchise tax ($25 FDM) times the MCTD apportionment percentage, so the most it can be is $7.50. It scales with the state tax if the state FDM or capital base is higher.

profitTaxes.name: NYC Business Corporation Tax, business income base
profitTaxes.notes: 8.85% of NYC-allocated business income. Small corporations pay a lower rate that phases from 6.5% up to 8.85% by income (Schedule H), and qualified manufacturers 4.425% to 8.85%. It's zero while losing money.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: CAPITAL BASE: 0.15% of NYC-allocated business capital, minus a flat $10,000 reduction (floored at 0), with a $10M maximum (2025 NYC-2, Schedule C Part 3). It only exceeds zero when NYC-allocated net assets top about $6.67M, which is rare pre-profit. Example: $10M net assets x 2.5% NYC share gives $375 - $10,000 = $0. NEXUS: a company with an office or employees in NYC is taxable. A remote seller is taxable once its NYC receipts reach $1,128,000 (2025 NYC-2 instructions). C corporations file the BCT (NYC-2). The General Corporation Tax now applies only to S corporations. Corporations don't pay the Unincorporated Business Tax. COMMERCIAL RENT TAX (rent-based, already in expenses as rent): applies to premises in Manhattan south of 96th St with annualized base rent of $250,000 or more. The rate is 6% after a 35% base reduction, an effective 3.9%. It's fully credited away if total income is $5M or less and base rent is under $500k, with a partial credit up to $550k rent / $10M income. Bill S451 (2025) to widen the exemption covers only retail and food businesses and was still in committee. MCTMT employer payroll tax (Zone 1) is at the top of the state's MCTD rate table: up to 0.60%, or 0.895% on quarterly payroll above $2.5M from 7/1/2025. It's an expense item. SALES TAX (pass-through): SaaS and prewritten software sold to NYC users carry 8.875% (4% state, 4.5% city, 0.375% MCTD). NYC has no general business license or business-privilege tax for software or professional-services offices.

calculatorOption.label: New York City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: New York City charges no receipts tax: there's a $25 business corporation tax minimum that steps up with NYC receipts ($1,500 at $1-5M, $3,500 at $5-25M), plus up to $7.50 of state MTA surcharge on the NY minimum.

jurisdictions.name: Buffalo, NY
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Buffalo has no city corporate income tax, gross receipts tax or business-privilege tax. NY cities' local gross-receipts authority (General City Law §20-b, up to 3% for Buffalo) reaches only utilities. Buffalo issues licenses only for listed regulated business types, such as restaurants, contractors, collection agencies, amusements, and peddlers. No general business license applies to a software or professional-services office. That list comes from search-engine extracts of buffalony.gov; the city's license page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches, which is why confidence is medium. SALES TAX (pass-through): Erie County's combined rate is 8.75% (4% state + 4.75% county) on taxable sales, including SaaS sold to Buffalo users. No MTA surcharge or MCTMT applies, because Erie County is outside the MCTD. State-level Article 9-A taxes still apply.

calculatorOption.label: Buffalo
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Buffalo has no city business, receipts or income tax; the only local tax is Erie County sales tax, which customers pay.

jurisdictions.name: Yonkers, NY
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Yonkers has the only other city income taxes in NY, and both fall on individuals, not corporations. One is a 0.5% nonresident earnings tax on wages and self-employment earnings earned in Yonkers (Form Y-203, 2025). The other is a resident surcharge on NY state income tax (16.75% of net state tax, per tax.ny.gov materials seen only as search extracts). Employers withhold both, so they're payroll items borne by employees, not a business cost. Yonkers is in Westchester, so it's inside the MCTD: the state MTA surcharge (30% of the state franchise tax apportioned to the MCTD; at most $7.50 at the $25 minimum) and MCTMT Zone 2 apply. The combined sales tax is 8.875% (pass-through).

calculatorOption.label: Yonkers
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Yonkers taxes only individuals' wages (withheld from employees), so it adds no business tax beyond the state's MTA surcharge.

jurisdictions.name: North Carolina
jurisdictions.taxYear: Franchise tax: rate for taxable years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2025 (reported on 2024 and later CD-405 returns, prepaid for the following year). Income tax: 2.25% for 2025, 2.0% for 2026. Annual report fees: current G.S. 55-1-22 schedule.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate franchise tax (minimum)
fixedAnnual.notes: Tax on the privilege of doing business, owed whether or not there is profit, filed on Form CD-405. Base is net worth only: total assets with depreciation and amortization ignored, less total liabilities, under GAAP. The property-based alternative bases were removed for tax years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2023. Net worth is apportioned with the same single-sales-factor fraction used for income tax. C-corp rate is $1.50 per $1,000 (0.15%), capped at $500 on the first $1,000,000 of apportioned net worth, plus 0.15% above $1M. The minimum is $200. Worked through: $200 until NC-apportioned net worth exceeds about $133,333, then rises to $500 at about $333,333, flat $500 up to $1M, then 0.15% more. A nationally selling startup with $5M of net worth and about 3% NC sales has about $150k apportioned, so it pays about $225. A startup with mostly NC customers and a few $M of equity on the books could owe $500 to $2,000 or more. Net worth cannot drive the tax below $200, including when it is negative (e.g. SAFEs carried as liabilities). Source: G.S. 105-122(b), (c1), (d), (d2); 2025 CD-405 instructions.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (business corporation, domestic or foreign)
fixedAnnual.notes: G.S. 55-16-22 requires every foreign corporation authorized to do business in NC to file. It is due on the 15th day of the 4th month after fiscal year end. G.S. 55-1-22 sets the fee at $25 on paper or $18 electronic; the SOS FAQ lists online at $21 including the card fee. I used $25 to be conservative. The one-time $250 certificate of authority fee for registering as a foreign corporation is not annual.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 2.0% for taxable years beginning in 2026 and 2.25% in 2025 (NCDOR rate table; G.S. 105-130.3), phasing toward 0% after 2029. The statute text as published lists 2025 2.25%, 2026 2%, 2028 1%, after 2029 0%. Apportionment is a single sales factor. Service receipts are sourced where the service is delivered and intangibles where they are used (market-based). Zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
North Carolina has no gross receipts tax, and no local governments can levy business privilege license taxes. Both city authority (G.S. 160A-211) and county authority (G.S. 153A-152) were repealed by S.L. 2014-3 effective July 1, 2015. The state privilege license tax on professionals was repealed effective July 1, 2024 (NCDOR); it still applies only to loan agencies, pawnbrokers, and check cashers. No other NC city has a local receipts or business license tax on software or services firms, so none is added.

Sales tax: NCDOR private letter rulings (e.g. SUPLR 2021-0007) say NC does not impose sales or use tax on subscription fees for remotely accessed prewritten software (SaaS). From memory, not verified this session: downloaded or digital software and repair, maintenance, and installation services are taxable, while consulting and professional services generally are not. In any case these taxes are collected from customers, so they pass through.

Counties and cities levy annual ad valorem tax on business personal property such as computers and furniture. It is listed each January, scales with equipment cost, and is a property tax rather than a receipts tax; see the city entries for rates.

Payroll: state unemployment insurance (employer) is an expense the user already counts. NC income tax withheld from employees is the employees' tax. NC has no local payroll or head taxes.

calculatorOption.label: North Carolina
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; $200 minimum franchise tax (0.15% of NC-apportioned net worth, max $500 on the first $1M) plus $25 annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Charlotte, NC
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026-27 (no business license tax since July 1, 2015)
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Charlotte has no business license or privilege license tax and no gross receipts tax. City authority to levy one was repealed statewide effective July 1, 2015 (S.L. 2014-3, G.S. 160A-211). Charlotte has no city income or payroll tax.

The only recurring local cost not tied to profit is ad valorem tax on business personal property (computers, furniture), listed with Mecklenburg County each January. The county rate is $0.4927 per $100 for FY2026-27, and the city rate is $0.2741 per $100 for FY2026 (city FY2026 budget ordinance; I did not verify the FY2027 city rate). Combined that is about 0.77% of assessed equipment value, which scales with assets rather than revenue.

calculatorOption.label: Charlotte
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city business, receipts, or payroll tax; NC repealed local privilege license taxes in 2015.

jurisdictions.name: Raleigh, NC
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026-27 (no business license tax since July 1, 2015)
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
The city states that effective July 1, 2015 it no longer requires a business license, because HB 1050 (S.L. 2014-3) removed the authority. Raleigh has no gross receipts, city income, or payroll tax. Specific activity permits still exist (beer/wine, food trucks, zoning) but do not apply to a software firm.

Wake County taxes business personal property. The rates on the Wake tax-rates page (fiscal year not labeled) are county $0.5371 plus Raleigh $0.3720 per $100, about 0.91% combined.

calculatorOption.label: Raleigh
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city business, receipts, or payroll tax; Raleigh dropped its business license in 2015.

jurisdictions.name: Durham, NC
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2025-26 / FY2026-27 (no business license tax since July 1, 2015)
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Durham has no general privilege license or business license tax, because city authority was repealed effective July 1, 2015 (S.L. 2014-3, G.S. 160A-211). An older city 'Business Tax Unit' application PDF still shows up in search; it predates the repeal. The Durham County privilege license page now covers only beer and wine retailers ($5-$25). Durham has no gross receipts, city income, or payroll tax.

Business personal property is taxed at the combined city/county rate of $0.9913 per $100 inside Durham city limits for FY2025-26 (Durham County tax administration).

calculatorOption.label: Durham
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city business, receipts, or payroll tax; NC repealed local privilege license taxes in 2015.

jurisdictions.name: North Dakota
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (corporate income tax Form 40 for calendar 2025; SOS annual report fee current as of 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (foreign business corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 per year, due May 15, filed through the FirstStop portal. The same $25 applies to domestic and foreign corporations. If you file late you pay a late fee: secondary sources give $20 or $60 depending on timing, or totals of $45/$85, and I did not confirm the exact schedule on an official page. If the report stays unfiled for 6 to 12 months, the state revokes your authority to transact business. The one-time foreign registration (certificate of authority) is $145. It is not annual, so it is not counted here.

profitTaxes.name: Corporation income tax (Form 40)
profitTaxes.notes: Graduated rates on ND taxable income: 1.41% on $0 to $25,000; $352.50 plus 3.55% on $25,000 to $50,000; $1,240 plus 4.31% over $50,000. The top marginal rate is shown. Rates have been unchanged since 2015. There is no minimum tax: a pre-profit company owes $0 but must still file Form 40 if it does business in ND or has ND-source income. Water's-edge electors pay an extra 3.5% surtax on ND taxable income. Apportionment defaults to the equally weighted three-factor formula. You can elect a phased-in single sales factor, and the election is binding for 5 years. Service receipts are sourced by cost of performance (greater portion of costs incurred in ND), not by market. I took this from secondary sources and ND Admin Code chapter titles and did not read it in full.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: North Dakota has no franchise tax, no gross receipts tax and no minimum tax, so a pre-profit Delaware C-corp only pays the $25 annual report fee. Sales tax: the state rate is 5%. The Computers Guideline (Guideline 21825, updated 2-2026) treats commercial off-the-shelf software as taxable however it is delivered, including downloads and load-and-leave. Custom programs, web hosting, web development, separately billed computer time-sharing and data-processing services are not taxable. Remotely accessed SaaS is generally treated as nontaxable. That conclusion rests on the time-sharing provision plus secondary sources: the guideline never names SaaS. Either way, sales tax is collected from customers and passes through. Professional services are generally not taxable. Payroll: employers withhold ND individual income tax and pay state unemployment insurance through Job Service North Dakota. These are payroll expenses; I did not verify the rates. ND has no state disability or paid-leave payroll tax. A commercial registered agent, if you use one, is a private cost (often $100 to $300 a year), not a tax.

calculatorOption.label: North Dakota
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts or franchise tax in North Dakota; $25/yr foreign-corporation annual report; income tax (1.41% to 4.31%) is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.name: Fargo, ND
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Fargo has no city income tax, no business receipts tax and no general business license. Its licensing page says: 'The City does not require business licenses for every type of commerce'. Licenses apply only to listed trades such as excavators, plumbers, pawn brokers, haulers and alcohol sellers. Software and professional-services firms are not on the list. Fargo's '2.25% sales, use, and gross receipts tax' (raised from 2% on April 1, 2025; $56.25 per-sale cap) is the local sales tax. The 'gross receipts' wording covers sales tax on farm machinery and alcohol, per the home-rule statute NDCC 40-05.1-06(5). It is not a tax on a business's revenue. That tax follows state taxability, so SaaS and services are generally untaxed. The combined Fargo rate is 7.75% (5% state + 2.25% city + 0.5% Cass County), collected from customers. Since August 1, 2017, ND home-rule cities may not levy taxes beyond those listed in NDCC 40-05.1-06(5).

calculatorOption.label: Fargo
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Fargo has no receipts tax, income tax, or general business license; its 2.25% city sales tax is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Bismarck, ND
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Bismarck's official page says: 'The City of Bismarck does not presently have a general business license, however certain occupations may require a license or permit, specific to that use, to operate.' There is no city income tax or business receipts tax. The local sales tax is collected from customers and follows state taxability.

calculatorOption.label: Bismarck
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Bismarck has no receipts tax, income tax, or general business license.

jurisdictions.name: Grand Forks, ND
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Grand Forks has no city income tax or business receipts tax (NDCC 40-05.1-06 limits home-rule taxes to the listed types). It apparently has no general business license, only licenses for specific activities such as transient merchants, food vendors and towing. That comes from secondary sources: the city's own pages returned 403 to my fetches. Watch out for search results showing a $75 or $200 'Grand Forks business licence'. That fee belongs to Grand Forks, British Columbia (grandforks.ca), not North Dakota.

calculatorOption.label: Grand Forks
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Grand Forks has no receipts tax, income tax, or general business license.

jurisdictions.name: Ohio
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 and 2026 (CAT exclusion is $6M per calendar year from 2025 on; the statute has not changed since HB 33, 135th General Assembly)
