receiptsTaxes.name: Commercial Activity Tax (CAT)
receiptsTaxes.base: Taxable gross receipts sitused to Ohio, less a $6,000,000 exclusion per calendar year. Service and SaaS receipts are sitused to Ohio in proportion to where the purchaser gets the benefit, which is mainly where the purchaser physically uses or receives it (R.C. 5751.033(I)). IP licence receipts follow use or right-to-use in Ohio (5751.033(F)). No deduction for costs.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Ohio-sitused taxable gross receipts for the calendar year (not total revenue everywhere)
receiptsTaxes.notes: The rate is 2.6 mills (0.26%) on taxable gross receipts after subtracting the exclusion amount (R.C. 5751.03). The exclusion was $3M in 2024 and has been $6M since 2025 (R.C. 5751.01(R)). It works as a deduction, not a cliff: the first $6M of Ohio receipts is never taxed, so tax = 0.26% x (Ohio receipts - $6M). The annual minimum tax (formerly $150 to $2,600) is gone: current 5751.03 has no minimum. A business registers within 30 days of Ohio receipts first passing the exclusion in a year (R.C. 5751.04(B)). There is a one-time $20 registration fee, taken out of the first payment. Returns are quarterly, due the 10th day of the second month after each quarter; the full exclusion is applied on the first quarterly return and any unused part carries forward within the same year (R.C. 5751.051, 5751.03). Bright-line nexus is $500k of Ohio receipts, $50k of Ohio property, $50k of Ohio payroll, or 25% of any of these (R.C. 5751.01(I)). In practice nothing is owed until Ohio receipts pass $6M. A national seller with about 3.5% of revenue in Ohio would hit that at roughly $172M total revenue. CAT is a privilege tax, not a sales tax: it cannot be billed to customers as a separate tax line.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report / franchise tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Ohio has no annual report and no annual fee for for-profit corporations. The fee statute (R.C. 111.16) lists only a one-time $99 foreign corporation licence (111.16(I)(1)), plus $50 for amendments. The corporate franchise tax was phased out: R.C. 5733.01 says 'For tax year 2010 and each tax year thereafter, no tax' for general corporations.

fixedAnnual.name: CAT annual minimum tax
fixedAnnual.notes: Eliminated from 2024 by HB 33. Businesses at or below the $6M exclusion don't register or file.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate franchise/income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Ohio has no state corporate income tax for general C corporations; the CAT replaced it. The franchise tax under R.C. 5733 applied only to calendar years before 2014 and was phased to zero for non-financial corporations from tax year 2010. Ohio cities do tax net profits; see the city entries.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Sales tax on SaaS (pass-through): Ohio's 5.75% sales tax (R.C. 5739.02) applies to automatic data processing, computer services and electronic information services 'for use in business' (R.C. 5739.01(B)(3)(e)). B2B SaaS is generally taxable; sales to consumers for personal use generally are not. Personal and professional services are excluded (5739.01(Y)(1)(d)). County and transit permissive sales taxes are added on top; those county rates were not verified here. Payroll (already in expenses): Ohio state income tax withholding, Ohio unemployment insurance (employer-paid), and city income tax withheld from employees' wages, which is the employee's tax. Cities can't levy gross receipts taxes: R.C. 715.013 bars municipal taxes 'the same as or similar to' taxes under Chapter 5751 (the CAT), so no Ohio city has a business receipts tax. Cities levy income taxes under R.C. Chapter 718 on wages and business net profits. One-time costs: $99 foreign corporation licence with the Secretary of State. Sources: tax.ohio.gov and ohiosos.gov returned 403/404 to automated fetches, so the figures come from the Ohio Revised Code text on codes.ohio.gov. Secondary summaries of tax.ohio.gov agree: 0.26%, $6M exclusion from 2025, minimum tax eliminated.

calculatorOption.label: Ohio
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Ohio CAT is 0.26% of Ohio-sourced receipts above a $6M yearly exclusion (only the excess is taxed); Ohio has no minimum tax, annual report fee, or corporate income tax.

jurisdictions.name: Columbus, OH
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (BR-25 instructions for tax year 2025, rev. 8/20/2026); rate unchanged for 2026

fixedAnnual.name: General business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Columbus has no general business license. Its License Section issues licences only for listed activities (alarm dealers, arcades, itinerant vendors, short-term rentals, vehicles for hire, etc.); software and professional services aren't among them. No minimum tax appears in the BR-25 instructions.

profitTaxes.name: Columbus municipal income tax on net profits (Form BR-25)
profitTaxes.notes: The rate is 2.5% on net profits apportioned to Columbus. A BR-25 return must be filed even when the business reports a net loss. Since 2023, NOLs can offset 100% of income and carry forward 5 years; carrybacks aren't allowed. Businesses can elect to file the net profit return centrally with the Ohio Department of Taxation (R.C. 718.80 et seq.).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no receipts tax: Ohio law (R.C. 715.013) bars cities from taxes similar to the CAT. Payroll (already in expenses): employers must withhold the 2.5% city income tax from wages of employees working in Columbus. That tax is the employee's, so the employer only bears the admin work. Sales tax on B2B SaaS follows the state rule, plus Franklin County and transit rates, which were not verified here.

calculatorOption.label: Columbus
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Columbus taxes only net profit (2.5%) and has no receipts tax or general business license, so nothing is owed before profitability.

jurisdictions.name: Cleveland, OH
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (CCA net profit return for 2025, due April 15, 2026); rate unchanged for 2026

fixedAnnual.name: General business license
fixedAnnual.notes: The Division of Assessments and Licenses issues more than 140 activity-specific licences (vendors, garages, entertainment venues, waste haulers, etc.). No general business licence for software or professional-services firms was found. This is absence of evidence on the city's licence page, not an explicit statement, so medium confidence on this item.

profitTaxes.name: Cleveland municipal income tax on net profits (CCA Net Profit Return)
profitTaxes.notes: The rate is 2.5%, collected by the Central Collection Agency (CCA). It was raised from 2.0% on January 1, 2017. Every entity doing business in a CCA municipality must file a Net Profit Return. The return includes a 5-year loss carryforward schedule. Estimated payments are required if the expected tax is $200 or more.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no receipts tax (R.C. 715.013 preemption). Payroll (already in expenses): employers with employees working in Cleveland must withhold the 2.5% city income tax and file withholding returns plus a W-3 reconciliation with CCA. CCA also administers income tax for many other small Ohio cities. Sales tax on B2B SaaS follows the state rule, plus the Cuyahoga County rate, which was not verified here.

calculatorOption.label: Cleveland
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Cleveland taxes only net profit (2.5%) and has no receipts tax or general business license, so nothing is owed before profitability.

jurisdictions.name: Cincinnati, OH
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (2025 Business Tax Return); rate unchanged for 2026

fixedAnnual.name: General business license
fixedAnnual.notes: The Finance/Treasury business licence list covers only specific activities (admissions tax, antique dealer, appliance dealer, peddler, etc.). There is no general business licence for software or consulting firms.

profitTaxes.name: Cincinnati municipal income tax on net profits
profitTaxes.notes: The rate has been 1.8% since 10/02/2020, cut from 2.1%. Since 2023, NOLs can offset 100% of income and carry forward up to 5 years.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no receipts tax (R.C. 715.013 preemption). Payroll (already in expenses): employers withhold the 1.8% city income tax from employees working in Cincinnati. Sales tax on B2B SaaS follows the state rule, plus the Hamilton County rate, which was not verified here.

calculatorOption.label: Cincinnati
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Cincinnati taxes only net profit (1.8%) and has no receipts tax or general business license, so nothing is owed before profitability.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (corporate income tax rate from the 2026 Form OW-8-ESC). Registered agent fee from Form FRX-200-R for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, set by statute at $100/yr. Franchise tax repealed from tax year 2024.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign corporation annual registered agent fee (18 O.S. 1142)
fixedAnnual.notes: All foreign (non-Oklahoma) corporations, a Delaware C corp included, owe $100 each year so the Secretary of State can act as their registered agent. It is due July 1 and paid to the Oklahoma Tax Commission on Form FRX-200-R. If unpaid by September 1, the OTC may suspend and forfeit the charter. It used to be paid with the franchise tax return and is now filed on its own because the franchise tax was repealed. Owed only if the company has qualified to do business in Oklahoma, which is typically triggered by employees or an office there. The one-time qualification fee is separate and not annual: at least $300, or $1 per $1,000 of authorized or invested capital, with a minimum of $300. No annual report is required for corporations. A yearly certificate is required only if the company chose to pay the qualification fee on invested capital rather than on total authorized capital over $300k.

profitTaxes.name: Oklahoma corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 4% of Oklahoma taxable income, confirmed on the 2026 OW-8-ESC (rev. 6-2025). Multistate income is apportioned by formula. Zero before profit. Estimated payments are required only if the expected liability is $500 or more. HB 2764 (2025) cut the individual top rate to 4.5% but did not change the corporate rate. No 2026 corporate rate change was found.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Oklahoma franchise tax: REPEALED. HB 1039X (2023) made tax year 2023 the last year with a filing requirement. From 2024 on there is no franchise tax return and no franchise tax (formerly $1.25 per $1,000 of capital employed in Oklahoma, capped at $20,000). Unpaid tax for 2023 and earlier is still collectible.

There is no state gross receipts tax.

Sales tax: SaaS and electronically delivered prewritten software are NOT taxable. OAC 710:65-19-156(b)(5) and 68 O.S. 1357(32) exempt it, and electronic data processing services are exempt under (b)(3). Custom software and software services are non-taxable service transactions (OAC 710:65-19-52(g)). Software on tangible media or delivered by load-and-leave is taxable. Professional services are generally not taxed.

Business personal property tax: counties assess ad valorem tax on tangible business assets such as computers and furniture. Form 901 (the business personal property return) is due March 15, with a 10%/20% late penalty. The amount is small for a laptop-only startup but not zero. It is not modeled here.

Payroll: state income tax withholding and state unemployment insurance (SUTA) on Oklahoma employees belong in expenses.

The state requires no general business license.

calculatorOption.label: Oklahoma
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Oklahoma receipts or franchise tax (franchise tax repealed from 2024); $100/yr foreign-corporation registered agent fee.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma City, OK
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city income tax, payroll tax or gross receipts tax. Oklahoma municipalities fund themselves mainly through sales tax: the combined rate in Oklahoma City is about 8.625% (secondary sources). That doesn't apply to SaaS because the state base exempts electronically delivered software. The city issues only industry-specific licenses (alcohol, food service, hotel/motel, massage, vehicles for hire, contractors and similar). There is no general business license for a software or professional-services firm. Oklahoma County ad valorem tax on business personal property applies to any equipment kept in the city.

calculatorOption.label: Oklahoma City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Oklahoma City has no receipts, income, or general business license tax for software/services firms.

jurisdictions.name: Tulsa, OK
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city income tax, payroll tax or gross receipts tax. Combined sales tax is about 8.517% (secondary sources) and doesn't apply to SaaS. The city's business licensing page lists only industry-specific licenses: alarm, beverage, chauffeur, coin-op, food and liquor, hotel, outdoor seller, pawnbroker, short-term rental, taxi and similar. The city's 'Doing Business in Tulsa' guide says: 'In Oklahoma there is no general license required to start or own a business.' Tulsa County ad valorem tax on business personal property applies to any equipment kept in the city.

calculatorOption.label: Tulsa
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Tulsa has no receipts, income, or general business license tax for software/services firms.

jurisdictions.name: Oregon
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 (CAT, minimum excise tax and fees are unchanged for 2026; HB 2039 (2025), which would have raised the CAT exclusion to $10M, died in House Revenue committee)

receiptsTaxes.name: Corporate Activity Tax (CAT)
receiptsTaxes.base: Taxable Oregon commercial activity: gross receipts sourced to Oregon, minus exclusions and a subtraction of 35% of the greater of cost inputs (COGS) or labor costs. The subtraction is apportioned to Oregon by the sales factor and capped at 95% of Oregon commercial activity. Sourcing (ORS 317A.128): services are sourced where they are delivered, and intangibles where they are used (market-based). A SaaS subscription is effectively sourced to the customer's location.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: taxable commercial activity sourced to Oregon (after the 35% subtraction), not total revenue
receiptsTaxes.notes: Tax = $250 + 0.57% of taxable Oregon commercial activity above $1M. The $1M is an exclusion, not just a cliff, so applying 0.57% to all Oregon receipts above the threshold overstates the tax by about $5,450/yr. The 35% subtraction cuts the effective rate further: if labor costs roughly equal revenue (typical pre-profit SaaS), the effective rate is 0.57% x 0.65 = ~0.37%. If labor is at least ~2.7x revenue, the 95% cap applies and the rate is ~0.03%. Labor costs are capped at $500k of compensation per employee. Companies must register with DOR once Oregon commercial activity reaches $750k, and file once it exceeds $1M, even if no tax is due. At Oregon's ~1.25% population share, Oregon receipts reach $1M only around $80M of national revenue, so a typical startup owes nothing. The CAT is separate from, and in addition to, the corporate excise tax.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate excise minimum tax (ORS 317.090)
fixedAnnual.notes: Every C corporation doing business in Oregon pays the greater of the calculated excise tax or the minimum, even at a loss, and credits cannot offset it. The minimum is tiered by the filing group's Oregon sales: under $500k $150; $500k-$999,999 $500; $1M-$1.99M $1,000; $2M-$2.99M $1,500; $3M-$4.99M $2,000; $5M-$6.99M $4,000; $7M-$9.99M $7,500; $10M-$24.99M $15,000; $25M-$49.99M $30,000; $50M-$74.99M $50,000; $75M-$99.99M $75,000; $100M+ $100,000. 'Doing business' includes an office, employees, or an economic presence regularly exploiting Oregon's economy. A corporation not doing business in Oregon but with Oregon-source income files OR-20-INC instead and has no minimum. DOR warns that filing an OR-20 unnecessarily can trigger a minimum-tax bill.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign business corporation annual report (renewal), Secretary of State
fixedAnnual.notes: Annual renewal for a foreign business/professional corporation (a Delaware corp registered in Oregon). The Application for Authority is also $275, one time. A domestic Oregon corporation pays $100. Source is the SOS Business Registry fee schedule PDF (dated 07/13), corroborated by 2026 secondary guides.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate excise tax
profitTaxes.notes: 6.6% of Oregon taxable income up to $1M; 7.6% above $1M (i.e. $66,000 + 7.6% of the excess). Uses single-sales-factor, market-based apportionment (ORS 314.665/314.666). Zero before profit, but the minimum tax above still applies.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Oregon has no sales tax, so there is no SaaS sales/use tax to collect. These payroll taxes belong in expenses (2026 figures from DOR's combined payroll instructions):
- Unemployment insurance: taxable wage base $56,700.
- Paid Leave Oregon: 1% on wages up to $184,500. Employers with 25+ employees pay 40% of it; employees pay 60%.
- Workers' Benefit Fund assessment: 1.8 cents per hour worked.
- Statewide transit tax: 0.1%, withheld from employees.
- TriMet transit payroll tax: 0.8237% employer-paid (2025 and 2026), on wages for work in the Portland metro district.
- Lane Transit District payroll tax: 0.80% employer-paid (2025 and 2026), Eugene/Springfield area.
No Oregon city other than Portland (with Multnomah County and Metro) taxes business income or receipts. Other cities charge only flat or per-employee license fees. Gresham (official page): $80 + $3 per employee after the first two, for businesses located in or conducting business in Gresham. Beaverton charges a per-employee license fee; the official fee schedule blocked automated access, so the amounts are unverified. Salem: voters rejected a proposed 0.814% payroll tax in November 2023 (secondary sources only). Default share is Oregon's share of US population (4,273,586 / 341,784,857, Census V2025 figures from search results).

calculatorOption.label: Oregon
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.57% CAT on Oregon-sourced receipts above $1M/yr (the real tax is $250 + 0.57% of the excess after a 35% labor/cost subtraction, so this overstates it), plus a $150 minimum excise tax and a $275 foreign annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Portland, OR
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025 and 2026 (gross receipts exemption $50k for 2025, $75k for 2026, $100k from 2027)

fixedAnnual.name: City of Portland Business License Tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: PCC 7.02.545 says each return 'must be accompanied by a minimum tax of $100', so it is owed even at a loss by any non-exempt business doing business in the City. A business is exempt if its total gross receipts from all business, everywhere, are below $50,000 (2025), $75,000 (2026), or $100,000 (2027+) (PCC 7.02.400). The City and County file a combined return (Form C for corporations), administered by the Portland Revenue Division.

fixedAnnual.name: Multnomah County Business Income Tax minimum (bundled here; see Multnomah County entry)
fixedAnnual.notes: MCC 12.500: each non-exempt taxfiler 'must pay at least a minimum tax of $100.00', even at a loss. A business is exempt if its gross receipts from all business, inside and outside the county, are below $100,000.

profitTaxes.name: Portland Business License Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 2.6% of adjusted net income apportioned to Portland, unchanged since 2018. Apportionment for 2023+ is single sales factor using Oregon's market-based sourcing (PCC 7.02.611). A pay-ratio surtax of 10%/25% of base tax applies only to publicly traded companies.

profitTaxes.name: Multnomah County Business Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 2.00% of net income apportioned to the county (since tax year 2020). Applies to all of Portland, which sits almost entirely in Multnomah County.

profitTaxes.name: Metro Supportive Housing Services Business Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 1% of net income apportioned to the Metro district, only for businesses with over $5M of gross receipts from all sources. Minimum $100 for filers over $5M (see Metro entry). Expires after 2030 unless voters renew it.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
Portland has no gross receipts tax that applies to a SaaS startup. The Clean Energy Surcharge (1% of Portland retail gross receipts) applies only to businesses with $1B+ total gross receipts and $500k+ Portland receipts.

Nexus: per the Portland Revenue Division (seen in search results), an 'economic presence through which the taxpayer regularly takes advantage of' the Portland/Multnomah/Metro economy counts as doing business, and services are apportioned to the customer's location. A company with Portland customers but no office may therefore be expected to file and pay the $100 + $100 minimums. A company with an office or employees there certainly is.

Payroll and personal taxes (expenses or employee-paid, not business taxes):
- TriMet transit tax: 0.8237% employer-paid.
- Metro SHS personal income tax: 1% above $125k single / $200k joint, inflation-indexed from 2026; employers withhold it.
- Multnomah County Preschool for All: personal income tax with employer withholding.
- Portland Arts Tax: $35 per resident.

Portland has no sales tax.

calculatorOption.label: Portland
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts tax; Portland and Multnomah County each charge a $100 minimum business tax even at a loss once total gross receipts reach $75k (city, 2026) / $100k (county), and their 2.6% + 2% net-income taxes start only at profit.

jurisdictions.name: Multnomah County, OR

fixedAnnual.name: Business Income Tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: MCC 12.500(A): every non-exempt taxfiler pays at least $100, even at a loss. A business is exempt if its gross receipts from all business, inside and outside the county, are below $100,000 (the threshold was $50,000 before 2020). Filed on the combined Portland/Multnomah return through the Portland Revenue Division. This $100 is already included in the Portland calculator option.

profitTaxes.name: Multnomah County Business Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 2.00% of net income from business within the county, for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2020 (1.45% before). Single sales factor, market-based apportionment.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: The county option is bundled into the Portland option to avoid double counting. Add it separately only for a company located in the county outside Portland (e.g. Gresham, Troutdale), which owes the county $100 minimum but not Portland's. The Preschool for All tax is a personal income tax (employer withholding); it is not a business tax.

calculatorOption.label: Multnomah County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $100 Multnomah County minimum business income tax once total gross receipts reach $100k; already included in the Portland option.

jurisdictions.name: Metro (Portland regional government), OR

fixedAnnual.name: Supportive Housing Services Business Income Tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $0 for a small startup. Only businesses with over $5M of gross receipts from all sources, inside and outside Metro, are subject. For them the 2025 METBIT-20 instructions say 'The minimum tax due is $100. If the amount calculated is less than $100, enter $100.' The instructions don't say explicitly whether this applies in a loss year, but the wording suggests it does.

profitTaxes.name: Metro SHS Business Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 1% of net income apportioned to the Metro district (single sales factor, market-based sourcing), for businesses with over $5M of total gross receipts. Approved by voters in May 2020 and effective 2021. Expires after 2030 unless voters renew it. Starting in 2026, the estimated-payment threshold rises from $1,000 to $5,000.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: The Metro district covers urban Multnomah, Washington and Clackamas counties (Portland, Beaverton, Hillsboro, Gresham, etc.). Metro's 1% personal income tax (above $125k single / $200k joint, inflation-indexed from 2026) is withheld by employers but paid by employees. A pre-profit startup owes nothing to Metro until total revenue exceeds $5M, and then only the possible $100 minimum.

calculatorOption.label: Metro (Portland region)
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Metro's 1% business income tax applies only to net income of businesses with over $5M total gross receipts (minimum $100 for those filers); nothing for a small pre-profit startup.

jurisdictions.name: Eugene, OR
jurisdictions.otherNotes:
No gross receipts or business income tax found. Eugene has a Community Safety Payroll Tax, which belongs in expenses:
- Employer portion: 0.21% of wages, for businesses with a physical location in Eugene. Employers averaging 2 or fewer employees pay a reduced 0.15% on the first $100k of wages.
- Employee portion: 0.44% for employees earning over ~$31,304/yr (July 2025-June 2026).
The tax expires after 12/31/2028 unless voters renew it. These rates come from secondary sources (payroll vendors, local news) because eugene-or.gov blocked automated access, so they are unverified against the city's own pages. Employers there also pay the Lane Transit District payroll tax: 0.80% for 2025-26, verified on DOR's official publication.

calculatorOption.label: Eugene
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No receipts or business income tax; Eugene's Community Safety Payroll Tax (0.21% employer) is a payroll expense.

jurisdictions.name: Pennsylvania
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (CNIT rate and DOS annual report fee for 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Department of State Annual Report (foreign business corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: Required from 2025 onward for all registered foreign associations. Corporations file between Jan 1 and Jun 30. Starting with reports not filed in 2027, a foreign corporation that misses it can have its registration administratively terminated. Separate from the one-time $250 Foreign Registration Statement fee (not annual).

profitTaxes.name: Corporate Net Income Tax (CNIT)
profitTaxes.notes: Rate is 7.49% for tax years starting in 2026. It was 7.99% in 2025, falls to 6.99% in 2027 and steps down 0.5 points a year to 4.99% from 2031 (Act 53-2022). Act 45 of 2025 decouples PA from federal R&E expensing: you add back the federal R&E deduction and deduct it at 20% a year. So a company with heavy R&D that is close to breakeven can owe PA tax before it is profitable federally. Economic nexus: a rebuttable presumption at $500,000+ of PA-sourced receipts a year (Corporation Tax Bulletin 2019-04). There is no minimum tax.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No state-level gross receipts or minimum tax applies to a software/services C corp. Capital Stock/Foreign Franchise Tax was eliminated for tax years starting in 2016 or later. From memory, not re-read this session: PA's separate 'Gross Receipts Tax' applies only to utilities, telecom and transportation. SALES TAX (pass-through, collected from customers): the 6% sales tax covers canned software however it is delivered, including software accessed remotely (SaaS) by users in PA. Allegheny County adds 1% (7%) and Philadelphia adds 2% (8%). PAYROLL (already counted in expenses): PA unemployment comp; local Earned Income Tax withheld from employees under Act 32; Local Services Tax, usually $52 a year per employee, withheld by the employer. LOCAL RECEIPTS TAXES: about 272 PA municipalities and school districts kept the Business Privilege/Mercantile taxes on gross receipts that existed before the 1988 freeze. They usually run 1 to 3 mills on services and are generally sourced to the business's base of operations, so a startup located in one owes on most receipts. The listed cities were checked. Philadelphia-suburb hubs also charge BPT; these figures come only from search snippets because the official pages returned 403: Radnor Twp 3 mills on services with the first $25,000 exempt, and Upper Merion Twp (King of Prussia) 1.5 mills. Lower Merion, Radnor and Upper Merion each collect over $10M a year (BDO). Erie was not verified. Founders should check the municipality and school district of their office.

calculatorOption.label: Pennsylvania
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Pennsylvania has no receipts or minimum tax for a corporation that isn't profitable yet, only the $7 annual report; its 7.49% corporate income tax is zero until profit.

jurisdictions.name: Philadelphia, PA
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2026 (returns due April 15, 2027); TY2025 rates in notes

receiptsTaxes.name: Business Income & Receipts Tax (BIRT), gross receipts portion
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts sourced to Philadelphia. A 'Software Company' (NAICS 5415/54151/541512, 51121, 51611, 51811, 518210, 52232) uses market-based sourcing for all its product and service receipts: receipts count in proportion to the benefit customers receive in Philadelphia (BIRT Regulations §101DD, §408(G)–(G.1)). For other service businesses, a secondary source (Sales Tax Institute) says service receipts are sourced where the service is performed. That would put close to 100% of a Philadelphia-based professional-services firm's receipts in Philadelphia.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none for businesses located in Philadelphia (the $100,000 exclusion ended with tax year 2025). An out-of-city business has economic nexus only once it has at least $100,000 of Philadelphia gross receipts in any 12-month period.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rates: 1.395 mills for TY2026 (phila.gov, June 2026); 1.410 mills for TY2025; 1.415 mills for TY2016–2024. Under the city's FY26 tax plan, cuts continue and the gross receipts portion is eliminated by FY39. The $100,000 statutory exclusion ended with TY2025 after a legal challenge. Every for-profit business active in the city must file, whether or not it made a profit. Cash flow: from the second return onward, 100% of the next year's estimated BIRT is due with the April 15 return. Newly required filers with under $100k Philadelphia sales in the prior three years are excused from that estimate on their first (2026) return. Jump Start Philly: a new business that has not filed BIRT in the prior five years and is not in real estate is exempt from BIRT for its first two years if it has 3 employees by the end of year one and 6 by the end of year two.

fixedAnnual.name: Commercial Activity License
fixedAnnual.notes: No cost and no renewal. The city can revoke it if BIRT and wage tax returns aren't filed and paid.

profitTaxes.name: BIRT net income portion
profitTaxes.notes: 5.65% for TY2026 (5.71% for TY2025, 5.81% for TY2024). Applies to Philadelphia-apportioned net income using a single receipts factor. NOLs carry forward 20 years. Corporations do not pay Net Profits Tax.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Wage Tax is withheld from employees' pay: 3.74% for residents and 3.43% for non-residents from July 1, 2025. It is an employee tax the company already counts in payroll. Use & Occupancy Tax: 1.21% of the assessed value of occupied commercial space, and the $2,000 annual exemption ended Jan 1, 2026. Landlords usually pass it through in rent, so treat it as an expense. Sales tax in Philadelphia is 8% (6% state + 2% local) on taxable canned software and SaaS, collected from customers. Calculator note: a share near 100% fits a Philadelphia-based business that is not classified as a Software Company. A Software Company sourcing by market should use its share of customers in Philadelphia (about 0.46% by population).

calculatorOption.label: Philadelphia
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.1395% (1.395 mills, tax year 2026) of receipts sourced to Philadelphia, which for a software company means its share of customers there; there is no $100k exclusion from 2025.

jurisdictions.name: Pittsburgh, PA

fixedAnnual.name: City business registration
fixedAnnual.notes: The City's Business Registration Form (rev. 07/26) lists no fee. It registers employers for Local Services Tax and Payroll Expense Tax.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Pittsburgh has no gross receipts tax on for-profit businesses. Per the City's own documents (seen via search), the Business Privilege Tax on service receipts was eliminated in 2010. The Institution & Service Privilege Tax on gross receipts applies only to non-profits. PAYROLL (already in expenses): Payroll Expense Tax is 0.55% of gross compensation paid to anyone working in the city. The employer pays it, it can't be withheld from wages, and it's filed quarterly. Local Services Tax is $52 a year per employee, withheld. Earned Income Tax is withheld through Jordan Tax Service. Sales tax in Allegheny County is 7% (6% state + 1% county) on taxable canned software and SaaS, collected from customers.

calculatorOption.label: Pittsburgh
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Pittsburgh has no receipts tax or fixed fee; its 0.55% payroll expense tax belongs in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Allentown, PA

receiptsTaxes.name: Business Privilege Tax (service rate)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross volume of business transacted in the City. A company whose base of operations is in Allentown is taxed on receipts generated by its activities there. A unitary business in interstate commerce apportions using a three-factor formula: property, sales from City activities, and payroll (Regs §204–205).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none for businesses located in Allentown. A business with no physical presence has economic nexus at 15+ transactions totaling $500,000+ to points in the City in a calendar year.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rates: service 3 mills, rental 3 mills, retail 1.5 mills, wholesale 1 mill. They are unchanged in the City's 2026 final budget narrative, and the current regulations date from Jan 1, 2021. No small-receipts exemption. For an interstate SaaS company the share may come in under 100% after three-factor apportionment, but property and payroll factors near 100% keep it high. Allentown School District BPT: none found (not confirmed).

fixedAnnual.name: Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: Annual, calendar year, required of every person trading for profit in the City (Chapter 196). Renewal invoices are due January 1.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Local Services Tax of $52 per employee and EIT are withheld from employees. Sales tax is 6% (state only).

calculatorOption.label: Allentown
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.3% (3 mills) of receipts for a company based in Allentown, plus a $35 business license; interstate apportionment can lower the share.

jurisdictions.name: Reading, PA

receiptsTaxes.name: Business Privilege Tax (service rate, City + Reading School District)
receiptsTaxes.base: All receipts if the business's only place of business is in Reading. Service receipts count if the activity occurs in the City or is generated, directed, managed or controlled from a Reading office (BPT Regs III-2). Receipts of a bona fide branch office outside the City can be excluded.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: 2026 rates: service, commission and rental 2.25 mills (City 1.50 + School District 0.75); retail 1.5 mills; wholesale 1.0 mill. 2% discount if filed and paid by April 15; face amount due June 15; penalty from July 16. Collected by Keystone Collections Group. No receipts exemption found.

fixedAnnual.name: Business Privilege License
fixedAnnual.notes: Annual fee per the City's 2026 tax rate sheet.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Local Services Tax is $52 a year per employee. EIT is withheld from employees (3.6% resident, 1% non-resident). Sales tax is 6%.

calculatorOption.label: Reading
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.225% (2.25 mills, city plus school district) of receipts for a company based in Reading, plus a $55 business privilege license.

jurisdictions.name: Harrisburg, PA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (rates from the City's current license application; no rate change found)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business Privilege Tax (City + Harrisburg School District)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts from business conducted within the City of Harrisburg. A license is required whether the business is headquartered in the city or elsewhere.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Tiered. City: 2 mills on gross receipts up to $3,300,000 and 0.5 mill on the excess. School District: 1 mill up to $3,300,000 and 0.5 mill on the excess. Combined that is 3 mills up to $3.3M and 1 mill above, read here as marginal. So a flat 0.3% slightly overstates the tax once revenue passes $3.3M. Annual return due April 15 (Chapter 5-715, from a search snippet). Wholesale and retail have lower rates.

fixedAnnual.name: Business Privilege and Mercantile License
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 each calendar year, not prorated in the first year.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: The Local Services Tax and EIT are employee withholding. Sales tax is 6%. The license application text read this session is undated, but it was issued under Mayor Wanda Williams (in office since 2022).

calculatorOption.label: Harrisburg
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.3% (3 mills, city plus school district) of receipts up to $3.3M for a company based in Harrisburg (1 mill above that), plus a $50 license.

jurisdictions.name: Bethlehem, PA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025–2026 license year (current regulations and city page)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business Privilege and Mercantile Tax (service rate, combined City + Bethlehem Area School District)
receiptsTaxes.base: Services performed in Bethlehem. Services managed, directed or controlled from a Bethlehem office are also presumed to belong to Bethlehem, even when the customer is elsewhere. Receipts already taxed by another local BPT, or run from a bona fide branch office elsewhere, are excluded.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes: Effective combined rate is 1.5 mills on services, retail and rentals and 1 mill on wholesale (Act 511 caps the combined City + School District rate). Annual return due the first Monday in May. Optional quarterly filing for businesses expecting over $2,000,000.

fixedAnnual.name: Business Privilege and Mercantile Tax License
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 per license year (May 1–Apr 30): $13 to the City and $12 to the School District.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: The Local Services Tax and EIT are employee withholding. Sales tax is 6%.

calculatorOption.label: Bethlehem
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.15% (1.5 mills) of receipts for a company based in Bethlehem, plus a $25 license.

jurisdictions.name: Scranton, PA
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Scranton repealed its Business Privilege and Mercantile taxes effective Jan 1, 2022 (File of Council No. 95 of 2021). It replaced them with a Payroll Preparation Tax of 0.2787% of payroll, paid by the employer. That is a payroll cost that belongs in expenses, not a receipts tax.

calculatorOption.label: Scranton
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Scranton has no receipts tax since 2022; its 0.2787% payroll preparation tax belongs in expenses.

jurisdictions.name: Lancaster, PA
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Lancaster has no gross receipts or business privilege tax. It had none before the 1988 cutoff, so it cannot add one, according to a City Home Rule Study Commission post (search snippet). The City charges a $35 business registration fee; the page read here doesn't say whether it is one-time or annual, so it is left out of fixed amounts. The Local Services Tax of $52 and EIT are employee withholding.

calculatorOption.label: Lancaster
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Lancaster has no receipts tax; its $35 business registration fee may be one-time.

jurisdictions.name: Rhode Island
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax year 2025 and 2026 (minimum tax unchanged at $400 since TY2017; checked against FY2025, FY2026 and FY2027 enacted budgets); annual report fee per current RI Dept. of State fee schedule

fixedAnnual.name: Business corporation tax minimum (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2(e))
fixedAnnual.notes: Every corporation doing business in RI files Form RI-1120C and pays the greater of 7% of apportioned net income or $400 (for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2017). RI Dept. of State says it is owed by every registered for-profit entity whether or not business is actually conducted or a profit is made, and it is not prorated for a partial first year. The Governor's proposal to cut it to $350 effective 1/1/2025 was NOT adopted (House Fiscal FY2025 Budget as Enacted revenue changes); the FY2026 and FY2027 enacted budgets contain no change to it.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report (foreign business corporation), RI Dept. of State
fixedAnnual.notes: $50 per year, filed Feb 1 to May 1 starting the year after registration. One-time foreign registration (certificate of authority) fee is $310, not counted here. Late filing penalty $25 (secondary sources).

profitTaxes.name: Business corporation tax (RI-1120C)
profitTaxes.notes: 7% of net income apportioned to RI, or the $400 minimum if greater. Zero above the minimum until profitable. RI decoupled from federal immediate R&D expensing starting TY2026 (keeps 5-year amortization) and decouples from QSBS gain exclusion and a business-interest provision from TY2027 (FY2027 enacted budget); these matter only once profitable. Single-sales-factor, market-based apportionment and combined reporting are from recall, not verified this session.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No state gross receipts, franchise-on-capital, or margin tax applies to a SaaS/services corporation (RI's franchise tax on authorized capital was repealed years ago; the gross earnings taxes cover utilities, insurers, and banks, not software). Sales/use tax: 7% statewide, no local add-on; it applies to vendor-hosted prewritten software (SaaS) and electronically delivered prewritten software under R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-7 (added by P.L. 2018 ch. 47, effective Oct 1, 2018). It is collected from RI customers, so it passes through and isn't counted here. Professional services are generally not taxable. The FY2026 Governor's proposal for a 10% digital advertising revenue tax (only for companies with $1B+ global revenue) was not enacted. Payroll costs belong in expenses: employer state unemployment insurance plus the Job Development Fund assessment on taxable wages; TDI is withheld from employees. The tangible personal property tax is a local property tax, with a statewide mandatory $50,000 exemption per taxpayer from the 12/31/2023 assessment date on (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-5.3-1). A startup with only laptops is usually under the exemption. tax.ri.gov sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and couldn't be read directly, so the figures were confirmed from the statute, the RI Dept. of State fee page, and General Assembly fiscal reports.

calculatorOption.label: Rhode Island
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Rhode Island: $400 minimum business corporation tax plus $50 annual report each year; no receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Providence, RI
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2026 and FY2027 (proposed ordinance books; tax rates and exemption identical in both)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Providence has no city income, gross receipts, payroll, or head tax. RI municipalities rely on property taxes, plus state-administered local meals/beverage and hotel taxes that don't apply to SaaS. The Board of Licenses issues licenses only for specific regulated activities (liquor, food dispensing, hackney, peddlers, motor vehicle repair, entertainment, second-hand, etc.). No general business license for an office-based software or professional-services firm was found. Tangible personal property tax (Class 4): $53.40 per $1,000 of assessed value, after the mandatory $50,000 statewide exemption (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-5.3-1, adopted in the city ordinance). A startup with less than $50k of assessed business equipment owes $0. Above that it is a property tax on equipment, not on receipts, so it isn't modeled. Other RI cities and towns (Warwick, Cranston, Pawtucket, etc.) work the same way: no local receipts or business tax on software/services companies was found in any RI municipality. That conclusion comes from how RI local taxing authority works, not a city-by-city ordinance check.

calculatorOption.label: Providence
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Providence: no city receipts, income, or general business-license tax; only tangible property tax above a $50,000 exemption.

jurisdictions.name: South Carolina
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years 2025-2026. SC1120 instructions (rev. June 2025) and SC Code 12-20-50/60 read this session. No change to the corporate license fee was enacted in the 2025 session (SCDOR Information Letter #25-11). H.3773, which would exclude the first $50M of VC/angel equity for SC-headquartered companies, is still in House Ways and Means (last action Jan 28, 2025).

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate license fee (SC1120 Part II / Schedule E)
fixedAnnual.notes: $15 plus 0.1% ($1 per $1,000 or fraction) of capital stock and paid-in or capital surplus, taken from the applicable financial statement on the first day of the tax year. Retained earnings are excluded, so an accumulated deficit does NOT reduce the base (SC Code 12-20-50). Multistate corporations multiply the base by the SC income-tax apportionment ratio (12-20-60; Schedule E). The minimum is $25, and the minimum is not apportioned. The fee is paid in advance with the SC1120: the return for tax year 2025 pays the license fee for 2026. $25 is the right figure for a foreign corporation with little SC apportionment, such as one registered because of a remote SC employee. A VC-backed startup HEADQUARTERED in SC with near-100% SC apportionment pays about 0.1% of the capital it has raised: about $5,015/yr on $5M of paid-in capital, or $20,015 on $20M. This is capital-based, not receipts-based, so the calculator's revenue model can't represent it.

fixedAnnual.name: Initial license fee (Form CL-1, one-time)
fixedAnnual.notes: One-time $25 initial corporate license fee with the Initial Annual Report of Corporations (CL-1), due within 60 days of first doing business in SC. It is not recurring, so it is entered as 0/yr. The annual report itself is Schedule D of the SC1120 and has no separate Secretary of State annual-report fee. The Secretary of State also charges a one-time certificate-of-authority filing fee to register a foreign corporation (amount not verified this session).

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 5% of SC taxable income. Service and non-tangible-goods companies apportion with a single gross-receipts ratio (Schedule H-2). Service receipts are sourced by INCOME-PRODUCING ACTIVITY (where the work is performed), not by where the customer is: 'receipts from services if the entire income-producing activity is within the state...to the extent of the income-producing activity performed within South Carolina' (SC1120 instructions). An out-of-state SaaS/services firm therefore apportions little to SC. The tax is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes:
SALES TAX (pass-through): SCDOR treats SaaS/ASP charges (customer uses software hosted on the provider's site) as taxable 'communications' under 12-36-910(B)(3) (SC Revenue Ruling #12-1, citing #03-5 and #06-8). The state rate is 6% plus local option taxes, collected from SC customers. Electronically downloaded software is not taxable. Custom programming services are generally not taxable.

PAYROLL: SC income tax withholding and SC unemployment insurance are expenses, not counted here. I found no local payroll or head taxes in SC (from memory, not checked against a source this session).

PROPERTY: corporations report business personal property (computers, furniture) for county property tax on SCDOR Form PT-100. It is a real pre-profit cost, but it depends on assets, not revenue, so it isn't modeled here.

LOCAL BUSINESS LICENSE TAX: SC's main pre-profit cost is local. Nearly every SC municipality, plus counties for their unincorporated areas (e.g. Charleston County, Richland County), levies an annual business license tax on GROSS RECEIPTS under the Business License Tax Standardization Act (SC Code 6-1-400). The license year runs May 1-Apr 30 and the tax is measured on the prior calendar year's gross income. Under the MASC 2025 class schedule (license years starting May 2026), NAICS 51 (Information) and NAICS 54 (Professional services) are both Class 4. A business DOMICILED in a city owes tax on ALL its gross receipts, including out-of-state receipts. The only deduction is receipts on which it paid license tax to another SC county or municipality. Other notable cities (Mount Pleasant, North Charleston, Rock Hill, Spartanburg, Summerville) levy the same kind of tax; their rates were not verified this session.

calculatorOption.label: South Carolina
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No SC receipts tax. Corporate license fee is $15 + 0.1% of paid-in capital apportioned to SC, $25 minimum; an SC-headquartered startup pays about $1,000 per $1M raised.

jurisdictions.name: Charleston, SC
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year May 1, 2026 - April 30, 2027, measured on calendar-2025 gross income. Rates are from the city's posted '2026/2027 ordinance and appendix' (Code Supp. 112, which includes Ord. 2025-152, effective for the license year beginning May 1, 2026).

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license tax (Class 4: Information / Professional, scientific & technical services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts. If the company has a domicile in the city (an office from which the business is conducted, directed, or managed), the base is ALL gross receipts everywhere, less receipts on which business license tax was paid to another SC county or municipality and fully reported. The ordinance adds that 'properly apportioned income from business in interstate commerce shall be included...and is not exempted.' Without a domicile, only receipts from business done within the city count, at doubled non-resident rates.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Class 4 costs $49 on the first $2,000 of gross income, plus $2.80 per $1,000 or fraction above $2,000 (0.28%). Above $4M of gross income, the per-$1,000 rate drops to 80% of the class rate. Example: $1M of gross income costs $49 + 998 x $2.80 = $2,843.40.

Charleston also has a much cheaper Class 9.8 subclass for NAICS 541511, 511210 (now 513210, Software Publishers) and 334611 ('Computer Programming Design, Prepackaged Software Design'). It is $10 on the first $2,000, then $0.55 per $1,000 up to $1M (0.055%), $0.10 per $1,000 from $1M-$2M, $0.05 per $1,000 from $2M-$10M, and $0.0025 per $1,000 above $10M. Ord. 2025-152 keeps Class 9 in force. A pure SaaS/software publisher may qualify; the license official decides the class.

When income from different classes at one location can't be separated, the tax uses the highest-rate class on combined income (Sec. 17-19(b)). That is why Class 4 is the default for a mixed SaaS + professional-services company.

Due April 30. Filing through the state's business license portal is allowed. The city's 'Applicable Fees' page quotes '$64 base + $3.90 per $1,000'; those are Class 7 rates and don't apply to NAICS 51/54.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license base tax (first $2,000 of gross income)
fixedAnnual.notes: Class 4 minimum. It is owed even with zero revenue if the business operates in the city, and covers gross income from $0 to $2,000. It is $10 if the business qualifies for software subclass 9.8.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Charleston has no city income or payroll tax. Charleston County's business license applies only in UNINCORPORATED areas (seen in search results, not in county source documents), so it doesn't stack on top of the city license. County/city property tax on business personal property applies separately and isn't modeled. Hospitality and accommodations taxes don't apply to SaaS. Out-of-state sellers with Charleston customers but no office in the city are technically 'non-residents' owing doubled rates on city-sourced receipts; enforcement against remote SaaS sellers is uncertain.

calculatorOption.label: Charleston
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Charleston business license: $49 + 0.28% of ALL gross receipts when your office is in the city (Class 4); pure software publishers may get a 0.055% subclass.

jurisdictions.name: Columbia, SC
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year May 1, 2026 - April 30, 2027, measured on calendar-2025 gross income. The class schedule is from Ord. 2025-072 (adopted Oct 7, 2025, effective for the license year beginning May 1, 2026). Rates are from Appendix A as restated in Ord. 2024-050 (Aug 6, 2024); I found no later rate ordinance.

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license tax (Class 4: Information and Professional, scientific & technical services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts. If the company is domiciled in the city, the base is ALL gross receipts everywhere, less receipts on which business license tax was paid to another SC county or municipality and fully reported. Without a domicile, only receipts from within the city count, at doubled non-resident rates.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Class 4 costs $75 on the first $2,000, plus $1.20 per $1,000 or fraction above $2,000 (0.12%). Declining rates apply to the per-$1,000 rate above $1M: 100% up to $1M, 90% from $1-2M, 80% from $2-3M, 70% from $3-4M, 60% from $4-5M, and 50% above $5M. That makes the effective rate about 0.096% at $5M of revenue. Example: $1M of revenue costs $75 + 998 x $1.20 = $1,272.60.

Ord. 2025-072 moved NAICS 54 from Class 5 ($80 + $1.30) to Class 4 starting May 2026. NAICS 51 stays in Class 4. Columbia has no software-specific subclass. Renewals are due April 30.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license base tax (first $2,000 of gross income)
fixedAnnual.notes: Class 4 minimum, owed even with zero revenue if the business operates in the city.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Columbia has no city income or payroll tax. Richland County's business license applies only to UNINCORPORATED areas (seen in search results, not in county source documents). Columbia's 2% hospitality tax and tourism development fee apply to prepared food and lodging, not SaaS. Business personal property tax is separate and not modeled.

calculatorOption.label: Columbia
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Columbia business license: $75 + 0.12% of ALL gross receipts when your office is in the city (Class 4), with the rate stepping down above $1M.

jurisdictions.name: Greenville, SC
jurisdictions.taxYear: License year May 1, 2026 - April 30, 2027, measured on calendar-2025 gross income. Rates are from the city's Business License Application 'Rev 1 2026'. The codified Appendix A (Supp. 16, 2023) shows the older $55 + $1.75 Class 4 rates, and I did not read the 2025/2026 adopting ordinance.

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license tax (Class 4: Information and Professional, scientific & technical services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts. If the company is domiciled in the city, the base is ALL gross receipts everywhere, less receipts reported on a paid license to another SC municipality (a paid copy must be attached). Without a domicile, only receipts from within the city count, at doubled non-resident rates ($114 + $3.54 per $1,000).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: none
receiptsTaxes.notes:
Class 4 resident costs $57 on the first $2,000, plus $1.77 per $1,000 above $2,000 (0.177%). Declining steps apply to the per-$1,000 rate: 100% up to $10M, 75% from $10-25M, 50% from $25-100M, 25% from $100-200M, and capped above $200M. Example: $1M of revenue costs $57 + 998 x $1.77 = $1,823.46.

Residents get a 2% discount for filing by Mar 31, but the fee can't go below the base. The MASC 2025 class schedule moves NAICS 54 from Class 5 to Class 4 starting May 2026; NAICS 51 stays in Class 4. City staff discussed revenue-neutral rate adjustments to offset the reclassification. The +$2 base / +$0.02 per $1,000 versus the codified schedule fits that, but I did not see the adopting ordinance.

fixedAnnual.name: Business license base tax (first $2,000 of gross income)
fixedAnnual.notes: Class 4 resident minimum, owed even with zero revenue if the business operates in the city.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Greenville has no city income or payroll tax. Greenville's economic development stimulus program (Code Sec. 8-31 to 8-35) refunds 100% of business license tax for 5 years for a NEW 'corporate headquarters' (25+ permanent employees with HQ functions in the city). It also refunds 1-3 years of license tax for adding 10/25/50 jobs at or above the county median wage plus $500k-$1M of capital investment. Most early startups won't qualify. Whether Greenville County has its own business license was not verified this session. Business personal property tax is separate and not modeled.

calculatorOption.label: Greenville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Greenville business license: $57 + 0.177% of ALL gross receipts when your office is in the city (Class 4, 2026-27 rates).

jurisdictions.name: South Dakota
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-2026 (annual report fee per SDCL 47-1A-122 as amended by SL 2025 ch 189; sales tax rates per DOR July 2026 Sales and Use Tax Guide; RA rates for calendar 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Annual report, foreign business corporation (Secretary of State)
fixedAnnual.notes: $55 filed online, $70 on paper ($55 plus a $15 paper-filing fee). SDCL 47-1A-122(25) sets the fee at $55; the statute's source note lists SL 2025 ch 189, and an online fee of $50 appears in older secondary sources, so the increase to $55 is probably a 2025 change. Late fee is $55 on top of the filing fee (47-1A-122(26)). The one-time Application for Certificate of Authority (foreign qualification) costs $750 online or $765 on paper. It is not annual, so it is excluded here.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: None. The SD DOR business tax page says: "South Dakota does not impose a corporate income tax." The only franchise tax is the bank franchise tax, which applies only to financial institutions (banks, savings and loans, production credit associations). It does not apply to a software or services C corp.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No gross receipts, margin, franchise, or capital-stock tax applies to an ordinary corporation, so before profit the only state cost is the $55 annual report. SALES TAX (pass-through, collected from customers): the state rate is 4.2%. HB 1137 (2023) cut it from 4.5%, and its sunset repeals the cut effective June 30, 2027, so the rate goes back to 4.5% on July 1, 2027. Municipal sales/use tax of 1-2% is added on top (2% in Sioux Falls and Rapid City). Products transferred electronically are taxed as tangible personal property, including temporary-use access, which covers SaaS and downloaded or custom software. Services are taxable unless specifically exempt. The exempt list covers health, education, social, agricultural, financial-institution, insurance-commission, broker, trucking, travel-agent and construction services, so consulting, IT, and other professional services are generally taxable. Tax is sourced to where the customer receives the product or service. Remote sellers must register once gross sales into SD exceed $100,000. PAYROLL (already in expenses): there is no state personal income tax and no withholding. Reemployment Assistance (unemployment) tax for 2026 is charged on the first $15,000 of each employee's wages. New non-construction employers pay 1.20% RA tax plus a 0.55% investment fee in year 1, and 1.00% plus 0.55% in years 2-3 if their account balance is positive.

calculatorOption.label: South Dakota
calculatorOption.assumptionText: South Dakota has no corporate income, franchise, or gross receipts tax; a registered foreign corporation pays only the $55 online annual report fee.

jurisdictions.name: Sioux Falls, SD
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Sioux Falls has no city gross receipts, business privilege, occupation, or income tax on a software or professional-services company, and no general business license. The city licensing page says "Not all businesses and professions need City licensing" (see Code of Ordinances §110.026). Its listed licenses are for specific trades only (alcohol, contractors, haulers, daycare, peddlers, pawnbrokers, transportation services, etc.), none of which covers a software or consulting office. The city's taxes are pass-through and run through the state DOR return. It levies a 2% municipal sales/use tax, which applies to anything subject to state sales tax, including SaaS and taxable services delivered there. Its 1% municipal gross receipts tax (MGRT) and 1% lodging tax apply only to alcohol, eating establishments, lodging, and admissions, not to software or services. Population share is about 0.06% of the US (approximate, from recall of Census estimates); it does not matter here because nothing is owed.

calculatorOption.label: Sioux Falls
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Sioux Falls has no city receipts tax, business tax, or general business license; its 2% municipal sales tax is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Rapid City, SD
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Checked as SD's second-largest city. The SD DOR municipal tax page lists only Rapid City's 2% municipal sales/use tax and the 1% MGRT on alcohol, eating establishments, lodging and admissions. Both are pass-through, and the MGRT does not reach software or services. Search results from rcgov.org show only trade-specific city licenses (pawnbrokers and secondhand dealers, contractors, residential roofing). I could not read the city's own business guide (rcgov.org returned HTTP 403), so the absence of a general business license there is not confirmed from the city itself. No other SD municipality is known to impose a receipts or business tax on software or services companies. State law limits municipal taxes to the 1-2% sales/use tax and the category-specific 1% MGRT (per the DOR guide).

calculatorOption.label: Rapid City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Rapid City has no city receipts or business tax on software or services; its 2% municipal sales tax is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Tennessee
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years ending on or after Dec 31, 2025 (Dept. of Revenue Business Tax and F&E manuals dated June 2026). Business tax rates and the $100k threshold have been unchanged since the 2023 Tennessee Works Tax Act. The 2025 and 2026 legislative summaries contain no business tax or franchise/excise changes that matter here.

receiptsTaxes.name: Tennessee business tax (state-level), Classification 3 retail (services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts from taxable services delivered to Tennessee customers. Services delivered to locations outside TN are deducted (BUS 428 Schedule B line 1), and the customer's access location controls for cloud/remote services. A company with a TN location sources all its TN-delivered sales to that location's county. A remote seller with no TN location reports them on a single state location ID.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: In-state location: gross sales sourced to the location's county of $100,000 or more. The Department says to test this on Schedule A line 1, total gross sales before deducting out-of-state service sales, so in practice it is the location's total taxable-type revenue. Out-of-state seller with no TN location: only counties where its TN receipts are $100,000 or more are taxed. It also needs substantial nexus, e.g. TN receipts above the lesser of $500k or 25% of total receipts, TN payroll above $50k, or TN property above $50k.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rates (TCA 67-4-709): Class 3 retail is 3/16 of 1% (0.001875) and Class 3 wholesale (sales for resale) is 3/80 of 1% (0.000375). B2B sales to end users count as retail. Once registered, the minimum tax is $22 per location ($44 if the location is also in a city that levies the tax). Business personal property tax paid can be credited against up to 50% of the tax. SOFTWARE: in SAP America v. Gerregano (Tenn. Ct. App., May 13, 2026), the court held that software license receipts, explicitly including remotely accessed software ('SaaS'), are intangible property and not subject to business tax. The Department's June 2026 manual adopted this. Before that, the 2025 manual taxed software as a Class 3 service. Still taxable: software support, training, configuration, consulting, cloud hosting/IaaS/PaaS and other 'cloud-based services', and general professional services. So for a pure-SaaS company the effective rate on subscription revenue is likely 0, and 0.001875 is an upper bound that applies to the services mix. The Tennessee Supreme Court could still take the case on discretionary review; I found no information on whether a petition was filed. Exempt service categories (accounting, legal, engineering, architecture, medical, etc.) owe nothing. Remote seller registering only with the state: no local license is needed, and receipts in counties under $100k are exempt. Return is due on the 15th day of the 4th month after year-end.

fixedAnnual.name: Franchise tax minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $100 minimum is owed every year by any corporation registered with the Secretary of State, active or not. Full tax is 0.25% of net worth (assets minus liabilities, book basis), apportioned by a single sales factor for tax years ending on or after Dec 31, 2025. Per the June 2026 F&E manual, if the everywhere sales denominator is zero, the apportionment ratio is zero, so a pre-revenue multistate company pays the $100 minimum. The property-measure alternative base was repealed for tax years ending on or after Jan 1, 2024 (Pub. Ch. 950, Notice 24-05). Example of the full tax: $10M net worth with 2% TN sales gives $500 a year. Trap: a company that is not taxable in any other state cannot apportion, so it would pay 0.25% of its entire net worth, e.g. $25k on $10M of VC equity.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $20 for a corporation, plus $20 if the registered agent or office changes. One-time $600 Certificate of Authority fee to register a foreign for-profit corporation (not annual).

profitTaxes.name: Excise tax
profitTaxes.notes: 6.5% of Tennessee-apportioned net earnings (single sales factor). Zero before profit; NOL carryforwards apply.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Sales/use tax (pass-through): Tennessee taxes remotely accessed prewritten software (SaaS) under TCA 67-6-231 when the customer accesses it from a TN address (Dept. letter rulings), at 7% state plus up to 2.75% local. That rate and the $100k remote-seller threshold are from recall; I did not re-read them this session. Collect it from customers. It is separate from, and not affected by, the SAP business-tax ruling. Payroll: there is no state or local tax on wages and no local head or payroll tax; the only payroll tax is state unemployment insurance, which belongs in expenses. Business tangible personal property (computers, furniture) at a TN office is assessed at 30% of value and taxed at local property rates, a small annual cost if you have an office. Business licenses: an in-state location pays a $15 registration fee to the county clerk, plus $15 to the city if the city levies the tax. Standard licenses renew free when the return is filed. A minimal activity license ($15) is required for $3,000 to $100,000 in gross sales. A remote employee's home office is not a business location for municipal tax, but more than $50k of TN compensation creates state business-tax nexus.

calculatorOption.label: Tennessee
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.1875% business tax on Tennessee-delivered service receipts once the TN location's gross sales reach $100k (SaaS license fees exempt since SAP v. Gerregano, 2026, so pure-SaaS revenue may owe nothing), plus the $100 minimum franchise tax and $20 annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Nashville, TN
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years ending on or after Dec 31, 2025 (rates per TCA 67-4-709 as of the June 2026 manual)

receiptsTaxes.name: Nashville (Metro urban services district) municipal-level business tax, Classification 3 retail
receiptsTaxes.base: Same base as the state-level tax for a location inside the Nashville urban services district (BUS 428 line 7 equals line 1). An in-state company's TN-delivered sales made anywhere in the state are sourced to its physical location. So if the only TN office is in Nashville, the city tax applies to all of its TN-delivered taxable service receipts, not just Nashville customers.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross sales sourced to the Nashville location of $100,000 or more (Schedule A total gross sales, i.e. the location's total taxable-type revenue before deducting out-of-state service sales)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Owed in addition to the state-level tax, so the combined rate is 0.375% for Class 3 retail. Applies only with a physical location in the urban services district. Out-of-state businesses with no TN location are exempt from municipal-level tax, and a remote employee's home office does not count as a location. The Department's manual says the Nashville city business tax is due in USD areas such as Antioch. TCA 67-4-705 sets municipal rates at the 67-4-709 rates, and Metro Code 5.16.080 levies business tax 'at the same rate' as the state statute. I did not locate the separate USD ordinance text, hence medium confidence. Minimum $22 once registered. The SAP v. Gerregano software-license exclusion applies equally.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: $15 city business license fee plus $15 Davidson County fee when first registering. Standard licenses renew at no charge when the return is filed; a minimal activity license costs $15 when gross sales are $3k to $100k. No local income, payroll or head tax. Metro levies property tax on business personal property at a TN office (USD rate was $3.254 per $100 of assessed value in FY25 per Metro's revenue overview; I did not verify the current-year rate).

calculatorOption.label: Nashville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Another 0.1875% city business tax on all Tennessee-delivered service receipts if your Tennessee office is in Nashville and its gross sales reach $100k; nothing for remote sellers without a Nashville location.

jurisdictions.name: Memphis, TN
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years ending on or after Dec 31, 2025 (rates per TCA 67-4-709 as of the June 2026 manual)

receiptsTaxes.name: Memphis municipal-level business tax, Classification 3 retail
receiptsTaxes.base: Same base as the state-level tax for a location inside Memphis city limits. All of an in-state company's TN-delivered taxable service receipts are sourced to its physical location; services delivered outside TN are deducted.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross sales sourced to the Memphis location of $100,000 or more (Schedule A total gross sales)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Memphis Code 5-12-3 levies the Business Tax Act privilege taxes 'at the rates and in the manner prescribed by such act'. Combined with the state-level tax, the rate is 0.375%. Shelby County no longer levies a separate county tax: since 2014 the former county tax is the state-level tax. Applies only with a physical location in the city; out-of-state businesses are exempt. Minimum $22 once registered. Software license receipts are excluded (SAP v. Gerregano, 2026).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Combined City of Memphis ($15) and Shelby County ($15) business license fee per memphistn.gov, renewed through the Shelby County Clerk. Standard licenses renew free when the business tax return is filed. No local income, payroll or head tax.

calculatorOption.label: Memphis
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Another 0.1875% city business tax on all Tennessee-delivered service receipts if your Tennessee office is in Memphis and its gross sales reach $100k; nothing for remote sellers without a Memphis location.

jurisdictions.name: Knoxville, TN
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years ending on or after Dec 31, 2025 (rates per TCA 67-4-709 as of the June 2026 manual)

receiptsTaxes.name: Knoxville municipal-level business tax, Classification 3 retail
receiptsTaxes.base: Same base as the state-level tax for a location inside Knoxville city limits. All of an in-state company's TN-delivered taxable service receipts are sourced to its physical location.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross sales sourced to the Knoxville location of $100,000 or more (Schedule A total gross sales)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Knoxville Code 16-26 adopts TCA 67-4-701 to 67-4-730 by reference and levies privilege taxes 'in the same amount, at the same rate, and in the same manner' as the statutes, as amended. Combined with the state-level tax, the rate is 0.375%. Applies only with a physical location in the city; out-of-state businesses are exempt. Minimum $22 once registered. Software license receipts are excluded (SAP v. Gerregano, 2026).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: $15 city license fee plus $15 Knox County fee at registration, according to search snippets of the city's Business License/Tax Office page; the page itself returned 403. Standard licenses renew free when the return is filed. No local income, payroll or head tax.

calculatorOption.label: Knoxville
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Another 0.1875% city business tax on all Tennessee-delivered service receipts if your Tennessee office is in Knoxville and its gross sales reach $100k; nothing for remote sellers without a Knoxville location.

jurisdictions.name: Chattanooga, TN
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years ending on or after Dec 31, 2025 (rates per TCA 67-4-709 as of the June 2026 manual)

receiptsTaxes.name: Chattanooga municipal-level business tax, Classification 3 retail
receiptsTaxes.base: Same base as the state-level tax for a location inside Chattanooga city limits. All of an in-state company's TN-delivered taxable service receipts are sourced to its physical location.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross sales sourced to the Chattanooga location of $100,000 or more (Schedule A total gross sales)
receiptsTaxes.notes: The Department's June 2026 manual uses Chattanooga as a city that levies the municipal tax (Chattanooga Location IDs, separate Chattanooga and Hamilton County returns). Under TCA 67-4-705, municipal rates are the 67-4-709 rates. I did not find the Chattanooga ordinance text in its Municode code, hence medium confidence. Tennessee has no special city receipts tax on software or services: all 215 cities that levy the business tax use these same rates, so any other city (Franklin, Murfreesboro, Clarksville, etc.) can be modeled the same way.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: $15 city plus $15 Hamilton County license fees at registration (statewide rule). No local income, payroll or head tax.

calculatorOption.label: Chattanooga
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Another 0.1875% city business tax on all Tennessee-delivered service receipts if your Tennessee office is in Chattanooga and its gross sales reach $100k; nothing for remote sellers without a Chattanooga location.

jurisdictions.name: Texas
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 and 2027 franchise tax reports (the 2026 report is generally based on the accounting year ending in 2025). Other figures are for 2026.

receiptsTaxes.name: Franchise (margin) tax, EZ computation
receiptsTaxes.base: Total revenue apportioned to Texas by a single gross-receipts factor (Texas receipts divided by receipts everywhere). Sourcing under 34 TAC 3.591: internet hosting/SaaS goes to the customer's location ((e)(13)); electronically delivered software licenses are treated as intangibles and go to the payor's location ((e)(3)(E) and (e)(21)(B)); services go to where the company's own personnel or property do the work ((e)(26), as amended in 2023 after Sirius XM), and multi-state services are split by the fair value of the work done in Texas.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Annualized total revenue of the whole business everywhere, not Texas revenue. This is the No Tax Due Threshold for the 2026-2027 reports.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Tiers for 2026-27 reports. (1) Total revenue at or below $2.65M: no tax, and no franchise tax report is required (since 2024 reports). Only the free Public Information Report or Ownership Information Report is filed. (2) $2.65M to $20M: the company may elect the EZ computation, 0.331% of apportioned total revenue with no deductions. Or it can file the long form at 0.75% of apportioned margin, where margin is the lowest of: 70% of revenue, revenue minus COGS, revenue minus compensation (wages capped at $480,000 per person, plus benefits), or revenue minus $1M. (3) Over $20M: long form only, at 0.75% of margin (0.375% applies only to retail/wholesale). Pre-profit nuance: the compensation deduction beats EZ once compensation is more than about 55.9% of revenue. If payroll is at or above revenue, margin and tax are both $0. So 0.331% is a ceiling for a payroll-heavy startup, not the typical bill. De minimis rule: under Tax Code 171.002(d)(1), nothing is owed if the computed tax is under $1,000. At the EZ rate that means Texas receipts under about $302k, or total revenue under about $3.26M at a 9.3% Texas share. Once over that line the full amount is due, which is a cliff the linear calculator model cannot represent. Report due May 15. Late filing penalty is $50 per report, plus 5% or 10% of the unpaid tax. Economic nexus for out-of-state entities with no Texas presence starts at $500k of Texas gross receipts (Comptroller page summary in search results, not read in full). Starting with 2026 reports, Texas uses the current-year IRC instead of the 2007 IRC, and electronic filing of EZ/Long Form reports was delayed while 89th Legislature changes were programmed.

fixedAnnual.name: Public Information Report / Ownership Information Report
fixedAnnual.notes: Filed every year with the Comptroller by May 15. There is no filing fee. For a foreign corporation, this replaces a Secretary of State annual report. The SOS collects no recurring annual fee.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign corporation registration with the Texas SOS (Form 301)
fixedAnnual.notes: One-time $750 when registering, not annual. If the company did business in Texas for more than 90 days without registering, a late fee equal to the registration fee applies for each year or part year.

fixedAnnual.name: Business personal property tax (county/city/school district)
fixedAnnual.notes: HB 9 (2025, approved by voters as Proposition 9 in Nov 2025) exempts the first $125,000 of income-producing personal property per location in each taxing unit, starting tax year 2026. A typical startup's laptops and furniture will be under that, so it owes $0. To skip future renditions, file a one-time certification by April 15.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Texas has no corporate or personal income tax. Its business tax is the franchise (margin) tax, listed above as receipts-like because the EZ and 70%-of-revenue options do not depend on profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Sales tax is a pass-through, not counted. SaaS and remote software access are generally taxable in Texas as 'data processing services'. 20% of the charge is exempt, so the tax applies to 80% of the price: 6.25% state plus up to 2% local, an effective rate of up to 6.6% of the price. Information services are also taxed on 80% of the charge. Professional and consulting services are generally not taxable, but if taxable services are more than 5% of a bundled, unitemized fee, the whole charge can be taxed. For 2026, remote sellers may use the 1.75% single local use tax rate. Payroll costs belong in expenses. Texas has no state income tax withholding. State unemployment tax for new employers is reported at 2.7% on the first $9,000 of wages per employee, about $243 per employee per year (from TWC search results; the TWC page would not load for direct reading). Local taxes: I found no Texas city with a local income tax, gross receipts tax, or general business license tax that applies to software or services companies.
