Houston, Dallas, Austin and San Antonio were each checked and all come back as zero. The state's own guidance is that 'a general business license is not required in Texas.'

calculatorOption.label: Texas
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.331% of Texas-sourced revenue once total revenue tops $2.65M/yr (EZ computation, 2026-27 reports); this is a ceiling, since a company whose payroll exceeds revenue owes $0 via the compensation deduction and computed tax under $1,000 isn't owed.

jurisdictions.name: Houston, TX
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city income tax, gross receipts tax, or general business license. The Houston Permitting Center's Nov 2025 'Permit 101' guide lists only activity- and premises-based permits: a Certificate of Occupancy for a physical space (one-time), plus alarm, sign and dumpster permits. If the office has a monitored burglar alarm, the non-residential alarm permit costs $128.66 plus a $32.16 admin fee when new and $122.07 per year to renew. This is premises-dependent (often the landlord's or coworking operator's) and is not counted here. Business personal property is taxed by Harris County taxing units only above the $125,000 HB 9 exemption. Local sales tax is pass-through, on top of the state's 6.25%.

calculatorOption.label: Houston
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Houston has no city income, gross receipts or general business license tax.

jurisdictions.name: Dallas, TX
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city income tax or gross receipts tax. Dallas does not require a general business license, only licenses for specific activities such as home-based, street or sidewalk businesses. That comes from a search-result summary of dallasor.gov FAQ 386; the page itself was behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read, so confidence is medium. Dallas Central Appraisal District confirms the $125,000 business personal property exemption from Jan 1, 2026. Local sales tax is pass-through.

calculatorOption.label: Dallas
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Dallas has no city income, gross receipts or general business license tax.

jurisdictions.name: Austin, TX
jurisdictions.otherNotes: The City of Austin's start-a-business page says 'the State of Texas does not require a general business license' and points to Travis Central Appraisal District for property tax on income-producing tangible property. That property is exempt up to $125,000 per location from 2026. There is no city income or gross receipts tax. A DBA filed with the Travis County Clerk is good for 10 years. Local sales tax is pass-through.

calculatorOption.label: Austin
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Austin has no city income, gross receipts or general business license tax.

jurisdictions.name: San Antonio, TX
jurisdictions.otherNotes: The City of San Antonio Finance Department's permits and licenses page lists only two licenses it collects for: coin-operated amusement machine decals and peddler's licenses. There is no general business license and no city income or gross receipts tax. Business personal property is exempt up to $125,000 per location from 2026. Local sales tax is pass-through.

calculatorOption.label: San Antonio
calculatorOption.assumptionText: San Antonio has no city income, gross receipts or general business license tax.

jurisdictions.name: Utah
jurisdictions.taxYear: Corporate franchise tax: tax years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2026 (4.45%; 4.50% for 2025). Division of Corporations FY2026 fee schedule (effective July 1, 2025).

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate franchise tax minimum (privilege tax)
fixedAnnual.notes: Utah Tax Commission: 'Every corporation that files form TC-20 must pay a minimum tax (privilege tax) of $100, regardless of whether or not the corporation exercises its right to do business.' Applies to foreign corporations qualified in Utah or doing business there, whether qualified or not. A loss-making corporation pays exactly $100. SB 60 (2026) left the $100 minimum unchanged.

fixedAnnual.name: Annual renewal / annual report (domestic/foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: Division of Corporations FY2026 fee schedule (effective July 1, 2025): $18, which includes a $5 single-sign-on surcharge. Late renewal adds $10. Due in the anniversary month of the Utah registration. Registering as a foreign corporation is a one-time $59 fee and is not counted here.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate franchise/income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 4.45% of Utah taxable income for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026 (SB 60, signed Mar 23, 2026, with retrospective operation); 4.50% for 2025. The tax is the greater of the rate times income or the $100 minimum, so it is $0 above the minimum before profitability. I could not reach the statute (le.utah.gov) from this environment, so the 4.45% figure comes from secondary reporting (Orbitax) and search snippets of the SB 60 bill text. The Tax Commission page I read gives the $100 minimum but no rate. Salt Lake City's economic-development page still says 5%, which is outdated.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Utah has no state gross receipts or margin tax. SaaS sales tax (pass-through, not counted): Utah taxes remotely accessed prewritten software (SaaS) when it is used in Utah. Remotely accessed custom software is not taxable (Tax Commission Publication 64). Remote sellers must register above $100,000 of Utah sales; the 200-transaction test was repealed effective July 1, 2025 (SB 47, per secondary sources). The combined rate in Salt Lake City is about 8.45%. Payroll (already counted in expenses): Utah income-tax withholding and state unemployment insurance. Business personal property tax: owners of tangible business property (computers, furniture) located in Utah file with the county assessor. A business whose property has a total taxable value of $30,100 or less can apply for an exemption (Salt Lake County assessor), so a small remote-first startup usually owes nothing. Above that, the tax is an asset-based cost that does not depend on revenue. Under Utah Code 10-1-203, cities may only charge business license fees that recover regulation or disproportionate-service costs. Revenue-measured city license taxes are limited to parking, public assembly, energy and telecom, so no Utah city levies a general gross receipts tax on software or services companies.

calculatorOption.label: Utah
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $100 Utah minimum corporate franchise tax plus $18 annual renewal; Utah has no gross receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Salt Lake City, UT
jurisdictions.taxYear: SLC Consolidated Fee Schedule as amended 06/16/2026 (Ord. 2026-29); the 'Effective Sept 2026' column is used

fixedAnnual.name: Business license base fee (commercial)
fixedAnnual.notes: $193 before Sept 2026 and $198 from Sept 2026 (city code 5.04.070). Applies only to businesses with a location in Salt Lake City. A home-occupation license is $157. The fee schedule lists category add-ons for some business types (e.g. Consulting $34, Miscellaneous Services $33, Design Services $34). It is unclear whether the city would assign one of these to a software company, so none is included.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Salt Lake City has no gross receipts tax and no city income tax. State law (Utah Code 10-1-203) limits city business license fees to cost recovery. Employee fee: the fee schedule charges '$28 ($29 from Sept 2026), annual, per full or part-time employee, if business has more than one employee.' This is effectively a small head tax that scales with headcount (e.g. about $290/yr for 10 employees), so treat it as an expense rather than a fixed amount. It is excluded from fixedPerYear. I read it as applying to every employee once there is more than one; the exact counting rule is in city code 5.04.070, which I could not open (403). Sales tax (pass-through): about 8.45% combined in Salt Lake City on taxable sales, which includes SaaS used in Utah. The city's economic-development tax page is outdated (it gives the state rate as 5%). Business personal property tax applies through Salt Lake County, with an exemption at $30,100 or less of taxable value.

calculatorOption.label: Salt Lake City
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $198/yr Salt Lake City business license base fee if you have an office there (plus $29 per employee once you have more than one); no city receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Lehi, UT
jurisdictions.taxYear: Lehi City FY2026 approved fee schedule

fixedAnnual.name: General business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Lehi FY2026 approved fee schedule lists 'General' and 'Base Fee' at $150 (FY2025: $140). A home-occupied business with no impact pays no fee. I assumed the annual renewal equals this fee; the schedule does not separate initial and renewal amounts.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Checked because Lehi is Utah's main tech hub ('Silicon Slopes'). It has no receipts or income tax, only a flat license fee like most Utah cities (state law limits cities to cost-recovery license fees). Listed so the absence of a receipts tax is explicit. It is not a major city and probably not worth a calculator option.

calculatorOption.label: Lehi
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $150/yr Lehi general business license if you have an office there; no city receipts tax.

jurisdictions.name: Vermont
jurisdictions.taxYear: Tax years 2025 and 2026. The minimum-tax schedule has applied since TY2023 (Act 148 of 2022), and the Legislature's Joint Fiscal Office still showed it unchanged in its Jan 8, 2026 and May 5, 2026 presentations. The foreign annual report fee has been $250 since the 2023 amendment, Act 77.

fixedAnnual.name: Corporate income tax minimum (minimum entity tax)
fixedAnnual.notes: The tax is the greater of graduated income tax or a minimum based on Vermont gross receipts, and it is owed even when the corporation has a loss (CO-411 instructions, Line 13). Minimum tiers by Vermont gross receipts: $500,000 or less = $100; $500,001 to $1,000,000 = $500; $1,000,001 to $5,000,000 = $2,000; $5,000,001 to $300,000,000 = $6,000; over $300,000,000 = $100,000. 'Vermont gross receipts' (CO-411 Line 17) means total receipts from Vermont sources with no deduction for costs. Services are sourced to the market (where the service is delivered) since TY2020. That last point comes from secondary and legislative summaries; I did not read the regulation itself. At Vermont's share of US population (about 0.19%), a nationally selling company only passes $500k of Vermont receipts at roughly $260M of total revenue, so a startup pays $100. A company whose sales are concentrated in Vermont would step up to $500, $2,000 or $6,000. This is a step function, not a rate. The minimum still applies when PL 86-272 protection is claimed. Only out-of-state corporations with no Vermont nexus in the year are exempt ('No Vermont Activity'), and having employees or customers in Vermont counts as nexus.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign corporation annual report (Secretary of State)
fixedAnnual.notes: 11A V.S.A. § 1.22(a) sets the fee at $250 for a foreign corporation and $60 for a domestic one (amended 2023, Act 77, effective June 20, 2023). The SOS fee schedule shows the same amounts. The one-time Application for Certificate of Authority costs $155 and is not annual. Secondary sources say the report is due within 2.5 months after fiscal year end and carries a $25 late fee; I did not verify that against an official source.

profitTaxes.name: Vermont corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Graduated on Vermont net income: 6.0% on the first $10,000, 7.0% from $10,001 to $25,000, and 8.5% above $25,000 (32 V.S.A. § 5832). Apportionment uses a single sales factor from TY2023 and Finnigan combined reporting for unitary groups. The tax is the greater of this or the minimum tax, so before profit only the minimum applies. A 2026 miscellaneous tax bill (H.933) dealt with federal conformity (R&E expensing, QSBS decoupling, a larger state R&D credit). It did not change the rates or the minimum-tax schedule.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: SaaS sales tax (pass-through): from July 1, 2024 (Act 183 of 2024, H.887), Vermont taxes prewritten software accessed remotely at the 6% sales tax rate. There is no business-use exemption, and custom software is exempt only when the customization charge is separately stated. Municipalities with the 1% local option sales tax (Burlington, South Burlington, Winooski, Rutland City, Montpelier from July 2025, and others) add 1% on taxable sales, for 7% combined. These taxes are collected from customers and should not be counted. Payroll (already in expenses): the Child Care Contribution has been 0.44% of Vermont wages since July 1, 2024, with no wage cap. The employer may withhold up to 0.11% from employees, so it pays at least 0.33%. Vermont unemployment insurance and income tax withholding also apply. There is no general state business license and no franchise tax, gross receipts tax or capital-stock tax for ordinary C corporations. The digital business entity franchise tax in 32 V.S.A. § 5832a only applies if a company elects into it. No Vermont municipality was found to levy a local income, gross receipts or business-license tax on software or professional-services firms. Local taxes are limited to the 1% local option sales, meals, rooms and alcohol taxes, plus Burlington's and Rutland's own meals and beverage taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Vermont
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Vermont has no receipts tax: $100 minimum corporate tax (Vermont receipts ≤ $500k; it steps to $500/$2,000/$6,000 above $500k/$1M/$5M) plus a $250 foreign-corporation annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Burlington, VT
jurisdictions.taxYear: FY2027, rates effective July 1, 2026
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Burlington's 'Gross Receipts Tax' (the Restaurant, Hotel and Amusements Tax, set by city ordinance and paid to the Clerk/Treasurer) covers only these categories, at rates effective July 1, 2026: alcoholic beverages 2.5%, amusements 2.5%, meals 2.5%, hotel/motel 4%, short-term rentals 9%. The admissions rate has been dropped. Software, SaaS and professional services are not covered. Burlington has levied the 1% local option sales tax since July 2006, which applies to the now-taxable SaaS sold to Burlington customers (7% combined). This is collected from customers and passed through. I found no general city business license for an office-based software firm; licenses exist only for specific activities such as peddlers, entertainment, liquor, tobacco and food. That conclusion rests on the city site and secondary sources, not on reading the full code. Burlington has no city payroll or head tax. I did not research municipal property tax on business personal property.

calculatorOption.label: Burlington
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Burlington has no tax on software or services receipts; its gross receipts tax covers only meals, alcohol, amusements and lodging.

jurisdictions.name: Virginia
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (SCC annual registration fee per the 2026-2028 Appropriation Act, FY2027-FY2028; corporate income tax rate current for 2025/2026)

fixedAnnual.name: SCC annual registration fee (foreign stock corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: Based on the number of authorized shares: $100 for 5,000 or fewer, plus $30 per additional 5,000 shares, capped at $1,700 once authorized shares exceed 270,000. A VC-backed Delaware C-corp usually authorizes 10M+ shares, so it pays the $1,700 cap. The Code (§ 13.1-775.1) still reads $50 + $15, max $850, but the Appropriation Act overrides it ('Notwithstanding § 13.1-775.1') at $100/$30/$1,700 for FY2027-2028. The SCC's 02/26 fee schedule matches $1,700. The annual report itself has no fee. Both are due by the last day of the month the corporation registered in Virginia, with a penalty of 10% or $10. Cutting authorized shares below 270,000 lowers the fee (e.g. 100,000 shares = $670).

profitTaxes.name: Virginia corporation income tax
profitTaxes.notes: 6% of Virginia taxable income (Form 500). Foreign corporations registered with the SCC must file every year even with no Virginia income. There is no minimum tax and no state franchise or capital tax. It is zero before profit.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: There is no state gross receipts tax. The tax that costs a pre-profit company money is the LOCAL BPOL license tax (see the locality entries). It is imposed by nearly every county, city and town, under state caps in Va. Code § 58.1-3706: 0.36% of gross receipts for repair/personal/business services (which is where SaaS, data processing and computer services fall), 0.58% for financial/real estate/professional services, 0.20% retail and 0.16% contracting. Localities with higher rates before 1978 are grandfathered. BPOL receipts are attributed to the locality where you have a definite place of business (an office, and possibly an employee's home office) and where the services are performed or directed. They are not attributed to where customers are. If receipts can't be traced to one office, they are apportioned by payroll (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(3)). If you have no definite place of business in Virginia, you generally owe no BPOL. Receipts attributable to business conducted in another state where you are liable for an income-based tax are deductible (§ 58.1-3732(B)(2)). The Tax Commissioner requires that you actually file an income tax return there (Ruling 24-89), and receipts taxes such as the OH CAT, TX margin tax and WA B&O don't qualify (Ruling 22-117). Localities may exempt receipts from creating software for sale, lease or license (§ 58.1-3703(B)), but a SaaS/cloud company was held to sell services, not software, and was denied that exclusion (Ruling 22-117). Localities also levy a business tangible personal property tax on computers and furniture, typically $4-$5 per $100 of depreciated or percentage-of-cost value. That is an asset tax, not a receipts tax, but it is a real pre-profit cost (e.g. Virginia Beach: 40% of original cost x $4/$100 = 1.6% of cost per year). Sales tax: SaaS/cloud software is not subject to Virginia sales and use tax (Ruling 16-135). HB 900 (2026), which would extend the tax to digital products and software services from 1/1/2027, was continued to 2027 in committee (secondary sources), and the final 2026 budget (Special Session I) did not include a digital sales tax. Re-check in 2027. Registering a foreign corporation carries one-time fees that are not annual and not counted here. Payroll: Virginia state unemployment insurance (expense). There are no local payroll or head taxes in Virginia.

calculatorOption.label: Virginia
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No state receipts tax; $1,700/yr SCC annual registration fee (cap tier for more than 270,000 authorized shares, typical of VC-backed startups); 6% income tax only after profit.

jurisdictions.name: Arlington County, VA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (BPOL on calendar-2025 gross receipts; rates confirmed in the County's CY2026 comparison table)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business, Professional and Occupational License (BPOL) tax
receiptsTaxes.base: All gross receipts attributable to your Arlington definite place of business in the prior calendar year (attributed to the office where services are performed or directed, not to customer location). New businesses estimate.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: gross receipts attributable to the Arlington location
receiptsTaxes.notes: $0-$10,000: no tax. $10,001-$50,000: $30. $50,001-$100,000: $50. Over $100,000: the rate applies to all receipts (a cliff, not marginal). The Arlington Code lists 'Data software programming service', business consultants, automation consultants and marketing analysts as specialized occupations at $0.36/$100. 'Computer time sharing' and 'Tabulating or computer service bureau' are business services at $0.35/$100. I use 0.36% to be conservative. Qualified technology businesses (Chapter 66 Technology Zone) pay $0.18/$100 with 1-499 employees, for up to 10 years. Receipts attributable to states where you file an income tax return are deductible. Due March 1. Register within 75 days of starting.

fixedAnnual.name: BPOL flat fee below $100k
fixedAnnual.notes: $0 if receipts are $10k or less, $30 for $10,001-$50k, $50 for $50,001-$100k. Replaced by the percentage tax above $100k.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Business tangible personal property tax is $5.00 per $100 of assessed value (computers, furniture). There is no local income or payroll tax.

calculatorOption.label: Arlington County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.36% BPOL on all receipts attributed to an Arlington office once they exceed $100k (flat $30-$50 below); receipts follow the office, not the customers.

jurisdictions.name: Fairfax County, VA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (BPOL on calendar-2025 gross receipts; rates confirmed in Arlington's CY2026 regional comparison table)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business, Professional and Occupational License (BPOL) tax
receiptsTaxes.base: All gross receipts attributable to your Fairfax County definite place of business in the prior calendar year (office-based situs, payroll apportionment if multiple offices).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: gross receipts attributable to the Fairfax County location
receiptsTaxes.notes: $0-$10,000: no fee. $10,001-$50,000: $30. $50,001-$100,000: $50. Over $100,000: rate on all receipts. Business Service Occupations are $0.19/$100; the ordinance names 'online computer services, computer time share services', data processing, computer services and systems development. Consultants and Specialized Occupations and Professional are $0.31/$100, so professional or consulting revenue should use 0.31%. Federally funded R&D can get $0.03 with approval. The County excludes 100% of receipts from the design, development or creation of software for lease, sale or license performed in the County. SaaS/hosted services generally don't qualify (Ruling 22-117 denied it to a cloud company in another county). The towns of Herndon, Vienna and Clifton impose their own license tax instead of the County's. Due March 1.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Business personal property tax is listed at $2.00-$4.57 per $100 depending on property class. There is no local income or payroll tax.

calculatorOption.label: Fairfax County
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.19% BPOL (business services; 0.31% for consulting) on all receipts attributed to a Fairfax County office once over $100k; flat $30-$50 below.

jurisdictions.name: Richmond, VA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (threshold raised to $500,000 effective January 1, 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business, Professional and Occupational License (BPOL) tax
receiptsTaxes.base: All gross receipts attributable to your Richmond definite place of business in the prior calendar year.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: gross receipts attributable to the Richmond location
receiptsTaxes.notes: $5,000 or less: $0. $5,000-$500,000: $30 flat. Over $500,000: gross receipts x rate. City Council raised the threshold from $250,000 to $500,000 on July 29, 2025, effective January 1, 2026; the 2025 application still showed $250,000. Richmond's schedule has no separate 'business services' line, so business services are taxed with personal services at $0.36/$100. Professional services are $0.58/$100, using the narrow statutory definition (architects, attorneys, CPAs, engineers, etc. plus occupations the Department of Taxation lists). SaaS and most IT consulting should fall in the $0.36 class. Under City Code § 26-874, qualifying new businesses with over $250,000 of receipts in their first two years can get a grant reducing the license to $30. Due March 1.

fixedAnnual.notes: $30 for gross receipts from $5,000 to $500,000.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Business tangible personal property tax applies (rate not researched). There is no local income or payroll tax.

calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.36% BPOL (business/personal services; 0.58% if professional) on all receipts attributed to a Richmond office once over $500k; $30 flat below.

jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (Commissioner of the Revenue's current rate table)

receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: gross receipts attributable to the Virginia Beach location

jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 license year (FY2026 approved rates; confirmed in Arlington's CY2026 comparison table)

receiptsTaxes.base: All gross receipts attributable to your Alexandria definite place of business in the prior calendar year.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: gross receipts attributable to the Alexandria location

jurisdictions.name: Washington
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (B&O rates in force since Oct 1, 2025; small-business credit amounts unchanged through Dec 31, 2028)

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Retailing classification (SaaS / remote access software, digital automated services; since Oct 1, 2025 also IT services, custom software, customization of prewritten software, custom website development)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts from retail sales sourced to Washington. Sourcing follows sales-tax rules: where the customer receives or first uses the service (customer address as fallback).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Washington-sourced receipts. This is an approximation built from the small-business B&O credit, not a statutory exemption. The $100k economic-nexus test is separate and only matters when there is no physical presence in WA.
receiptsTaxes.notes: DOR rate table: Retailing 0.471% (.00471). DOR says RAS (SaaS) is 'classified as a retail sale for B&O tax purposes' and that IT services and custom software became retail sales on Oct 1, 2025 (ESSB 5814). Hosting, storage and backup stay under Service & Other. Small-business credit (DOR credits page): when under 50% of B&O liability is Service & Other, the credit is up to $55/month and phases out completely at $110/month of tax. At 0.471% that zeroes the tax up to about $140k/yr of WA receipts and is gone by about $280k/yr; between those points the calculator's cliff overstates the tax. The credit is computed per filing period (monthly, quarterly or annual). Out-of-state sellers with no physical presence have B&O nexus only above $100,000/yr of WA-sourced receipts (seen in a DOR search excerpt, not read in full). ESSB 6346 (c 238 L 2026): from Jan 1, 2029 the credit rises to $125/$375 per month, the annual filing threshold rises to $250k, and the ESSB 5814 retail-services sales tax (everything except advertising) is repealed. Whether IT services and custom software then go back to Service & Other B&O is unverified. SaaS/RAS keeps its retail treatment.

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Service & Other Activities (professional services not reclassified as retail, e.g. general/management consulting, hosting/storage)
receiptsTaxes.base: Apportionable income times the WA receipts factor: single-factor receipts sourced by where the customer receives the benefit (RCW 82.04.462).
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Washington-apportioned service income. Approximation from the small-business credit, which applies when 50% or more of B&O liability is Service & Other.
receiptsTaxes.notes: RCW 82.04.290 and the DOR special notice, effective Oct 1, 2025, set tiers by prior-calendar-year Service & Other taxable income, with affiliates over 80% common control combined: under $1M = 1.5%, $1M to $4,999,999.99 = 1.75%, $5M+ = 2.1%. A pre-profit startup is almost always in the 1.5% tier. The service-business credit is up to $160/month and phases out at $320/month of tax (Jan 1, 2023 to Dec 31, 2028). At 1.5% that is about $128k/yr of WA service income tax-free, phasing out by about $256k. A Washington-heavy consulting company could pay 1.5% on WA-apportioned income, more than three times the retail rate.

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report (profit/foreign corporation)
fixedAnnual.notes: $70 per WAC 434-112-085; $95 if delinquent. One-time costs are not annual: $180 foreign registration and the $50 DOR Business Licensing Service application fee. If city endorsements are renewed through DOR's Business Licensing Service, there is also a $5 annual renewal processing fee, plus the city fees, which are listed under each city.

profitTaxes.name: None: Washington has no corporate income tax
profitTaxes.notes: ESSB 6346 (2026) adds a 9.9% tax on individual income over $1M starting Jan 1, 2028. It applies to individuals only, not C corporations. The existing WA capital gains tax also falls on individuals.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Sales/use tax is collected from customers and passes through, so it is not counted. WA retail sales tax applies to SaaS/RAS and digital automated services, and since Oct 1, 2025 also to IT services, custom software, customization and custom website development (ESSB 5814). ESSB 6346 repeals the 5814 services (except advertising) from Jan 1, 2029. The state rate is 6.5% plus local rates. Payroll costs belong in expenses: state unemployment insurance, Paid Family & Medical Leave premiums, WA Cares (employee-paid), and L&I workers' comp. Surcharges that don't touch a startup: the 0.5% surcharge on WA taxable income over $250M (2026-2027; ESSB 6346 ends it early) and the advanced-computing surcharge. Local B&O: about 40+ WA cities levy their own B&O under the AWC model ordinance. Under that ordinance, retail receipts (SaaS/IT; confirmed for Seattle by Seattle Rule 5-503) go to the customer's location. Service & Other income is apportioned 50% by payroll and 50% by customer location, so a startup headquartered in a B&O city has half or more of its non-retail service income taxed there. Kent (gross receipts tax only on Kent receipts above $250k, plus a square-footage tax only for 12,000+ sq ft of office space) and Oak Harbor (new B&O since Oct 1, 2025) were not verified from the city pages and are not listed. The AWC rate table was blocked to automated download.

calculatorOption.label: Washington
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.471% retailing B&O on SaaS/IT receipts from Washington customers (1.5% on other professional services), with the small-business credit covering roughly the first $140k/yr of WA receipts; $70 annual report.

jurisdictions.name: Seattle, WA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Proposition 2 'Seattle Shield' rates for 2026-2029; council may extend to 2032)

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license tax (B&O), Retail Sales & Retail Services: SaaS/digital automated services and remote access software, plus, from Jan 1, 2026, custom software, customization, IT services, custom website development
receiptsTaxes.base: Seattle-sourced retail receipts (where the customer receives or first uses the service)
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Seattle taxable revenue across all classifications, after deductions other than the standard deduction
receiptsTaxes.notes: 2026 rate 0.342%, up from 0.222% in 2025. If Seattle taxable revenue is $2M or less, no tax is due. Above that, a $2M/yr standard deduction applies first to the highest-rate classification, with no carryforward, so in effect the tax falls only on Seattle revenue over $2M. The calculator's cliff overstates by up to $2M x rate. Digital automated services are 'retail sales and retail services' under Seattle Rule 5-503. Contracts signed before Oct 1, 2025 could stay under the service classification until Apr 1, 2026.

receiptsTaxes.name: Business license tax (B&O), Service & Other Business Activities (professional services not reclassified as retail)
receiptsTaxes.base: Service income apportioned to Seattle by the two-factor formula (payroll factor + service-income factor) / 2
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Seattle taxable revenue (same $2M threshold and standard deduction as above)
receiptsTaxes.notes: 2026 rate 0.658%, up from 0.427% in 2025. A Seattle-headquartered firm with all its payroll in Seattle has at least 50% of service income apportioned to Seattle, so pure consulting revenue can cross $2M at about $4M of total service revenue.

fixedAnnual.name: General business license tax certificate
fixedAnnual.notes: 2026 tiers on annual Seattle taxable revenue: $0-$19,999 = $73; $20,000-$499,999 = $147; $500,000-$1,999,999 = $667; $2M-$4,999,999 = $1,604; $5M+ = $3,210; $10 per branch. New licensees pay Tier 1. Businesses outside the city with no place of business there and $4,000 or less of Seattle income are exempt.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Payroll taxes belong in expenses. The JumpStart payroll expense tax applies only if 2025 Seattle payroll was at least $9,074,409 and an employee earns at least $194,452 in 2026; rates 0.746%-2.557% (from a seattle.gov search excerpt, not read in full). The Social Housing Tax is 5% of compensation paid in Seattle above $1M per employee, effective 2025. Customers in Seattle pay state plus local sales tax on SaaS, which passes through. Seattle licenses through FileLocal, not DOR's Business Licensing Service. With Seattle at about 0.23% of US population, a nationally-selling SaaS company would need hundreds of millions of revenue to cross $2M Seattle receipts. In practice the license fee, plus apportioned service income if the company is Seattle-based, is what bites.

calculatorOption.label: Seattle
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.342% of receipts from Seattle customers once Seattle receipts top $2M/yr (the law also deducts the first $2M, so this overstates slightly); $73 business license.

jurisdictions.name: Bellevue, WA

receiptsTaxes.name: Gross receipts B&O tax (single rate for all classifications)
receiptsTaxes.base: Bellevue taxable gross receipts: retail receipts sourced to Bellevue; service income apportioned by the two-factor (payroll + service income) method
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Annual Bellevue taxable gross receipts
receiptsTaxes.notes: 0.1596% for every gross receipts classification, per the Jan 1, 2026 Bellevue B&O Tax Guide. Taxable gross receipts of $215,000/yr or less are exempt, and quarterly filers reconcile to the annual threshold. Retail or wholesale sales delivered outside Bellevue are deductible.

fixedAnnual.name: Square footage B&O tax (illustrative 1,000 sq ft office)
fixedAnnual.notes: $0.3297475 per taxable sq ft per quarter, about $1.32/sq ft/yr, CPI-adjusted each January. It applies to office space supporting activity not taxed under Bellevue gross receipts, such as HQ/admin space and space supporting out-of-city sales. A nationally-selling startup's Bellevue office is almost entirely taxable. Offices of 250 sq ft or less are exempt. $1,319 assumes 1,000 sq ft; scale to the real office, and use $0 for a fully remote team.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: One-time $119 general business license registration fee (not annual); filed via FileLocal-WA, which charges user/service fees. Registration is required with a physical location in Bellevue, or with more than $4,000 of Bellevue receipts plus physical nexus. A return must be filed even when no tax is due. Customers pay sales tax on SaaS, which passes through.

calculatorOption.label: Bellevue
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.1596% of receipts sourced to Bellevue once they exceed $215k/yr; plus about $1.32/sq ft/yr square-footage tax, shown here for a 1,000 sq ft office ($0 if remote).

jurisdictions.name: Tacoma, WA

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Retailing (SaaS; from Jan 1, 2026 also IT services, custom software, custom website development)
receiptsTaxes.base: Retail receipts sourced to Tacoma (customer location)
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Company-wide (all-location) gross income. Companies located outside Tacoma also owe nothing unless their Tacoma income exceeds $20,000.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Rates per tacoma.gov: Retailing 0.153%, Wholesaling 0.102%, Manufacturing 0.11%, Service & Other / Service & Other Apportioned / Retail Service 0.4%. Small-business credit for company-wide gross income of $250,001-$300,000 phases in the tax: 90% credit at $250,001-$260,000, falling to 25% at $290,001-$300,000. Treating pre-2026 SaaS as retail is inferred from the model ordinance and was not stated on Tacoma's page.

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Service & Other Apportioned (non-retail professional services)
receiptsTaxes.base: Service income times (payroll factor + service-income factor) / 2
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Company-wide gross income
receiptsTaxes.notes: For a Tacoma-headquartered consultancy, at least 50% of service income is apportioned to Tacoma at 0.4%.

fixedAnnual.name: City business license (2024-2026 fee schedule)
fixedAnnual.notes: Tiered on company-wide gross income 'regardless of location': under $12,000 = $37; $12,000-$250,000 = $190; $250,001-$1M = $435; $1,000,001-$5M = $1,500; over $5M = $2,000. $435 assumes $250k-$1M of revenue. From Jan 1, 2026, out-of-city businesses with $4,000 or less of Tacoma income need no license (from a search excerpt).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: The $250k and $20k thresholds come from a Tacoma Tax & License workshop PDF (undated, but it says the $250k threshold took effect in 2011), and tacoma.gov's current page refers to this 'threshold framework'. Customers pay sales tax on SaaS, which passes through.

calculatorOption.label: Tacoma
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.153% of receipts sourced to Tacoma once company-wide revenue tops $250k/yr; $435 business license, which assumes $250k-$1M revenue and ranges from $190 to $2,000.

jurisdictions.name: Spokane, WA

fixedAnnual.name: City general business license (DOR endorsement)
fixedAnnual.notes: $131 per 12 months, or $65.50 for gross annual income of $0-$18,000. Employee fees are extra: 1-5 employees $10 each, 6-10 $15 each, 11+ $20 each, counting employees working in Spokane. Out-of-city businesses owe no fee at $4,000 or less of Spokane income. DOR adds a $5 renewal processing fee.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Spokane has no city B&O/gross receipts tax: DOR's endorsement page mentions none, and one secondary site claiming otherwise appears wrong. Per-employee license fees are head-based and belong in expenses. Customers pay sales tax on SaaS, which passes through.

calculatorOption.label: Spokane
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city receipts tax; $131 business license plus $10-$20 per Spokane employee.

jurisdictions.name: Vancouver, WA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (new B&O effective Jan 1, 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax on Retail Sales and Retail Services only
receiptsTaxes.base: Retail receipts from activity within Vancouver city limits (customer location for SaaS)
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Annual Vancouver retail receipts (or $12,500 in any quarter)
receiptsTaxes.notes: 0.100% rate. Professional/service income is not taxed. The city page describes retail as goods and services like construction and gyms and doesn't address SaaS. Treating SaaS/IT services as retail is inferred from the AWC model-ordinance update, so this is uncertain. Returns are required even below the threshold.

fixedAnnual.name: City business license (DOR endorsement)
fixedAnnual.notes: By gross annual income: $0-$4,000 = $0; $4,001-$53,000 = $53; $53,001+ = $347 plus $165 per calculated employee (total hours / 1,664, minimum 1). Remote employees working in the city count. Out-of-city businesses with $2,000 or less of city receipts are exempt.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: The $165/FTE license component is a head tax and belongs in expenses; a 10-person startup would pay about $1,650/yr on top of the $347.

calculatorOption.label: Vancouver
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.1% of retail receipts (likely including SaaS) sourced to Vancouver above $50k/yr; $347 business license plus $165 per FTE.

jurisdictions.name: Everett, WA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (changes proposed for 2027)

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax (all classifications)
receiptsTaxes.base: Everett taxable gross receipts (retail sourced to the customer; service income apportioned two-factor)
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Everett taxable gross receipts ($5,000/quarter for quarterly filers)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Currently 0.1% for retail, manufacturing, wholesale and services. Some service activities report as retailing from Jan 1, 2026. Pending proposal, with a council vote scheduled Oct 14, 2026 and effect from Jan 1, 2027 if adopted: threshold raised to $250,000; services and wholesale 0.15%; manufacturing 0.12%; retail 0.075%.

fixedAnnual.name: City business license renewal
fixedAnnual.notes: $111 for the primary location in 2026; $15 for in-city businesses under $45k/yr (from an everettwa.gov search excerpt). The proposal would drop fees for businesses under $45k.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: everettwa.gov pages returned 403 to automated fetches, so the figures come from search excerpts of everettwa.gov and the Everett Herald. Recheck after the Oct 14, 2026 vote.

calculatorOption.label: Everett
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.1% of receipts sourced to Everett above $20k/yr; $111 business license (a 2027 proposal would raise the threshold to $250k).

jurisdictions.name: Bellingham, WA

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Retailing (SaaS/IT likely retail under the model ordinance)
receiptsTaxes.base: Bellingham-sourced retail receipts
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Bellingham-sourced revenue ($5,000/quarter for quarterly filers)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Retailing, manufacturing, wholesaling and extracting are 0.17%. Services and other activities are 0.44%, apportioned two-factor, so a Bellingham-based consultancy pays 0.44% on at least half its service income. The city page doesn't address the 2026 SaaS/IT retail reclassification.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: City license (DOR endorsement) is a one-time $40 with no renewal; out-of-city businesses with $4,000 or less of Bellingham income need none.

calculatorOption.label: Bellingham
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.17% of receipts sourced to Bellingham above $20k/yr (0.44% for non-retail services); the city license is a one-time $40.

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Retailing / Retail Services
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross income from business activities in Olympia
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross income of business activities in Olympia
receiptsTaxes.notes: Updated Nov 18, 2025 for 2026: retail and retail services 0.15% (up from 0.1%); service & other 0.2%. The no-tax-due threshold rose from $20,000 to $500,000 starting with the 2026 tax period.

fixedAnnual.name: City endorsement fee
fixedAnnual.notes: $30, waived for 501(c)(3)s or under $4,000 of Olympia revenue.

calculatorOption.label: Olympia
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.15% of receipts sourced to Olympia once they exceed $500k/yr; $30 city endorsement.

jurisdictions.name: Renton, WA
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (rates in effect since 2023)

receiptsTaxes.name: B&O tax, Retailing (SaaS; from Jan 1, 2026 also IT services, custom software, advertising, temporary staffing)
receiptsTaxes.base: Renton taxable revenue (retail sourced to the customer)
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Annual taxable revenue (the page doesn't say whether this is Renton-only; presumably Renton taxable revenue)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Retailing 0.070%; Service & Other, Retail Service, Wholesaling and Manufacturing 0.121%. Annual tax is capped per business ($12M in 2025, inflation-adjusted).

fixedAnnual.name: Annual business license registration
fixedAnnual.notes: $150/yr. A per-worker-hour fee of about $0.0352/hour (roughly $73/FTE), exempt under 1,200 worker-hours/yr, comes from a secondary source and is not on the city page. Out-of-city businesses with $4,000 or less of Renton revenue are exempt from 2026.

calculatorOption.label: Renton
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.07% of receipts sourced to Renton once they exceed $500k/yr; $150 business license.

jurisdictions.name: Redmond, WA

fixedAnnual.name: City business license (per-FTE)
fixedAnnual.notes: $160 per FTE (1,920 hours/yr worked in Redmond), minimum $160. Out-of-city businesses with $4,000 or less of Redmond income pay $0.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city B&O/gross receipts tax. Fees beyond the $160 minimum are effectively a head tax ($160/FTE) and belong in expenses.

calculatorOption.label: Redmond
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No city receipts tax; business license is $160 per FTE working in Redmond ($160 minimum).

jurisdictions.name: West Virginia
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (WV Tax Division TSD-100 Rev. July 2026; SOS annual report form Rev. 07/2026; W. Va. Code 59-1-2a as in force after July 1, 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Secretary of State annual report fee (W. Va. Code 59-1-2a)
fixedAnnual.notes: $25 for every corporation, domestic or foreign, authorized to do business in WV. Statute says the fee also covers the SOS acting as attorney-in-fact; the official form shows no separate foreign-corporation fee. Filed Jan 1 to June 30 of each year after the year of registration. Late: $75 total ($50 late fee). From July 1, 2026, entities with 5+ years of on-time filings may elect biennial reporting at $50 per two years (same $25/yr).

profitTaxes.name: Corporation Net Income Tax
profitTaxes.notes: 6.5% of WV taxable income; federal taxable income is the starting point; single sales factor apportionment from Jan 1, 2022; combined reporting for unitary groups. Zero before profit. Estimated payments are required only if WV taxable income is expected to exceed $10,000. TSD-100 (Rev. July 2026) still shows 6.5%; 2026 bills proposing cuts were not reflected there.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: WV has no state gross receipts tax that applies to software or services. The state B&O tax applies only to public utilities, electric power generators, and natural gas storage operators. The Business Franchise Tax is not listed among current business taxes in TSD-100 (I recall it was repealed for 2015 and later). The Tax Division's Business Registration Certificate costs a one-time $30 and is permanent until relocation or closure, so it is not an annual cost (TSD-100 says a separate certificate is needed for each business location). Sales tax: 6% state consumers sales and service tax applies broadly to services, with professional services excluded (from memory, not checked against the statute). Secondary sources (TaxJar, Commenda, etc.) say SaaS is taxable in WV. I did not confirm this on an official source. Either way it is collected from customers, so it passes through. Many cities add a 1% municipal sales and use tax: Charleston, Huntington, Morgantown, Parkersburg, Wheeling, Fairmont, South Charleston and others (tax.wv.gov list). Payroll: WV income tax withholding and WorkForce WV unemployment tax are expenses. City 'service fees' are flat weekly charges per employee working in the city, withheld from employee pay: Charleston $3/wk, Huntington $5/wk, Morgantown $3/wk. Local receipts tax: TSD-100 says most WV cities levy a broad municipal business and occupation (B&O) tax on gross receipts with no deductions, at rates that vary by city and activity. Since July 11, 2025, under HB 2451 / W. Va. Code 8-13-5(d)(2), a city may not impose B&O on a business with gross revenue below $2,500 a year. Other city service rates I saw: Fairmont $0.70 per $100 (0.70%) per the city's B&O page.

calculatorOption.label: West Virginia
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No West Virginia state receipts or franchise tax on software/services; $25 annual report fee to the Secretary of State; 6.5% corporate income tax only once profitable.

jurisdictions.name: Charleston, WV
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (City Collector New Business Handbook rev. 05/2024, posted 2026-03; B&O FAQ rev. 12/2022; $2,500 exemption per Bill 8058, passed Oct 6, 2025)

receiptsTaxes.name: Municipal Business & Occupation (B&O) Privilege Tax: Service/All Other Businesses (class 12)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross income with no deductions (no cost of goods, labor, or any expense) from services rendered to others in Charleston, whether or not the business is based in the city. Also included: WV-sourced service income not taxable by another WV city, if the services are directed from a Charleston location or the principal WV office is in Charleston. The city's guidance only addresses receipts within WV; ask the City Collector about out-of-state receipts of a Charleston-based company.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: total annual gross income of the business (state law HB 2451 / W. Va. Code 8-13-5(d)(2), adopted in City Code 110-63 in Oct 2025: businesses with less than $2,500 in annual gross income are exempt)
receiptsTaxes.notes: Flat 1% (multiplier 0.01) with no tiers. Other rates: retail 0.5%, wholesale 0.15%, contracting 2%, manufacturing 0%. Returns are quarterly, due the last day of the month after each quarter. Annual filing can be requested in writing if total liability is under $2,500/yr. Zero returns are required and cannot be filed online. Penalty is 5% for the first month plus 1% per month after; interest is 8%/yr. Lack of profit is irrelevant to liability.

fixedAnnual.name: General Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: $20, renewed by June 30 each year. Required only for businesses with a storefront or physical location in Charleston, home-based businesses, or rental owners. A company with no Charleston location still files the business registration and B&O returns but buys no license.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: City Service Fee (CSF): $3.00 per week for every full- or part-time employee who reports to a physical location in the city or works from home in the city. The employer withholds it from employee pay and remits it quarterly. It is payroll-like, so it belongs in expenses, and it applies even if the business is exempt from B&O. Charleston also has a 1% municipal sales and use tax (since July 1, 2015), collected from customers through the state return, so it passes through. Sourcing caveat: for a remote SaaS company with no Charleston presence, how far 'rendering services therein' reaches customers located in the city is not settled in the guidance I read. The default share below is Charleston's share of US population. A company headquartered in Charleston could owe 1% on all of its WV-sourced service receipts not taxed by another WV city, up to about WV's 0.54% population share.

calculatorOption.label: Charleston, WV
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 1% Charleston B&O tax on gross receipts from services rendered in Charleston (more if headquartered there); exempt under $2,500 total gross income; $20/yr business license if you have a location in the city.

jurisdictions.name: Huntington, WV
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2025-26 (current B&O return form; business license application dated 10/1/2025)

receiptsTaxes.name: Municipal B&O Tax: Service and All Other Business (code 12)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross receipts from business activity in Huntington, before any deductions, excluding sales/excise taxes collected
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: total annual gross revenue (state law HB 2451, W. Va. Code 8-13-5(d)(2)). Huntington's own guidance applies the exemption only to independent contractors or sole proprietors under $2,500 with no physical location in the city.
receiptsTaxes.notes: 0.5% (multiplier 0.005). Retail and restaurants (class 5) have been waived to 0% since Sept 13, 2021. Contracting 2%, rents 1%, banking 1%. Quarterly returns are due 30 days after each quarter end, and zero returns are required. Late penalty is 5% plus 1.5% per month (max 25%); interest is 8%/yr.

fixedAnnual.name: General Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: $20 a year; licenses expire June 30. Applies to businesses doing business within city limits.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: City Service Fee: $5.00 per week per individual working in city limits, including people working from home in the city. The employer withholds and remits it quarterly. It is payroll-like and belongs in expenses. 1% municipal sales and use tax since Jan 1, 2012, which passes through. Default share is Huntington's 2020 Census population over the US total.

calculatorOption.label: Huntington, WV
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.5% Huntington B&O tax on gross receipts from services in Huntington; $20/yr business license.

jurisdictions.name: Morgantown, WV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Current quarterly B&O return form (undated); license fee per current municipal business license application

receiptsTaxes.name: Municipal B&O Tax: Service Business or Calling (item G)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross taxable income from business activity in Morgantown
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: revenue sourced to Morgantown. This is an approximation of the $3.44-per-quarter credit (about $13.76/yr ÷ 0.9%). The state $2,500 total-gross-revenue exemption under W. Va. Code 8-13-5(d)(2) also applies, and Morgantown limits it to sole proprietors and independent contractors with no city location.
receiptsTaxes.notes: $0.90 per $100 (0.9%), less a $3.44 credit on each quarterly return for the service class. Annual and by-the-job return forms also exist. Other classes: retail 0.45%, contracting 2%, wholesale 0.15%, manufacturing 0.30%. The form is undated, so confirm the rate with the Finance Department (BandO@morgantownwv.gov).

fixedAnnual.name: Municipal Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: $20 per fiscal year; expires June 30, renew by July 1.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Safe Streets & Safe Community (municipal service) fee: $3.00 per calendar week per employee who reports to work or works from home in the city. It is payroll-like and belongs in expenses. 1% municipal sales and use tax since July 1, 2020, which passes through. Default share is Morgantown's 2020 Census population over the US total. At that share, sourced revenue would not pass the credit-equivalent threshold until total revenue reaches about $17M.

calculatorOption.label: Morgantown, WV
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.9% Morgantown B&O tax on service receipts from Morgantown, less a small $3.44/quarter credit; $20/yr business license.

jurisdictions.name: Wheeling, WV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Rates 'updated as of April 1, 2015' per city page (still posted in 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Municipal B&O Tax: Service Business
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross income from business activity in Wheeling
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: total annual gross revenue (state law, W. Va. Code 8-13-5(d)(2), effective July 11, 2025)
receiptsTaxes.notes: $0.88 per $100 (0.88%). Banking 0.94%, retail 0.365%, wholesale 0.15%, manufacturing 0.28%, contracting 2%, rents 0.73%. Quarterly returns plus an annual return; zero returns are required. No city credit or exemption is listed on the city pages.

fixedAnnual.name: General Business License
fixedAnnual.notes: $15 a year; licenses expire June 30.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Wheeling also has a City Service Fee, but I did not verify the amount. It is payroll-like and belongs in expenses. 1% municipal sales tax since July 1, 2015, which passes through. A March 2026 Intelligencer editorial called for modernizing Wheeling's tax structure, so the rates could change. Default share is Wheeling's 2020 Census population over the US total.

calculatorOption.label: Wheeling, WV
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.88% Wheeling B&O tax on service receipts from Wheeling; $15/yr business license.

jurisdictions.name: Parkersburg, WV
jurisdictions.taxYear: Q3 2024 standard B&O return form (form rev. 8-23)

receiptsTaxes.name: Municipal B&O Tax: Service & All Other Business (code 13)
receiptsTaxes.base: Gross sales/receipts from business activity in Parkersburg, before deductions, excluding sales/excise taxes
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: revenue sourced to Parkersburg. This is an approximation of the $200-per-quarter exemption against gross tax ($800/yr ÷ 0.9%). Above it, the real tax is 0.9% × receipts − $800, so the calculator overstates by up to $800/yr.
receiptsTaxes.notes: 0.9% (multiplier 0.009). Every taxpayer gets an exemption of up to $200 of gross tax per quarter, and it cannot go below zero. Other classes: retail 0.28%, wholesale 0.15%, contracting 2%, rents 0.8%, banking 1%. Quarterly returns are due the last day of the month after each quarter, and zero returns are required.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: I could not check the business license fee or the city service/user fee because the city's fees page returned HTTP 403. Most WV cities charge a small annual license ($15-$20 elsewhere), but I left it at $0 rather than guess. 1% municipal sales tax since July 1, 2015, which passes through. Default share is Parkersburg's 2020 Census population over the US total. With the $200/quarter exemption, a nationally selling startup without an office in Parkersburg would effectively owe $0.

calculatorOption.label: Parkersburg, WV
calculatorOption.assumptionText: 0.9% Parkersburg B&O tax on service receipts from Parkersburg after a $200/quarter tax exemption (about the first $89k/yr of Parkersburg receipts).

jurisdictions.name: Wisconsin
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (DFI fees from the current fee page and Form Corp18, revised May 2026; DOR corporate rate and surcharge rules in effect for tax years 2025 and 2026)

receiptsTaxes.name: Economic development surcharge (minimum)
receiptsTaxes.base: Not a receipts-rate tax. The greater of $25 or 3% of Wisconsin gross tax liability, capped at $9,800. Gross receipts set only the threshold, not the amount.
receiptsTaxes.thresholdBasis: Gross receipts from all activities everywhere: federal Form 1120 line 1c plus gross dividends, interest, rents, royalties and gross sale proceeds of assets. This is total receipts, not Wisconsin-sourced. In a combined group, each member is tested separately.
receiptsTaxes.notes: Listed here because the threshold is measured on gross receipts. A loss corporation at or above $4M total gross receipts still owes the $25 minimum: DOR Pub 400 (02/26), Example 4 shows a $10,000 Wisconsin net loss with $4.5M receipts owing $25. Below $4M it owes nothing. A foreign corporation without Wisconsin nexus is exempt. Reported on Form 4 line 21. Wisconsin has no tax that scales with gross receipts.

fixedAnnual.name: Foreign business corporation annual report (DFI)
fixedAnnual.notes: $65 if filed online, $80 on paper (DFI fee page; Form Corp18 lists the $80 paper fee). The statutory base in Wis. Stat. 180.0122 is $65. A capital-representation fee is added when capital employed in Wisconsin grows: $3 per $1,000 of the increase over the amount already paid on. Because it is paid on increases only, it is not a recurring annual amount (see otherNotes).

fixedAnnual.name: Economic development surcharge minimum
fixedAnnual.notes: $25/yr, but only once total gross receipts everywhere reach $4M. Small startups below that owe $0, so it is excluded from fixedPerYear.

profitTaxes.name: Corporate franchise/income tax
profitTaxes.notes: Flat 7.9%. DOR's general information page lists no minimum tax. Every corporation licensed to do business in Wisconsin must file Form 4 (or Form 6 for combined groups) even with no activity. Single sales factor apportionment. Service receipts are sourced to where the purchaser receives the benefit (market-based). This sourcing rule is from recall of Wis. Stat. 71.25(9); I did not re-read it this session. Above $4M total receipts, the economic development surcharge adds 3% of gross tax liability (max $9,800).

jurisdictions.otherNotes: One-time and capital-based fees: the certificate of authority costs $100, plus $3 per $1,000 of capital employed in Wisconsin above $60,000, unless the company is a WEDC 'qualified new business venture' (Wis. Stat. 180.0122, 180.1503). On Form Corp18, capital means par value plus additional paid-in capital on par-value stock, so it effectively includes venture money raised. That capital is multiplied by (WI gross business + WI property) / (total gross business + total property). Because the fee is charged only on increases over capital already paid on, it works like a ratchet: about 0.3% of the growth in capital represented in Wisconsin. Example: a fully remote seller with $10M raised, $2M revenue and $8M of other assets, with 1.75% of revenue in Wisconsin, has about 0.35% representation, or roughly $35k of capital, under $60k, so the fee is $0. A company with a Wisconsin office or a large Wisconsin customer base could owe a few hundred to a few thousand dollars, mostly at funding events. Not modeled. I could not confirm whether the $60k exemption carries into the annual-report calculation; check the 'Paid Capital Represented' field on the DFI record. Personal property tax was repealed from the January 1, 2024 assessment (2023 Act 12). There are no local income, payroll or gross receipts taxes in Wisconsin. Sales tax: state 5% plus county 0.5% in most counties (Milwaukee County 0.9%) plus 2% in the City of Milwaukee. Per DOR, remotely accessed SaaS on servers the vendor controls is a nontaxable data processing service. Downloaded or transferred prewritten software is taxable. Sales tax is pass-through either way. State unemployment insurance is a payroll cost already in expenses.

calculatorOption.label: Wisconsin
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Wisconsin receipts tax; $65/yr foreign-corporation annual report, plus $25/yr surcharge only once total receipts reach $4M (not modeled).

jurisdictions.name: Milwaukee, WI
jurisdictions.otherNotes: No city gross receipts, income or payroll tax, and no general business license. Licenses are activity-specific, such as food, alcohol, tobacco and home improvement. This comes from the City Clerk License Division as quoted in search results; the city's pages returned Cloudflare 403 to direct fetches. The only new local tax under 2023 Wis. Act 12 is a 2% city sales and use tax from January 1, 2024. Milwaukee County's sales tax rose from 0.5% to 0.9% the same day, for a combined 7.9% on taxable sales. That is pass-through to customers, and remotely accessed SaaS is generally not taxable in Wisconsin. Business personal property tax ended statewide in 2024.

calculatorOption.label: Milwaukee
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Milwaukee has no receipts tax or general business license; its 2% city sales tax is collected from customers.

jurisdictions.name: Madison, WI
jurisdictions.otherNotes: The City of Madison says it 'does not have a generic business license'. Clerk licenses are for inspected or regulated activities such as restaurants, hotels and pools. No city gross receipts, income or payroll tax. Dane County sales tax is 0.5% on top of the state's 5%, collected from customers. Business personal property tax ended statewide in 2024.

calculatorOption.label: Madison
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Madison has no receipts tax or general business license.

jurisdictions.name: Wyoming
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Secretary of State fee schedule effective July 1, 2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Annual Report License Tax (W.S. 17-16-1630)
fixedAnnual.notes: Greater of $60 or two-tenths of one mill ($0.0002) on the dollar of capital, property and assets located and employed in Wyoming. A foreign corporation counts only its Wyoming-located assets, using balance-sheet values, with assessed values for land and buildings. Cash and receivables count if they are located in Wyoming. Anything at or below $300,000 of Wyoming assets pays the $60 minimum, which covers a small startup with a Wyoming office or remote employees. Due on or before the first day of the anniversary month of registration. Online filing adds a payment-processor convenience fee that scales with the tax; the SOS does not publish the amount. A commercial registered agent is also required, but that is a private service fee, not a tax.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Wyoming has no corporate income tax, no franchise tax on income or capital, and no gross receipts or margin tax. The only recurring state cost for a pre-profit foreign C-corp is the $60 minimum annual report license tax. One-time cost: a Certificate of Authority (foreign corporation registration) is $150. Operating without authority carries a $5,000 penalty plus back fees, license taxes and 18% interest. Sales/use tax is 4% state plus up to about 2% local. It is collected from customers, so it is pass-through and not counted here. Wyoming's sales tax rule (Rules ch. 2 §12) makes prewritten software taxable however it is delivered, including electronically, and says creating custom software is not taxable. That rule does not address remotely accessed software or SaaS. Secondary sources (Numeral, Commenda, TaxCloud) say pure SaaS with no transfer of software is not taxable in Wyoming. I did not find an official DOR statement saying so. Payroll: there is no state income tax withholding. Employers pay state unemployment insurance (rate and wage base not researched here). Workers' compensation goes through the state-run fund, and whether office employees must be covered depends on occupation class. These belong in expenses. Business personal property (equipment) located in Wyoming is subject to county ad valorem property tax. That depends on assets, not receipts.

calculatorOption.label: Wyoming
calculatorOption.assumptionText: No Wyoming income or receipts tax; $60 minimum annual report license tax (≤ $300k of Wyoming assets).

jurisdictions.name: Cheyenne, WY
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (current City Clerk license fee schedule)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Cheyenne has no city income tax, no gross receipts tax and no general business license. The City Clerk licenses only listed activities, such as auctions, barber shops, restaurants, pawnbrokers, taxicabs, tattoo establishments, temporary merchants and vending machines. None of them covers an office-based software or professional-services business. Contractor licenses go through the Building/Compliance division and apply only to building trades. Sales tax in Laramie County (state 4% plus local option) is collected from customers, so it is pass-through. Wyoming cities cannot levy income taxes.

calculatorOption.label: Cheyenne
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Cheyenne has no receipts tax and no general business license for software or services firms.

jurisdictions.name: Jackson, WY
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (Town of Jackson business license application revised 07.01.2026)

fixedAnnual.name: Town of Jackson annual business license
fixedAnnual.notes: Required for every business that transacts or carries on business within Town limits (Municipal Code Title 5). The fee is flat and set by employee headcount. Non-sales-tax-collecting businesses pay $179 (1–10 employees), $397 (11–49), $535 (50–99) or $891 (100+). Sales-tax-collecting businesses pay $136, $274, $410 or $684. Independent contractors and agents pay $136. The fee is non-refundable, not pro-rated, and renewed annually by January 30. A pure SaaS seller is likely in the non-sales-tax-collecting tier. This applies only if the company has a location or employees in the Town, not just because it has customers there.

jurisdictions.otherNotes: Jackson has no receipts tax and no income tax. The license is a flat fee by headcount, and only companies with a presence in the Town pay it. Teton County lodging taxes and local sales tax are collected from customers, so they are pass-through. I found no other Wyoming city with a general business license that scales with receipts.

calculatorOption.label: Jackson, WY
calculatorOption.assumptionText: $179/yr Town of Jackson business license (1–10 employees, non-sales-tax-collecting); applies only with a location in the Town.

jurisdictions.name: Casper, WY
jurisdictions.taxYear: 2026 (current City of Casper licensing page)
jurisdictions.otherNotes: Casper has no general business license, no receipts tax and no income tax. The city's licensing page lists the only businesses that need a license: junk dealers, pawnshops, itinerant merchants, unsolicited salesmen, secondhand dealers, hotels and rooming houses, and vehicles for hire. Health, liquor and special-event permits are separate. A software or professional-services office needs none of these. I could not read the Municipal Code Chapter 5.04 text itself (the municode page did not render), so this rests on the city's licensing page. Sales tax is collected from customers, so it is pass-through.

calculatorOption.label: Casper
calculatorOption.assumptionText: Casper has no receipts tax and no general business license for software or services firms.
